info.title: bxapi
info.description:
bxapi runs games of the 1981 B/X (Basic/Expert) fantasy adventure game over HTTP.
[osrlib](https://github.com/mmacy/osrlib-python), a Python rules engine, applies every rule, while
bxapi adds API keys, SQLite storage, one-at-a-time access to each game, and RFC 9457 error
responses. Your client application draws the screen and reads the player's input. bxapi rolls the
dice, applies the rules, stores the game, and returns what happened.

## Base URL

Each bxapi server runs at its own address. The `bxapi` command listens on
`http://127.0.0.1:8640` unless the server's `BXAPI_HOST` and `BXAPI_PORT` settings specify another
address, and the examples in this reference use `http://127.0.0.1:8640`. Every path in this
reference is relative to the server's address. Every operation except `GET /health` is under `/v1`.

## Play a game

1. `GET /v1/meta` checks your API key and returns your client name, role, and storage usage.
2. `POST /v1/ability-rolls` rolls six ability scores and lists the classes they qualify for.
3. `POST /v1/characters` creates a character from the roll and the player's choices. Save the
   character's `id`. To show the player the hit points and starting gold first, send the same
   choices to `POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview`, which stores nothing.
4. `GET /v1/adventures` lists the adventures you can play. Every server includes `builtin-barrow`.
5. `POST /v1/sessions` starts a game of an adventure with a party of stored characters. Save the
   session's `id`.
6. `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands` lists the commands that are legal now.
7. `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands` sends one command and returns what happened.
8. `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/view` returns what the players can see, so your client can draw
   the screen. Pass `include=view` in step 7 to get the view in the command's response instead.

Repeat steps 6 to 8 until `ended` is `true` in a command's response. For a runnable end-to-end
walkthrough with shell variables, see [Play a game](https://mmacy.github.io/bxapi/docs/play-a-game/)
and [`examples/play_barrow.py`](https://github.com/mmacy/bxapi/blob/main/examples/play_barrow.py).

## Authentication

Send an API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
Whoever runs the server configures its keys in the `BXAPI_API_KEYS` setting and assigns each key a
client name and a role. Every path under `/v1` requires an API key, whereas `GET /health`, `/docs`,
`/redoc`, and `/openapi.json` require none. A request with no key, or with an unknown key, gets 401
`unauthorized`.

A server started with no keys and `BXAPI_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true` asks for no key. It treats every
caller as a referee for the client `local`, and `GET /v1/meta` returns `auth_enabled` set to
`false`. Such a server answers a request under `/v1` only when the request's `Host` header is
`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`, with or without a port. A request with another host gets 421
`misdirected_request`.

Each key grants one of two roles:

- `player`: everything a game client needs. In a session, a player sees only what the players may
  see.
- `referee`: everything a player may do, plus the referee view, referee events, referee commands,
  chosen seeds, character and save imports, and full adventure and save documents.

A player request for a referee feature gets 403 `referee_required`, or 403 `referee_command` when a
player sends a referee command.

A key identifies a client application, not a person. Every key for one client reads and changes
that client's characters, adventures, sessions, and saves, whereas another client's resources are
hidden. A request for another client's resource gets the same 404 `not_found` as an id that
doesn't exist.

## Conventions

- **Ids.** A stored resource's id is a prefix followed by 22 random URL-safe characters: `rol_` for
  an ability roll, `chr_` for a character, `adv_` for an adventure, `ses_` for a session, and
  `sav_` for a save. Built-in adventure ids start with `builtin-`.
- **Timestamps.** UTC timestamps in RFC 3339 format with whole seconds, such as
  `2026-11-20T22:01:05Z`.
- **Lists.** Every list operation except `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events` accepts `limit` (1
  to 200, default 50) and `offset` (0 to 2^53 - 1, default 0), and returns `items`, `total`,
  `limit`, and `offset`. Add `limit` to `offset` for the next page, and stop when `offset` plus
  `limit` is `total` or greater. The server lists stored resources newest first. The session event
  log (`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events`) uses `after` and `next_after` (`limit` 1 to 500,
  default 100) per `visibility` instead.
- **Documents.** A *document* is osrlib's JSON envelope for an adventure, a character, a party, or
  a save. It is an object with `kind`, `schema_version`, `engine_version`, and `payload`. The
  server accepts documents whose `schema_version` is at most the `schema_version` that
  `GET /v1/meta` returns, and refuses newer ones with 409 `version_unsupported`.
- **Seeds.** osrlib draws every random number from one integer, the *seed* (0 to 2^53 - 1). The
  stateless operations under `/v1/dice` and `/v1/generate` accept an optional `seed` from any
  caller and return the seed they used. Sending the same request with the same seed returns the
  same result on the same osrlib version. For ability rolls, characters, and sessions, only a
  referee may choose a seed, and the server never returns it to a player. Each new session also
  gets a separate secret key for opaque player feature handles. Session and save documents store
  that key, while both views omit it.
- **Unknown fields.** A request body with a field the operation doesn't define gets 422
  `validation_error`, whereas commands and documents are osrlib models and ignore unknown fields.
- **osrlib's descriptions.** The schema descriptions for commands, events, views, and rules models
  come from osrlib. Where an osrlib description mentions a validation check, the server returns 422
  `validation_error` for a malformed command or request body, and 422 `content_invalid` for an
  uploaded or imported document. A name in code there, like `MAX_SCORE` or `load_ability_tables`,
  is a constant or a function in osrlib's Python package, documented in the
  [osrlib reference](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/). For the scores that an ability adjustment can reach,
  call `GET /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/adjustment-limits`.
- **JSON bodies.** Send a request body as UTF-8 JSON with `Content-Type: application/json` (or an
  `application/*+json` media type). A non-empty body without a JSON `Content-Type` gets 415
  `unsupported_media_type`. The server refuses undecodable bytes, integers with more than 4,300
  digits, `NaN`, `Infinity`, numbers too large for a 64-bit float, strings with half of a UTF-16
  surrogate pair, or arrays and objects nested more than 100 levels deep, with 400 `bad_request`.
- **Body size.** A body is at most 65,536 bytes. On the five operations that accept an osrlib
  document, the limit is the server's `BXAPI_MAX_BODY_BYTES` setting instead (8,388,608 bytes by
  default): `POST /v1/adventures`, `POST /v1/adventures/validate`, `POST /v1/characters/import`,
  `POST /v1/saves/import`, and `POST /v1/sessions`. A larger body gets 413 `content_too_large`.
- **Compression.** Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, and the server compresses every response of 1,024
  bytes or more. Most HTTP clients send the header and decompress the response automatically.
- **Conditional requests and caching.** Every 200 response to a `GET` includes a weak `ETag`
  header. Send that `ETag` in `If-None-Match` to check whether your copy is still current: the
  server answers 304 with no body while the content is unchanged, or 200 with the new content when
  it has changed. Successful `GET` responses under `/v1/rules` include
  `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600`, while other `/v1` `GET` responses include
  `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`.
- **HEAD.** Every `GET` operation also answers `HEAD` with the same status and headers and no body.
- **Idempotency keys.** To retry a `POST` under `/v1` without running it twice, send an
  `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 printable ASCII characters with no spaces, such as a UUID) on
  the first request and on every retry. The server stores a 2xx response for 24 hours and returns
  it with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` on a retry. When a request fails with a problem other than
  500 `internal_error`, nothing changed and the server releases the key so a retry runs the
  request again. Keys are scoped to your client.
- **Request ids.** Every response includes an `X-Request-Id` header, such as
  `req_Zk3uY0mWq1x8Jr5cTt2aLw`, which the server logs with the request. Send `X-Request-Id` with 1
  to 128 letters, digits, and `.`, `_`, `~`, or `-` to supply your own id. The server replaces any
  other value with a generated `req_` id.
- **Storage.** The server counts the bytes of the documents it stores for your client: ability
  rolls, characters, adventures, sessions, saves, and stored idempotency responses. `GET /v1/meta`
  returns the current count and the limit (`BXAPI_MAX_CLIENT_BYTES`, 1,073,741,824 bytes by
  default, or `null` when disabled). At or above the limit, any request that would store a
  document gets 507 `storage_full` until you delete something.
- **Rate limits.** Each client has a token-bucket budget of `BXAPI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` requests
  per server process (600 per minute by default). You can spend the full budget in a burst and
  regain tokens steadily. A request over the limit gets 429 `rate_limited` with the seconds to wait
  in `Retry-After`.

## Refused commands

A command that the B/X rules forbid isn't an HTTP error. `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`
returns 200 with `accepted` set to `false` and osrlib's `rejections`, and the session doesn't
change. An HTTP 4xx or 5xx status means the request itself failed.

## Errors

Every error response is an RFC 9457 problem document with the media type
`application/problem+json`. Branch on `code`, which stays stable across releases. `detail` is a
human-readable sentence of at most 1,000 characters. Each operation lists the codes it can return
and how to handle each one.

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "No session has the id 'ses_nope'.",
  "code": "not_found",
  "request_id": "req_Zk3uY0mWq1x8Jr5cTt2aLw",
  "resource": "session",
  "id": "ses_nope"
}
```

Every problem document includes `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `code`, and `request_id`
(matching the response's `X-Request-Id` header). Specific codes add extra members:

| Code | Added members |
| --- | --- |
| `validation_error` | `errors`: the first 20 parts of the request that failed validation, each with `loc`, the path to the value, `msg`, and `type`. `error_count`: how many parts failed, including any that `errors` leaves out. |
| `not_found` | `resource`: the kind of resource the request asked for, such as `session`. `id`: the id in the request, or its first 128 characters followed by `...`. |
| `revision_conflict` and `session_busy` | `revision`: the session's current revision. |
| `referee_command` | `command_type`: the `command_type` of the referee command a player sent. |
| `character_invalid` | `rejections`: osrlib's reasons for refusing the character, each with `code` and `params`. When osrlib reports no rejections, `field` and `id` appear instead: the request field that failed and the value of the entry, plus `index` (from 0) when `field` is a list. |
| `storage_full` | `used_bytes`: the bytes of documents the server stores for your client. `max_bytes`: the most bytes the server stores for one client. |

Later releases may add members, so ignore any member your client doesn't recognize.

Five error codes can succeed when you send the same request again: 409
`idempotency_key_in_progress`, 429 `rate_limited`, and 503 `database_busy` after waiting the
seconds in their `Retry-After` headers, 408 `request_timeout` right away, and 409 `session_busy`
right away unless you passed `expected_revision` (if you did, read the session first). For any
other code, fix the request before retrying. When no response arrives at all, retry a `POST` with
the same `Idempotency-Key`. For a 500 error, report `request_id` to the server's operator.

get.summary: Check that the server is up
get.description:
Return `{"status": "ok"}` while the HTTP server is accepting requests.

Requires no API key, touches no database tables, and has no rate limit, so load balancers
and container health probes can poll it frequently. Does not verify database connectivity or API
keys. To verify an API key and inspect server versions, call `GET /v1/meta`.

200.description: `{"status": "ok"}`.

304.description: The response whose `ETag` you sent in `If-None-Match` is still current. The response has no body.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of a cached response for this request, such as `W/"5f0c1b6de0a94d7f8f3f0f5b7a1c2d3e"`, or `*`. While the content is unchanged, the server answers 304 with no body.

get.summary: Get the server's versions and the caller's role
get.description:
Verify your API key and return the server's versions, your client and role, and your storage usage.

Call this operation at application startup. A 200 response confirms that your bearer token is
valid, and `role` indicates whether your key can call referee-only operations (`"referee"`) or
player operations (`"player"`). Compare `schema_version` against any adventure, character, or
save documents your client stores before uploading or importing them, because documents with a
higher `schema_version` fail with 409 `version_unsupported`.

Inspect `storage.used_bytes` and `storage.max_bytes` to monitor your client's document quota
before hitting 507 `storage_full` or to confirm space reclaimed after deleting resources.

200.description: Server versions, authentication mode, caller client and role, and storage usage.

Cache-Control.description: `private, no-cache`. Revalidate with `If-None-Match` before reusing a cached copy.

304.description: The response whose `ETag` you sent in `If-None-Match` is still current. The response has no body.

Cache-Control.description: `private, no-cache`. Revalidate with `If-None-Match` before reusing a cached copy.

401.description: - `unauthorized`: The request has no API key or has an unknown key. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with a key configured on the server. Retrying the same request fails.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer`, the authentication scheme the server accepts.

421.description: - `misdirected_request`: The server runs without API keys, and the request's `Host` header isn't `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`. Call the server by one of those names, or configure API keys on the server. A server with API keys never returns this code.

429.description: - `rate_limited`: Your client exceeded the per-minute request budget (`BXAPI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, 600 by default). Wait the seconds in the `Retry-After` header and retry. Requests without a valid API key share a separate budget and receive 429 instead of 401 `unauthorized` when that budget is exhausted.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, at least `1`.

500.description: - `internal_error`: The server failed because of a bug. The response says nothing about the cause, and the server logs it. Report the request to the server's operator.

503.description: - `database_busy`: Another process held the SQLite write lock for more than 5 seconds. Wait the 1 second in the `Retry-After` header and retry.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying: `1`.

get.description:
Return osrlib's `ClassDefinition`: requirements, armour and weapon rules, abilities, and level progression.

`requirements` maps each constrained ability score to its minimum value, and `progression` contains one row per
level with required XP, hit dice, `thac0`, `saves`, and spell slots. Pass `class_id` to `GET /v1/rules/spells` to
list the spells this class can cast, or to `POST /v1/characters` to create a character of this class.

morale, and special abilities, or to `POST /v1/generate/monsters` to roll hit points.

get.description:
Return osrlib's `MonsterTemplate` stat block: attacks, saves, morale, movement, treasure, and abilities.

Use `display_name` and `display_name_plural` when naming the creature in prose (for example, `"giant centipede"`
for the index name `"Centipede, Giant"`). `family_id` groups variants of the same creature and matches the
`family_id` reported on encounter groups in `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/view`. This endpoint requires a
template `id` rather than a `family_id` (for example, `hellhound_3` through `hellhound_7`, whereas `hellhound`
returns 404 `not_found`).

Pass `monster_id` to `POST /v1/generate/monsters` to spawn instances with rolled hit points, or pass each letter
in `treasure` as `treasure_type` to `POST /v1/generate/treasure`.

order, returning the `character`, `derived` stats, and every individual die in `rolls` (`ability_rolls`,
`hit_point_roll`, and `gold_roll`). The `ruleset` decides how osrlib rolls the scores and the hit points. Both
`player` and `referee` keys may pass `seed` to reproduce a character, or omit it to draw a new seed.

`POST /v1/sessions`. To store a character for play, call `POST /v1/characters` instead. This operation rolls new
scores and takes no `ability_roll_id`. To see the character a stored ability roll would create, call
`POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview`.

post.description:

osrlib's `generate_treasure` rolls each entry in `GET /v1/rules/tables/treasure` in table order. `coins` reports
each denomination (`pp`, `gp`, `ep`, `sp`, `cp`), `valuables` lists rolled gems and jewellery with `value_gp`,

rolled gem or piece of jewellery has no name of its own, so its `phrase` is empty. A monster's treasure letters
appear on `GET /v1/rules/monsters/{monster_id}` under `treasure`.

Any caller may pass `seed` to repeat a roll, or omit it to get a new random seed. In an active session, osrlib
rolls area and lair treasure automatically during play.

post.description:
Roll six ability scores with osrlib, store the roll, and return the scores, their dice, and eligible classes.

Display `scores` and `eligible_class_ids` to the player. A client that animates the dice shows `rolls.rolls`, the
three d6 that count toward each score. Then pass `id` as `ability_roll_id` to `POST /v1/characters` along with
the player's class, alignment, and equipment choices. The request body is optional: with no body, osrlib rolls
3d6 for each score from a seed the server draws. A referee may pass `seed`.

`4d6_drop_lowest`, osrlib rolls four d6 for each score and drops the lowest, and `rolls.dropped` has the dropped
die of each ability. The server stores the method with the roll and returns it as `ability_score_method`. Send
the same `ruleset` when you preview or create the character, because a request whose ruleset has another method
gets 409 `ability_roll_ruleset_mismatch`.

player to discard such a character and roll again. osrlib only reports it, and the server accepts a sub-par roll
like any other.

same seed when `POST /v1/characters` consumes the roll. Retrying `POST /v1/characters` after a 422

before you create the character, call `POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview`.

no limit on how many rolls a client creates. To roll scores and create the character in one step, omit
`ability_roll_id` on `POST /v1/characters`.

get.summary: Get the limits on an ability score trade
get.description:
Return how far the `adjustment` trade can move each of this roll's ability scores for a class.

The response is osrlib's `AdjustmentLimits`, unchanged. osrlib computes it from the roll's scores as rolled and
from the class's prime requisites and `may_not_lower`, so it holds for every trade on this roll and class. Read it
once, when the player picks a class, and use it to drive the adjustment step's controls. A trade that
`POST /v1/characters` or `POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview` refuses doesn't change it.

Count the points the current trade buys: `raise_step` for each step of lowering. Then drive each ability's
controls from its entry in `abilities`:

- A lower control takes `lower_step` off the ability. Enable it while the current score is above `lowest` and the
  points bought are below `max_points`. When the score is at `lowest`, show `lowest_reason`. Otherwise show
  `max_points_reason`.
- A raise control adds `raise_step` to the ability. Enable it while the current score is below `highest` and the
  trade has a point that it bought and hasn't spent. When the score is at `highest`, show `highest_reason`.
  Otherwise the player has no point to spend, which your client tracks itself and which has no code.
- When `can_trade` is `false`, no trade changes a score. Disable the whole step and show `max_points_reason`.

For a class with two prime requisites, each one's `highest` is its own limit, and `max_points` caps the points
raised across both. The rules above keep the total within `max_points`, because a raise spends a point the trade
bought and the lower controls stop buying at `max_points`.

Each reason is a `Rejection`, with the `code` and `params` that the rejections of a 422 `character_invalid` have:

- `lowest_reason`: `creation.adjustment.not_lowerable`, `creation.adjustment.prime_requisite_lowered`,
  `creation.adjustment.class_restriction`, `creation.adjustment.below_floor`, or the code of `max_points_reason`.
- `highest_reason`: `creation.adjustment.raise_not_prime_requisite`, `creation.adjustment.above_cap`, or the code
  of `max_points_reason`.
- `max_points_reason`: `creation.adjustment.no_room_to_raise` when the prime requisites have room for only
  `max_points` points, or `creation.adjustment.no_room_to_lower` when the abilities the class can lower pay for
  only that many. Both have the params `{"max_points": integer}`. These two codes appear only here, never in the
  `rejections` of a 422.

`below_floor` and `above_cap` have the `ability`, and the `score` and `amount` of the first trade osrlib refuses:
the rolled score, and the amount that takes it one step past the limit.

The operation takes no `ruleset` and no other choice, and it works on a used roll, as
`GET /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}` does. The server stores nothing. A `player` key and a `referee` key can both
call this operation.

post.summary: Preview a character from an ability roll
post.description:
Return the character that `POST /v1/characters` would create from this ability roll and these choices.

The response has the `character`, its `derived` stats, and every die osrlib rolled for it in `rolls`: the dice
behind the roll's scores in `ability_rolls`, the hit point roll in `hit_point_roll`, and the starting gold roll in
`gold_roll`. Use it to show a player their hit points and starting gold before they shop, and before the character
exists. The roll stays unused. Without an `Idempotency-Key`, the server stores nothing and `storage.used_bytes`
doesn't change. With one, the server stores the response for the key, as it does for every `POST`.

Send the choices `POST /v1/characters` accepts, without `ability_roll_id`, because the path names the roll, and
without `seed`. The preview and the creation run the same steps on the roll's private seed, so:

- Every preview of one roll with the same choices returns the same response.
- `POST /v1/characters` with this roll and the same choices stores a character equal to `character`, with the
  same hit points, gold, and inventory.
- A choice that `POST /v1/characters` refuses gets the same 422 `character_invalid` here, with the same members,
  and the roll stays unused.

For one roll, `gold_roll` changes only when `class_id` or the ruleset's `hp_reroll_at_first_level` changes, and
`hit_point_roll` changes only with those two and the ruleset's `max_hp_at_first_level`. The `adjustment`,
`starting_spell_ids`, `extra_languages`, `name`, `alignment`, `purchases`, and `equip_item_ids` change neither
roll. So once the player has chosen a class under the table's ruleset, you can show the hit points and gold and
let the player make every other choice without the dice changing. A different class or reroll option can change
the gold as well as the hit points.

For the limits on the `adjustment`, call `GET /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/adjustment-limits` with the class. It
takes no other choice, so it answers before the player has chosen the starting spells that a preview of a

post.summary: Send a command to a session
post.description:
Execute one osrlib command, such as `{"command_type": "move_party", "direction": "north"}`.

Select the command variant with `command_type` (up to 65,536 bytes). `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`
lists commands legal in the current mode for your role, and `GET /v1/rules/commands/{command_type}` returns each
command's JSON Schema. Command models ignore unknown fields. Display `messages` to the player and update your UI
from `view` (pass `include=view` to receive `PlayerView` alongside `revision` in one atomic response, or call
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/view`).

Mapping `PlayerView` fields into common multi-field commands:

- **Town purchases (`purchase_equipment`):** Pass a party member's `party[i].id` (such as `"character-0001"`) as
  `character_id` and repeat equipment `id` values in `item_ids` once per purchase lot (unlike `purchases` on
  `POST /v1/characters`, which takes `{item_id, quantity}` objects).
- **Temple services (`purchase_healing`):** Pass `character_id` and a `service` from `town_healing_prices`.
  Leave `caster_level` out for the lowest level that can perform the service, which
  `town_healing_caster_levels` gives. Leave `spell_mode` out for the service's first usage, or set it to a usage
  key from `town_healing_mode_names`, such as `"cure_paralysis"` on `cure_light_wounds`.
- **Out-of-battle spells (`cast_spell`):** Pass `character_id`, `spell_id`, and `mode` set to the `key` of an
  entry in the player view's `spell_modes[spell_id]` (such as `"heal"` on `cure_light_wounds`, not the session's
  `SessionMode`), plus target IDs in `targets` (such as `["character-0001"]`). A usage whose `accepts_cells` is
  `true` also takes a cell of the level the party stands on, in the form `"cell:barrow:1:0,0"`. A usage whose
  `one_target_per_missile` is `true` takes exactly the caster's `missile_counts[spell_id]` targets.
- **Scrolls (`use_item`):** An identified spell scroll's entry in a member's `inventory` lists the spells left on
  it in `spells`. Pass one of them as `spell_id`, or leave `spell_id` out to read the first.
- **Battle rounds (`resolve_battle_round`):** Include exactly one `BattleDeclaration` in `declarations` for each
  member ID in `encounter.declarers`. Pass `target_group_id` from `encounter.groups[i].id` (such as
  `"group-0001"`) for `attack`, `close`, thrown splash items, and spells whose usage has a `target_group` of
  `"required"` or `"optional"` in `spell_modes` (such as `fire_ball`, or `sleep` with `spell_mode: "hd_budget"`).
  In battle, spell casts set `spell_mode` rather than `mode`. Spells and scrolls with `single` or `up_to_n`
  targeting (such as `magic_missile` with `spell_mode: "missiles"`) take individual `"monster-NNNN"` or
  `"npc-NNNN"` IDs from `encounter.groups[i].members` in `targets`. Use an entry whose `status` is `"alive"`.
- **Treasure caches (`inspect_treasure`, `remove_treasure_trap`, `take_treasure`):** Pass a handle from the
  player view's `features_here` as `feature_id`. The list has the `explored[i].features[j].id` of each treasure
  cache the party can reach from where it stands. The handle starts with `feature:`. Don't parse it. A referee
  tool reads the same handle from `feature_handles` in the referee view. osrlib also accepts the feature's
  authored ID from the adventure document, a legacy form, and resolves either form only among the features at
  the party's location.

When osrlib refuses a command under the B/X rules, this operation still returns HTTP 200 with `accepted` set to
`false` and rule `rejections`, leaving the session and `revision` unchanged. When accepted, the server persists
the updated state before responding, increments `revision` by 1, and returns the command's events followed by any
triggered quest or area events (filtered by `visibility`, which defaults to `player`).

To retry safely after a lost connection or timeout, send an `Idempotency-Key` header (which replays the original
`CommandOutcome`) or pass `expected_revision` (which returns 409 `revision_conflict` if the first attempt
already succeeded).

post.description:
Judge the declarations planned so far for a battle round, and show where they would leave the party.

Call this after each choice on a battle screen, with every declaration made so far, to learn which declarations
the session would refuse and whose they are. `rejections` has one entry for each declaration you sent, keyed by
the declaring member's ID, with the same `code` and `params` that `resolve_battle_round` returns on
`POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`. An empty list means the session would accept that declaration. When
you send one declaration for each member in `encounter.declarers` and every list in `rejections` is empty,
`resolve_battle_round` accepts the same declarations.

`advance_feet` gives each living member's projected place on the range track once the planned moves are made,
and `front_rank` gives each group's projected front rank, keyed by group ID. The projection leaves out what the
monsters do, because the session decides that after it rolls initiative.

`can_hide` lists the declarers who could declare `hide` beside the other planned declarations, and
`can_back_stab` lists the declarers who could declare an `attack` with `back_stab`. Use them to offer those two
choices only to a member the session would accept them from.

To learn which targets each action on a member's menu reaches before the player picks one, send the actions in
`candidates`. A candidate is an osrlib `BattleCandidate`: a `declaration` that leaves out its target, the
`target_field` that each target ID goes in (`"target_group_id"` or `"targets"`), and the `target_ids` to judge
it at. Build one candidate for each choice on the menu:

- A melee attack is an `attack` with `weapon_id`, at group IDs in `target_group_id`.
- A close and attack is the same `attack` with `move` set to `"close"`.
- Each missile weapon the member wields is an `attack` of its own with that `weapon_id`.
- A spell is a `cast` with `spell_id`, `spell_mode`, and `reversed`. Use `target_group_id` for a spell aimed at a
  group, and `targets` for one aimed at a member, a monster, or an NPC.
- A potion given to another member, or a touch with an item such as a staff of healing, is a `use_item` with
  `item_id`, at member IDs in `targets`.
- Handing over an item is a `give_item` with `item_id`, at member IDs in `targets`.

Name `weapon_id` in every `attack` candidate. When you leave it out, the session picks the weapon at the member's
projected distance to each group, and the answer doesn't say which weapon it judged. A `move` with
`fighting_withdrawal` or `retreat` can't be a candidate, because it takes no target and can turn the plan into a
formation move. Send it in `declarations` instead.

The response's `candidates` has one `BattleCandidateJudgement` for each candidate, in the order you sent them.
Its `rejections` maps each target ID to every reason the session would refuse the action there, with the same
`code` and `params` as the plan's `rejections`, and an empty list means the session would accept it. A rejection
that doesn't depend on the target, such as `battle.declaration.weapon_not_wielded`, appears under every target,
and an ID that names nothing gets the rejection the same declaration would get in the plan, such as
`battle.declaration.unknown_group`. Its `attack_kinds` maps each target ID of an `attack` candidate to `"melee"`
or `"missile"`, the kind of attack the member would make there. A target refused before the session decides the
kind of attack, for example because its group is unknown, has no entry.

Each candidate is judged in place of the member's own planned declaration, after every other member's planned
move, as `can_hide` is judged. The member's own planned move isn't made first, so a candidate that closes is judged
from where the member stands now. A candidate's entry reports only its own rejections: a close that would push
another member's planned close and attack out of the front rank is still accepted, and the other member's
rejection shows in the next preview. To send the action the player picks, set the target in the candidate's
declaration and put it in `declarations`, replacing the member's earlier declaration.

A request takes at most 64 candidates and 256 target IDs counted over every candidate's `target_ids`. Split a
larger menu over several previews.

The preview takes the session lock, rolls no dice, passes no game time, and changes nothing: `revision` stays the
same, so the request takes no `expected_revision` and needs no `Idempotency-Key`.

408.description: - `request_timeout`: The full request body didn't arrive within `BXAPI_BODY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30 seconds by default). Retry the request.

409.description:
- `not_in_battle`: The session isn't in `battle` mode (`mode` reports its mode). Read `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/view` and preview a round only while `mode` is `battle`.
- `session_busy`: The request waited more than 5 seconds for another request running on the session and made no changes. `revision` reports the session's current revision. Retry the request.
- `idempotency_key_in_progress`: The first request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running. Wait the 1 second in the `Retry-After` header and retry.
- `idempotency_key_interrupted`: The server failed or stopped while handling the first request with this `Idempotency-Key` and has no record of whether it took effect. Inspect the target resource first. If the change didn't take effect, send the request again with a new key.

413.description: - `content_too_large`: The request body exceeds 65,536 bytes (the limit for operations that take no document), or exceeds `BXAPI_MAX_BODY_BYTES` when set lower. Send a smaller body. Retrying the same body fails.

415.description: - `unsupported_media_type`: The request includes a non-empty body without a JSON `Content-Type` header. Send `Content-Type: application/json`.

421.description: - `misdirected_request`: The server runs without API keys, and the request's `Host` header isn't `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`. Call the server by one of those names, or configure API keys on the server. A server with API keys never returns this code.

Fix the request before you send it again. More than 20 `declarations`, more than 64 `candidates`, or more than 256 target IDs counted over every candidate's `target_ids` returns this code too. 503.description: - `database_busy`: Another process held the SQLite write lock for more than 5 seconds. Wait the 1 second in the `Retry-After` header and retry.

507.description: - `storage_full`: Stored documents for your client have reached `BXAPI_MAX_CLIENT_BYTES` (1,073,741,824 bytes by default). `used_bytes` and `max_bytes` report your current usage and limit, and the request stored nothing. get.description:
Return osrlib's `PlayerView`: everything the players may see at the session's current revision.

Render your game screen from this object (or pass `include=view` to `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands` to
receive `PlayerView` alongside `revision` in one response, because standalone `PlayerView` omits `revision`).
Acquires the session lock so the snapshot always reflects state between commands. The view never includes
unexplored cells, monster hit points, referee rolls, or the secret feature-handle key.

Key fields for rendering a client UI:

- `mode`: current session mode, which governs legal commands (`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`).
- `location`: `kind` is `"town"` in town, or `"dungeon"` with `dungeon_id`, `level_number`, `[x, y]` `position`,
  and `facing`.
- `party`: party members in marching order, with in-session `id` (such as `"character-0001"`, passed as
  `character_id` to commands), hit points, conditions, inventory, `scores`, `armour_class`, `thac0`, `saves`,
  `movement_rate_feet`, and `thief_skills`. Combat stats include bonuses and curses from worn unidentified magic
  items while `inventory` masks unidentified names (such as `"a shield with a faint aura"`). An identified spell
  scroll's `inventory` entry has `spells`, the spells left on it in the order `use_item` reads them, to offer as
  `use_item`'s `spell_id`.
- `dungeons`: IDs and names of dungeons the party has entered. `can_travel_to_town` states whether
  `travel_to_town` is currently usable from the party's position.
- `explored`: the party's known map for each level. Each entry includes mapped `cells` and `edges`, entered
  `areas` with their names, descriptions, and walked cells, visible `features` with opaque `feature:` IDs,
  known `transitions` without destinations or gates, and `entrance` when that cell is known. A feature's
  `emptied` is `true` once the party has emptied that authored cache, and `trap_state` on a feature or an area
  is the trap's state as the party knows it. An edge's `trap_state` marks a door where the party has found or
  sprung a room trap that opening the door springs. Feature cache contents, hidden discoveries, and destinations
  that the party hasn't learned stay omitted.
- `features_here`: the feature IDs that `inspect_treasure`, `remove_treasure_trap`, and `take_treasure` accept as
  `feature_id` from where the party stands. It's empty outside `exploring` mode.
- `spell_names`, `reversed_spell_names`, and `spell_levels`: the name and level of every spell ID the view
  shows. Each member's `spell_slots`, `preparable_spells`, and `learnable_spells` give what a `prepare_spells` or
  `learn_spell` dialog offers that member. A member's `can_prepare_now` says whether the session accepts a
  `prepare_spells` from them now, `needs_sleep_to_prepare` says whether they have to sleep first, and
  `reverses_at` says whether they choose a reversible spell's form at `"memorize"` or at `"cast"`. The names
  include the spells on an identified scroll.
- `spell_modes` and `reversed_spell_modes`: what a cast dialog offers for each spell in `spell_names`, in its
  normal form and its reverse. Each entry is osrlib's `SpellModeView` of one usage: its `key`, which you send as
  `cast_spell`'s `mode`, a battle `cast` declaration's `spell_mode`, or a scroll's `mode`, its `display_name`,
  whether it's `manual`, and the checks the session makes of its targets (`targeting`, `min_targets`,
  `max_targets`, `accepts_cells`, `target_group`, `one_target_per_missile`, and `scroll_missile_count`).
  `spell_ranges` and `reversed_spell_ranges` give each form's range as osrlib's `RangeSpec`, and
  `spell_range_texts` and `reversed_spell_range_texts` give it as the spell's page prints it, to show the player.
  Each member's `missile_counts` and `reversed_missile_counts` give how many targets that member's cast of a
  missile usage, such as `magic_missile`'s, takes.
- `item_names` and `item_names_plural`: what to call each item ID the view shows, in a member's `inventory` or
  in the `contents` of a pile in `piles`. `valuable_names` has the own name of each gem or piece of jewellery
  that has one, keyed by its instance ID, to show in a list. `valuable_phrases` has what to call each of those
  pieces in the middle of a sentence, with its article and its case, such as `"a silver altar candlestick"` or
  `"Ossor's Eye"`.
- `encounter`: active encounter state, or `null`. Pass `declarers` to build `resolve_battle_round`, and pass a
  group's `id` as `target_group_id` for attacks, `close`, thrown splash items, and spells whose usage names a
  group (such as `fire_ball` and `sleep`). Each group also has `members` with individual `"monster-NNNN"` or
  `"npc-NNNN"` IDs and coarse `status` values. Use an `"alive"` member's `id` in `targets` for a `single` or
  `up_to_n` spell or scroll. To find catalog templates matching a group's `family_id`, search
  `GET /v1/rules/monsters` with `q` and check `family_id` on `GET /v1/rules/monsters/{monster_id}`. In
  `encounter` mode, `evade_rejections` maps each `evade` `drop` value (`"none"`, `"treasure"`, and `"food"`) to
  the rejections the session would give that `evade` now, and an empty list means it would accept it. Read it to
  enable or disable each choice of a flee menu, and show the reason, such as
  `encounter.evade.nobody_able_to_act` when no living member can act or `encounter.evade.cannot_move` when a
  member is entangled or overloaded. The map is empty in `battle` mode, where the session refuses every `evade`.
  While monsters pursue the party, `pursuit_gap_feet` is the distance to the nearest pursuer, and each group's
  `distance_feet` follows the chase.
- `journal` and `quests`: discovered journal entries and active or completed quests.
- `supplies`: how long the party's light and food last, in rounds and days, so a client can show "light left"
  and "food left" without counting items. `light_reserve_usable` says whether the party has what a
  `light_source` for a carried torch or lantern needs, and `food_days` is the fewest rations any living member
  carries, with `food_short_first_ids` naming those members.
- `town_healing_prices`: gold-piece prices for temple services accepted by `purchase_healing`.
  `town_healing_funds_gp` is the whole gold pieces the party can pay toward a fee, so a service is affordable
  when its price is at most that number.
- `town_healing_rejections` and `town_healing_caster_levels`: in `town` mode, for each member ID and then each
  temple service, the rejections `purchase_healing` without `caster_level` or `spell_mode` would get, leaving the
  fee out, and the lowest cleric level that can perform each service the member can receive. An empty list means
  the temple can perform the service for that member, and the temple refuses a service that would do nothing,
  with `town.healing.no_effect` and a `reason` param. Read both to build the temple screen, and send the level as
  `caster_level`. Both maps are empty outside `town` mode.
- `town_healing_mode_rejections` and `town_healing_mode_names`: for each service that the temple sells in more
  than one usage, such as `cure_light_wounds` in `heal` and `cure_paralysis`, the same answer as
  `town_healing_rejections` for each usage, keyed by member ID, service, and usage key, and each usage's display
  name. Offer each usage with an empty list, and send its key as `purchase_healing`'s `spell_mode`.
  `town_healing_rejections` answers for each service's first usage only.

get.description:
Return osrlib's `SpellTemplate` for a spell that the session's player view names in `spell_names`.

A session's adventure can add spells to the built-in catalog, and `GET /v1/rules/spells/{spell_id}` serves only
the built-in ones. This operation reads the session's own catalog, osrlib's `GameSession.effective_spells`, so
it also answers for a spell the adventure adds.

The player view already has what a cast dialog needs: each usage's key, label, and target checks in
`spell_modes`, each form's range in `spell_ranges` and `spell_range_texts`, and each member's missile counts in
`missile_counts`. Call this operation for the rest of the spell, such as its `spell_list`, its `duration`, and
the text in `intro` and in each mode's `prose`, to show a spell's full description.

The operation serves the spells in `spell_names` and no others: the ones in a member's `spell_book`,
`memorized_spells`, `preparable_spells`, or `learnable_spells`, the ones on an identified scroll, and the ones
behind an effect on a member. So it answers for a spell the adventure adds as soon as a member could prepare or
learn it. A spell the view doesn't name gets 404 `not_found`, whether or not the session's catalog has it, so the
response doesn't reveal a spell on an unidentified scroll or a spell the adventure keeps for its monsters. A
player and a referee get the same answer.

Requires a `referee` API key. Return osrlib's `RefereeView` of the session.

Acquires the session lock to return a consistent snapshot containing the full embedded adventure, all spawned
monsters with hit points and group `monster_ids`, active effects, trigger flags, `command_log`, and `event_log`.
The view omits the master seed, RNG state, and secret feature-handle key. `feature_handles` maps each feature

401.description: - `unauthorized`: The request has no API key or has an unknown key. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with a key configured on the server. Retrying the same request fails.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer`, the authentication scheme the server accepts.

421.description: - `misdirected_request`: The server runs without API keys, and the request's `Host` header isn't `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`. Call the server by one of those names, or configure API keys on the server. A server with API keys never returns this code.

Requests without a valid API key share a separate budget and receive 429 instead of 401 `unauthorized` when that budget is exhausted.

post.description:
Start a new session from a saved checkpoint and return the new session's metadata at revision 0.

Save the returned session `id`, then continue play with `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands` and
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/view`. The new session inherits the save's `adventure_id`, `mode`, `clock`, party,
and RNG state, while leaving both the save and the original session untouched so one save can be restored any
number of times. The request body is optional: pass `name` to title the new session, or send an empty body.

parameters.description: Client-chosen key (1 to 255 printable ASCII characters with no spaces, such as a UUID) that deduplicates retries of this `POST` for 24 hours. Resending the identical request with the same key returns the stored 2xx response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of running the operation again.

400.description: - `bad_request`: The body doesn't decode as text, or contains a disallowed value: an integer with more than 4,300 digits, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a number too large for a 64-bit float, a string with half of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, or arrays and objects nested more than 100 levels deep. Check `detail` and send UTF-8 JSON without those values. Retrying the same body fails.

408.description: - `request_timeout`: The full request body didn't arrive within `BXAPI_BODY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30 seconds by default). Retry the request.

- `idempotency_key_interrupted`: The server failed or stopped while handling the first request with this `Idempotency-Key` and has no record of whether it took effect. Inspect the target resource first. If the change didn't take effect, send the request again with a new key.

Retry-After.description: With `idempotency_key_in_progress`, whole seconds to wait before retrying: `1`.

413.description: - `content_too_large`: The request body exceeds 65,536 bytes (the limit for operations that take no document), or exceeds `BXAPI_MAX_BODY_BYTES` when set lower. Send a smaller body. Retrying the same body fails.

415.description: - `unsupported_media_type`: The request includes a non-empty body without a JSON `Content-Type` header. Send `Content-Type: application/json`.

422.description:
- `validation_error`: The request doesn't match the operation's schema. A required field is missing, a value has the wrong type or is out of range, or the body isn't valid JSON. `errors` lists the first 20 problems, and the `loc` of each is the path to the value. Fix the request before you send it again.
- `idempotency_key_reused`: Your client already sent this `Idempotency-Key` with a different method, path, query, body, or role. Generate a new key for each distinct request.

Requests without a valid API key share a separate budget and receive 429 instead of 401 `unauthorized` when that budget is exhausted.

- `internal_error`: The server failed because of a bug. The response says nothing about the cause, and the server logs it. Report the request to the server's operator.
- `session_unreadable`: The server's osrlib can't load the save's stored document or refuses its embedded adventure. Report `save_id` and `request_id` to the server's operator.

503.description: - `database_busy`: Another process held the SQLite write lock for more than 5 seconds. Wait the 1 second in the `Retry-After` header and retry.

507.description: - `storage_full`: Stored documents for your client have reached `BXAPI_MAX_CLIENT_BYTES` (1,073,741,824 bytes by default). `used_bytes` and `max_bytes` report your current usage and limit, and the request stored nothing. Delete unused sessions, saves, adventures, or characters, then retry. Stateless operations such as dice rolls return this code only when `Idempotency-Key` is set, because storing the replay response counts toward the limit.

get.description:
Requires a `referee` API key. Return the complete save document envelope (`kind`, `schema_version`, `payload`).

Contains the session's master seed, RNG streams, unexplored map, monster hit points, `command_log`, and
`event_log`, so players receive 403 `referee_required` (use `GET /v1/saves/{save_id}` for player-safe metadata).
Pass the returned JSON object to `POST /v1/saves/import` on another server to migrate the game.

lowered.title: Lowered
lowered.description:
How much to take off each ability, as a positive number.

Only strength, intelligence, and wisdom may appear, each amount must be even, and no
score may end below `ADJUSTMENT_FLOOR`.

raised.title: Raised
raised.description:
How much to add to each ability, as a positive number.

Only the class's prime requisites may appear, the amounts must add up to half the
points taken off, and no score may end above
`MAX_SCORE`.

AbilityAdjustment.title: AbilityAdjustment
AbilityAdjustment.description:
A proposed trade of ability points, made once while a character is being created.

Build one from what the player chose, check it with
`validate_adjustment`, and apply it
with `apply_adjustment`, or pass it to
`create_character` as `adjustment`. The
exchange rate is two points down for one point up. The points bought can go only into
the class's prime requisites, the abilities the class is built around. An amount of
zero or less raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

An empty adjustment is legal and changes nothing. Build one for a player who keeps the
scores as rolled.

can_lower.title: Can Lower
can_lower.description: Whether some legal trade lowers this ability. It's true exactly when `lowest` is below the rolled score.

can_raise.title: Can Raise
can_raise.description: Whether some legal trade raises this ability. It's true exactly when `highest` is above the rolled score.

lowest.title: Lowest
lowest.description:
The lowest score a legal trade leaves this ability at.

It's the rolled score when the ability can't be lowered. It's always the rolled score
less a multiple of `lower_step`. For
example, a score of 10 has a `lowest` of 10, because one step would take it to 8, below
`ADJUSTMENT_FLOOR`.

lowest_reason.description:
Why no legal trade leaves this ability lower than `lowest`.

When a rule about this ability refuses one more step, this is the first rejection that
`validate_adjustment` reports for lowering
the ability by `score - lowest + lower_step`, where `score` is the rolled score. The code is
`creation.adjustment.not_lowerable`, `creation.adjustment.prime_requisite_lowered`,
`creation.adjustment.class_restriction`, or `creation.adjustment.below_floor`, whose `score`
and `amount` params are the rolled score and that refused amount. When the ability has more
to give but the prime requisites have no room for the points, this is the same rejection as
`max_points_reason`.

highest.title: Highest
highest.description:
The highest score a legal trade leaves this ability at.

It's the rolled score when the ability can't be raised. Only a prime requisite of the
class can be raised, and no further than
`MAX_SCORE`.

highest_reason.description:
Why no legal trade leaves this ability higher than `highest`.

For an ability that isn't a prime requisite, this is
`creation.adjustment.raise_not_prime_requisite`. For a prime requisite that the cap
stops, it's the `creation.adjustment.above_cap` rejection that
`validate_adjustment` reports for raising
the ability by `highest - score + raise_step`, where `score` is the rolled score. Its
`score` and `amount` params are the rolled score and that refused amount. When the cap
leaves room but the lowerable abilities can't
pay for more points, this is the same rejection as
`max_points_reason`.

AbilityAdjustmentLimit.title: AbilityAdjustmentLimit
AbilityAdjustmentLimit.description:
How far one ability score can move in a legal points trade, and why it can't move further.

`adjustment_limits` returns one for each ability
in `AdjustmentLimits.abilities`. Each
limit is the furthest that any legal trade moves this ability, counting the other abilities
that pay for its points or take the points it pays for. Use `lowest` and `highest` as the
bounds of the ability's control, and disable lowering when `can_lower` is false and raising
when `can_raise` is false.

Each limit is reachable on its own, but the player still has to balance the whole trade,
as `AdjustmentLimits` describes. For example,
when two abilities can each pay for every point the prime requisites have room for, the
player can lower either one to its `lowest`, but not both.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Ability roll identifier (`rol_` followed by 22 characters). Pass as `ability_roll_id` to
`POST /v1/characters`, or as `roll_id` to `POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview`.

scores.title: Scores
scores.description: Six rolled ability scores (`str`, `int`, `wis`, `dex`, `con`, `cha`), each from 3 to 18.

ability_score_method.title: Ability Score Method
ability_score_method.description:
How osrlib rolled the scores: `"3d6"` or `"4d6_drop_lowest"`, from the `ability_score_method` of the
`ruleset` that `POST /v1/ability-rolls` received. A preview or a creation from this roll needs a `ruleset`
with the same method.

rolls.description:
osrlib's `AbilityScoreRolls` behind `scores`, the same as `rolls.ability_rolls` on
`POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview`. `rolls.rolls` has the three d6 that count toward each score, in
the order osrlib rolled them. `rolls.dropped` has the die that a `4d6_drop_lowest` roll dropped for each
ability, and it's empty for a `3d6` roll. `rolls.sub_par` is `true` when the scores are sub-par under the B/X
rule that lets a referee allow a new roll: every score is 8 or less, or two or more scores are 5 or less.

eligible_class_ids.title: Eligible Class Ids
eligible_class_ids.description:
Class `id` values from `GET /v1/rules/classes` whose minimum ability requirements `scores`
satisfy, in catalog order.

used.title: Used
used.description:
Whether `POST /v1/characters` has already consumed this roll. Each roll creates at most one
character, and deleting that character does not reset `used`.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when the server stored the roll, in RFC 3339 format such as
`"2026-11-20T22:01:05Z"`.

AbilityRoll.title: AbilityRoll
AbilityRoll.description: Stored set of six rolled ability scores and the classes they qualify for.

anyOf.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

seed.title: Seed
seed.description:
Referee only. Seed (0 to 2^53 - 1) that determines the six ability scores as well as the hit
point and gold rolls of the character created from this roll. The server never returns `seed`.
Omit `seed` (or send no body) to let the server draw one.

ruleset.description:
Optional rules for the roll, as osrlib's `Ruleset`. Send the ruleset of the table the
character is for, the one you pass to `POST /v1/sessions`. The roll reads one field,
`ability_score_method`: `"3d6"` (the default) rolls three d6 for each score, and
`"4d6_drop_lowest"` rolls four and drops the lowest. The server stores the method with the roll.
Send the same ruleset when you preview or create the character from the roll. Omit or set to
`null` for the rules as written.

AbilityScore.title: AbilityScore
AbilityScore.description: One of the six B/X ability scores: `str` (Strength), `int` (Intelligence), `wis` (Wisdom), `dex` (Dexterity), `con` (Constitution), or `cha` (Charisma). Score objects use these six lowercase strings as keys and require all six.

scores.title: Scores
scores.description:
The total of each ability's three counted dice, keyed by `AbilityScore`.
All six abilities are present, each from 3 to 18.

rolls.title: Rolls
rolls.description:
The three d6 results that count towards each score, keyed the same way, in the order they were thrown.

All six abilities are present, each die is from 1 to 6, and each score is the sum of its three
dice. With the `"4d6_drop_lowest"` method, the die dropped from an ability's four is in `dropped`
instead, and the other three keep their order here.

dropped.title: Dropped
dropped.description:
The die that didn't count towards each score, keyed the same way.

A `"4d6_drop_lowest"` roll has an entry for all six abilities: the lowest of the four dice, or the
first of them thrown when two or more tie for lowest. A `"3d6"` roll drops nothing, so this is
empty, and so is a roll that osrlib 2.8.0 or earlier recorded. Read an ability with no entry as one
with no die dropped. To show all four dice of an ability, show its three `rolls` and this die.
When it isn't empty, all six abilities are present, and each die is from 1 to the lowest of the
ability's three `rolls`.

sub_par.title: Sub Par
sub_par.description:
Whether `scores` are sub-par, so that a referee may let the player discard the character and start again.

The SRD's "Sub-Par Characters" rule says: "If you roll a character with very poor ability scores—for example an
8 or less in every score or an extremely low rating in more than one ability—the referee may allow you to
discard the character and start again." It's true when every score is 8 or less, or when two or more scores
are 5 or less, as `scores_are_sub_par` decides.

The value is computed from `scores` each time you read it, so it's right for a roll that osrlib 2.8.0 or
earlier recorded too. It's in `model_dump()` and in the JSON, so a client that receives the roll as a document
can read it there. When you parse a document, a `sub_par` key in it is ignored.

It answers for the scores as rolled, before the adjustment step, so the `ability_rolls` of a
`CharacterCreationResult` says whether the character was
sub-par as rolled, whatever the adjustment changed afterwards. With the `"4d6_drop_lowest"` method, it's
decided by the three dice that count. osrlib only reports it. Whether the referee allows the discard is your
game's choice, so `Ruleset` has no flag for it, and
`create_character` never refuses or rerolls sub-par scores.

AbilityScoreRolls.title: AbilityScoreRolls
AbilityScoreRolls.description:
The six rolled ability scores, with the dice behind each, so you can show them.

`roll_ability_scores` returns one, and
`create_character` includes one in its result. Pass
`scores` to `validate_class_choice`, and read
`sub_par` to find out whether a referee may let the player start again. Frozen.

Parsing a document raises `pydantic.ValidationError` when `scores`, `rolls`, or `dropped` breaks
what its field says, so a roll you parse is one that the dice could have thrown.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: The strength table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

intelligence.title: Intelligence
intelligence.description: The intelligence table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

wisdom.title: Wisdom
wisdom.description: The wisdom table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

dexterity.title: Dexterity
dexterity.description: The dexterity table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

constitution.title: Constitution
constitution.description: The constitution table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

charisma.title: Charisma
charisma.description: The charisma table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

prime_requisite.title: Prime Requisite
prime_requisite.description: The prime requisite experience table's rows, lowest score first, together covering 3 to 18 with no gaps.

AbilityTables.title: AbilityTables
AbilityTables.description:
The SRD's ability tables, and the accessors that read a score out of them.

Get one from `load_ability_tables`, which loads the
tables that come with the package and caches them, so calling it again costs nothing.
Then call the accessor for the column you want, passing a score from
`MIN_SCORE` to
`MAX_SCORE`. A score outside that range raises
`ValueError`, because it's a mistake in your code, not an outcome the rules allow.

A `Character` reads these tables for you and offers
the results as properties, so use the accessors when you have a bare score and no
character.

The fields contain the raw rows. Read them to draw a table, and use the accessors to
play.

ac.title: Ac
ac.description: The armour class in the descending presentation, where lower is better.

ac_ascending.title: Ac Ascending
ac_ascending.description: The same armour class in the ascending presentation, where higher is better.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description:
When this value applies, in the SRD's words, like `"in human form"`.

Empty when the SRD prints the alternative without a condition, as it does for a band whose
members wear different armour.

AcAlternate.title: AcAlternate
AcAlternate.description:
An armour class a monster has only in particular circumstances.

Read them from
`MonsterTemplate.ac_alternates`. The SRD
prints more than one armour class for a creature that changes shape, or for a band whose members
wear different armour. The template's `ac` is the usual value, and these are the others.
Deciding when one applies is the referee's call, and osrlib never switches to one. Frozen.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"activate_quest"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

quest_id.title: Quest Id
quest_id.description:
Which quest to put into play, by
`QuestSpec.id` from the adventure's quests. The session
refuses an id that matches no quest spec with `session.command.unknown_quest`.

ActivateQuest.title: ActivateQuest
ActivateQuest.description:
Referee: put one of the adventure's quests into play.

This is the first of the quest commands, which change an adventure's quest state:
`ActivateQuest`,
`RevealObjective`,
`CompleteObjective`, and
`CompleteQuest`. Each quest has a status that
moves from `inactive` to `active` to `completed` and never back. Each of its objectives
is either hidden or revealed, and either complete or not. The session stores this state,
and only the quest commands change it, so a replay of the command log rebuilds it.

The quest commands accept only the quest and objective ids that the adventure's
`QuestSpec`s define, and refuse any other id, because
the player view gets an active quest's name, offer, and objectives from its spec.
`MarkTriggerFired` is different and
accepts any trigger id.

Issue the quest commands yourself when you run the quests in your code. To have the
quests run from the rules in the adventure instead, register an
`Interpreter`.

When the quest's author wrote an `offer` text in its narrative, an accepted activation
adds that text to the journal, and the event includes it. No
`JournalEntryAddedEvent` follows, because
the quest's event already includes the text. Only an `inactive` quest can be activated.
This command is legal in every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.unknown_quest` - `quest_id` matches no quest of the
  adventure.
- `session.command.quest_state` - the quest is already active or already
  completed. The rejection includes the quest id and its current state.

**Events:**

`QuestActivatedEvent` with the
quest id, the quest's name, and the offer text.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description:
The id of the `ActiveEffect` that granted the condition and will take
it back. `null` marks a condition that doesn't come from a timed effect. In osrlib, that's `dead`.

ActiveCondition.title: ActiveCondition
ActiveCondition.description:
One condition a creature currently has, paired with the effect that granted it.

You read these from a creature's `conditions` tuple rather than building them.
`EffectsLedger.attach` and
`grant_condition` add them. To ask whether a creature has a condition
from any effect, call `has_condition` instead of scanning the tuple.

Each record contains the id of the effect that granted it, so two effects can grant the same condition, and
ending one effect removes only the record that effect granted. A creature charmed twice has two records, and
releasing one charm leaves the other in place. Records compare by value, and a creature never has the same
condition from the same effect twice.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description:
The effect's id, like `effect-0001`, from the `IdAllocator` you
passed to `attach`. The conditions and modifiers the effect granted contain this id, which is how the ledger
finds them when the effect ends.

definition.description:
The `EffectDefinition` the effect was attached from. The ledger
ticks and expires the effect from this copy, so a saved ledger needs nothing else.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description:
What the effect is on. It's an entity id for a creature, or a location string, like one from
`cell_ref`, for an effect that stays in a place, like a pool of burning oil.
A location string isn't a key in the registry, so an effect on a location grants no conditions or
modifiers.

attached_round.title: Attached Round
attached_round.description:
The round the effect was attached on, counted from the start of the game clock. The effect ticks every
`tick_interval_rounds` from this round. When several effects resolve in one round, they go in order of this
value first, then in the order they were attached, which is their order in
`EffectsLedger.effects`.

expires_round.title: Expires Round
expires_round.description:
The round the effect expires on, counted from the start of the game clock, or `null` when it has no
duration or is permanent. While the bearer is petrified by another effect, this moves forward one round for
each round that passes. A suspended effect therefore has the same time left when the stone is undone.

caster_level.title: Caster Level
caster_level.description:
The level of the caster whose spell attached this effect, or `null` when `attach` got no `caster_level`.
When *dispel magic* tries to end the effect, osrlib rolls against it to decide whether the effect survives.

state.title: State
state.description:
The effect's running counters, like `revive_at`, the round a dead troll gets up on, or `rest_days`, the
rest days counted so far for a slowed-healing effect. The ledger and
`natural_healing` write it. Read it to show a countdown.

ActiveEffect.title: ActiveEffect
ActiveEffect.description:
One effect currently running on a creature or a location.

`EffectsLedger.attach` creates one, adds it to the ledger's
`effects` list, and returns it. `EffectsLedger.active_on` finds
it again. Read it to see how long the effect has left or what it is tracking. Pass its `effect_id` to
`EffectsLedger.release` to end it early. You don't build these
yourself. When `load_game` restores a ledger from a save, it rebuilds them.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
Which statistic the modifier adjusts, one of `MODIFIER_KINDS`. Any
other value raises pydantic's `ValidationError`.

value.title: Value
value.description:
The signed adjustment, like +1 for *bless*'s attack bonus or -1 for *protection from evil*'s penalty on
attackers. For `ac_set` and `ac_set_vs_missile` it's the armour class to set, and for `strength_set` the
strength score. Leave it at 0 for a kind that uses `dice` or acts as a flag.

dice.title: Dice
dice.description:
A dice expression rolled instead of adding `value`, for a kind that grants dice, like *striking*'s `"1d6"`
of extra weapon damage. osrlib checks it with `parse`, so a malformed
expression raises `ContentValidationError` when you build the
`ModifierSpec`, not when the combat code rolls it.

element.title: Element
element.description:
Narrows the modifier to one damage or save element, like `"fire"` for *resist fire*. The modifier counts
only for a roll with that same element. `null` means every element.

versus_other_alignment.title: Versus Other Alignment
versus_other_alignment.description:
True narrows the modifier to rolls against creatures of a different alignment, which is how *protection
from evil* works. The modifier then counts only when the call that reads it passes `versus_differs=True`.

save_categories.title: Save Categories
save_categories.description:
Narrows a save bonus to the named saving throw categories. A Displacer Cloak, for example, covers
`"paralysis"`, `"wands"`, and `"spells"` but not the others. Empty means every category.

melee_only.title: Melee Only
melee_only.description:
True narrows the modifier to melee attacks. That's how the Displacer Cloak's -2 on attackers leaves
missile attacks alone. The modifier then counts only when the call that reads it passes `melee=True`.

from_item.title: From Item
from_item.description:
True marks the modifier as coming from a magic item rather than a spell. Such a modifier is exempt from
the rule that only the largest spell bonus and the largest spell penalty count:
`modifier_total` adds every item modifier to the capped spell total.
Set it on the effects of potions and scrolls as well as worn items, because the rule covers magic items in
general.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description:
The id of the `ActiveEffect` that granted the modifier and will take
it back.

ActiveModifier.title: ActiveModifier
ActiveModifier.description:
One live modifier on a creature, paired with the effect that granted it.

These are the entries of a creature's `stat_modifiers` tuple. Attaching an effect turns each
`ModifierSpec` in its definition into one of these. When the effect
expires or is released, the ledger removes them again, the same way it removes conditions. Nothing else in
osrlib writes the tuple, so each modifier on a creature belongs to an effect on the ledger.

Read them through `modifier_total` rather than scanning the tuple,
because it applies the scope fields and the rule that spell bonuses don't add up.
`modifier_values`, `modifier_dice`,
and `has_modifier` cover the other ways the combat code reads them.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"add_journal_entry"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

text.title: Text
text.description:
The line to add, as the players will read it. The session stamps it with the clock time,
adds it to the end of the journal, and returns it unchanged in
`PlayerView.journal`. Entries are never rewritten,
so write the line you want kept.

AddJournalEntry.title: AddJournalEntry
AddJournalEntry.description:
Referee: add a line of story text to the session's journal.

The journal is the party's record of the adventure, in the order the party discovered
things. Entries are only ever added: none is rewritten, and none is rebuilt from other
state, so an entry stays after whatever caused it is gone. Each entry is stamped with
the game clock's time when it's added, and
`PlayerView.journal` returns the entries as they
were written. This command is legal in every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included, so you
can add a closing line after the adventure has ended.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

None.

**Events:**

`JournalEntryAddedEvent` with
the text and the clock time.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"add_member"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

character.description:
The character who joins. Build it with
`create_character` and pass its `character`. It
needs `id` set to `null`, no conditions or stat modifiers, and no magic items or valuables.
Constructing the command copies the character. A change you make
to your object afterwards doesn't reach the command, and the command log records the
character as you sent it. The member who joins gets the display names of the session's catalog
on each item template the character's stacks embed, as
`ItemInstance.template` describes, while the
command keeps the templates it arrived with.

AddMember.title: AddMember
AddMember.description:
Referee: add a character to the party during play.

Use it to bring a new character into a running game: a replacement for a character who
died, a prisoner the party set free, or an adventurer the party meets in town. Build the
character with `create_character`, the way you
build a starting party member, and send it here in `town` or `exploring`.

The session gives the new member an id and puts them at the back of the marching order, so
the front rank doesn't change. To move them, send
`ReorderParty`, which is legal in the same modes. The
session logs the command, so a saved game and a replay both have the new member.

The new id has the form `character-NNNN` and is unique in the party. It's never the id of a
member who left with `RemoveMember`. Read it from the
event, and pass it as the `character_id` of later commands. The session adds a copy of
`character`, not the object you pass. Your object stays as it was, with no id. Read the new
member with `GameSession.member`.

The character must be fresh:

- The character can't have a condition or a stat modifier, `dead` included. Each one comes
  from an effect in the game that applied it, and this session can't end an effect it
  doesn't track.
- The character can't carry a magic item or a valuable. Each has an instance id from the
  game that created it, which could match an id this session hands out. Mundane gear and
  coins are fine. Give magic items afterwards with
  `GrantItem`, which creates them with this session's
  ids.

The coins the new member brings earn no experience, because the party didn't find them as
treasure. Adding a member makes no draws and takes no time.

The session refuses the command during an encounter or a battle, because the fight is
already set up for the party it started with. It also refuses the command once the session
has ended, because a new member would restart play. To replace a party whose members are
all dead or turned to stone, first send `PlaceParty` to move it to town, which
takes the session out of `game_over`. Then add the new character.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - an encounter or a battle is open, or the session
  has ended.
- `party.add.id_assigned` - the character's `id` isn't `null`. The character has an
  id from another game, or is already a member.
- `party.add.under_effects` - the character has a condition, like `dead` or
  `asleep`, or a stat modifier.
- `party.add.carries_instances` - the character carries a magic item or a valuable,
  equipped or not.

The session checks in this order and reports the first that fails.

**Events:**

`MemberAddedEvent` with the new member's id,
name, class, and level.

lower_step.title: Lower Step
lower_step.description:
The points one step of the trade takes off a lowered ability, which is 2.

Move a lowering control in steps of this size.

raise_step.title: Raise Step
raise_step.description: The points one step of lowering buys for a prime requisite, which is 1.

can_trade.title: Can Trade
can_trade.description:
Whether some legal trade changes a score. It's true exactly when `max_points` is above 0.

When it's false, the only legal trade is the empty one, so you can skip the trade step.

max_points.title: Max Points
max_points.description:
The most points a legal trade buys for the prime requisites, and 0 when `can_trade` is false.

It's the smaller of two totals: the points the lowerable abilities can pay for before
they reach `ADJUSTMENT_FLOOR`, and the points
the prime requisites have room for below
`MAX_SCORE`.

max_points_reason.description:
Why no legal trade buys more than `max_points`.

The code is one of the following, and its `max_points` param equals `max_points`:

- `creation.adjustment.no_room_to_raise`: the prime requisites have no more room below
  `MAX_SCORE`. This is the code when the two totals
  that `max_points` compares are equal, and when every prime requisite is already 18.
- `creation.adjustment.no_room_to_lower`: the abilities that can be lowered can't pay for
  more points without going below
  `ADJUSTMENT_FLOOR`.

`validate_adjustment` never returns these
two codes. They explain where the limits stop, and a proposed trade that goes past a
limit breaks one of the rules that `validate_adjustment` does report.

abilities.title: Abilities
abilities.description: The limits on each of the six abilities, keyed in `AbilityScore` order.

AdjustmentLimits.title: AdjustmentLimits
AdjustmentLimits.description:
The limits on the points trade for one set of rolled scores and one class.

`adjustment_limits` returns one. Read
`can_trade` to decide whether to offer the trade at all, and the entry for each ability
in `abilities` to set the bounds of its control.

A trade is legal exactly when all of these hold:

- Each lowered amount is a multiple of `lower_step` and no greater than the ability's
  `score - lowest`.
- Each raised amount is no greater than the ability's `highest - score`.
- The points raised add up to the points lowered divided by `lower_step` and multiplied
  by `raise_step`.
- The points raised add up to no more than `max_points`.

A client that enforces these conditions proposes only legal trades and doesn't need to
implement any trade rule itself.

command_type.title: Command Type
