command_type.description: Always `"advance_time"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

n.title: N
n.description:
How many of `unit` to advance, up to 28 days of game time: 28 days, 4,032 turns, or
241,920 rounds. A larger `n` for its `unit` fails validation when the command is
constructed, so the session never sees it. For more time, send the command again. `0` is
legal, advances nothing, and still emits the `TimeAdvancedEvent`.

unit.description:
Which unit `n` counts: rounds, turns, or days. A B/X turn is 10 minutes, or 60 rounds,
and a day is 144 turns. Effects expire across the whole time whichever unit you pick, and
the party eats provisions at each day boundary the time crosses.

AdvanceTime.title: AdvanceTime
AdvanceTime.description:
Referee: move the game clock forward.

Use it for time that passes outside the commands, like a week of travel or a
referee's "an hour later". This command is legal in every mode, `game_over` and
`victory` included, so the clock keeps running after the party dies. The time limits on spells
that bring the dead back are measured on this clock. Everything that happens with time
happens as usual, like effects expiring and provisions eaten each day. The engine makes no
wandering-monster checks for it, because the referee decides on encounters, and the time
doesn't count toward the party's rest.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

None.

**Events:**

The events of the time passing: effects that expire, a
`LightEvent` for each light that burns out, and
`ProvisionsEvent`s. Then a
`TimeAdvancedEvent` with the clock's new
total.

name.title: Name
name.description: The adventure's title, to show the player.

description.title: Description
description.description: Text describing the adventure, to show the player.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.description:
The reasons a party might take the adventure on, as free-form strings, like a rumour in the
tavern or a patron's offer. osrlib never reads them. They let the adventure document include its
pitch.

party.description:
The levels and number of characters the adventure is written for, or `null` when it
doesn't give one. osrlib never reads it. See `PartySpec`.

town.description:
The base town. There is exactly one, and the session starts there. See
`TownSpec`.

dungeons.title: Dungeons
dungeons.description:
The dungeons, at least one, each with a unique id. One level of each dungeon needs an
`entrance`, because that is where the party arrives from town.

monsters.title: Monsters
monsters.description:
`MonsterTemplate`s the adventure adds to the built-in
catalog. In the sessions that play this adventure, they work everywhere a monster template id
does: keyed encounters, `SpawnMonsters`, wandering tables
on a level, and listening at doors.

A bundled id can't be the same as a built-in id or another bundled id.
`validate_adventure` reports a repeated id instead
of letting one template replace the other, because the template id in a
session's events has to refer to one monster. Each treasure type letter in a bundled template's
`treasure` has to be a B/X treasure type, `A` to `V`, and `validate_adventure` reports one that
isn't. The guide
[Authoring custom classes, spells, monsters, and items](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/guides/authoring-custom-content/)
covers writing a monster template.

items.title: Items
items.description:
`ItemTemplate`s the adventure adds to the built-in equipment
catalog: weapons, armour, gear, and ammunition. In the sessions that play this adventure, they
work everywhere an authored item id does: treasure caches, `has_item` gates,
`GrantItem`, and picking up a drop pile. An item instance
includes its template, so a bundled item can be given, equipped, and dropped like any other.

A bundled id can't be the same as an id in the equipment catalog, the magic-item catalog, or
another bundled item, because one item id has to mean one thing in a session. The town shop
doesn't sell bundled items. It sells only the built-in equipment.

spells.title: Spells
spells.description:
`SpellTemplate`s the adventure adds to the built-in spell
catalog. In the sessions that play this adventure, they work everywhere a spell id does:
`PrepareSpells`,
`LearnSpell`, `CastSpell`,
and a `cast` declaration in a battle. A caster can prepare and cast a bundled spell when the
spell's `spell_list` is the list of the caster's class, as for a built-in spell.
`GameSession.effective_spells` is the catalog
the session looks them up in.

A bundled id can't be the same as a built-in spell id or another bundled id, because a spell id
on a character and in a session's events has to refer to one spell.
`validate_adventure` reports a repeated id instead of
letting one template replace the other.

To give a new caster a bundled spell in their first spell book, pass a catalog with the same
spells to `create_character` as `spell_catalog`. The
spells on a scroll that treasure rolls, and the spells of an NPC adventurer, come from the
built-in catalog only. The guide
[Authoring custom classes, spells, monsters, and items](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/guides/authoring-custom-content/)
covers writing a spell and bundling it.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description:
The adventure's `TriggerSpec`s: what happens when
something happens in play. Triggers that match the same event fire in the order of this tuple.

Triggers do nothing by themselves. To play them, register an
`Interpreter` on the session. An adventure with no
triggers plays the same whether or not one is registered. See the guide
[Gates, triggers, and quests](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/guides/gates-triggers-quests/).

quests.title: Quests
quests.description:
The adventure's `QuestSpec`s: what the party is trying to do.
When `GameSession.new` creates the session, it sets up
the state of each quest in this order, and it goes
through the quests in this order whenever it checks them.

The session keeps quest state apart from trigger state, so quest ids and trigger ids don't
clash, and a quest can have the same id as a trigger.

Adventure.title: Adventure
Adventure.description:
An adventure: one or more dungeons, the base town, and everything they need.

This is the root of the content tree and the document a session plays. Build the levels first,
put them in `DungeonSpec`s, write a
`TownSpec`, and construct the adventure from them. Then call
`GameSession.new` with a
`Party` and the adventure. It validates the adventure, gives each
party member an entity id, combines the built-in catalogs with the templates the adventure
bundles, sets up the state of each quest, and returns a session with the party in town. The
adventure is frozen, and it stays as you wrote it for the life of the session.

Every model in the tree is a pydantic model with keyword arguments, so you can write an
adventure as Python calls, generate it from your own file format, or round-trip it through
JSON with pydantic's `model_dump_json` and `model_validate_json`. osrlib has no function that
reads an adventure from a file.

visibility.description: Player visibility: it's the party's ending.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `adventure_completed`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

quest_id.title: Quest Id
quest_id.description: The quest that concluded the adventure.

name.title: Name
name.description:
That quest's display name. The engine always fills it. It's empty only on an event loaded
from a save written before the field existed.

narrative.title: Narrative
narrative.description:
The quest's completion text, the same line as on its
`QuestCompletedEvent`, or `null`.

AdventureCompletedEvent.title: AdventureCompletedEvent
AdventureCompletedEvent.description:
The adventure is over and the party won.

Emitted by `CompleteQuest` when the quest
that concludes the adventure completes, right after that quest's
`QuestCompletedEvent`, with the same
text. The session mode becomes `victory`, which is final: the session refuses play
commands and never leaves that mode, so you can show a closing screen.

A session that has already ended doesn't end twice. When a party that has already
fallen completes the quest, the quest completes with no `AdventureCompletedEvent`,
and the session stays in `game_over`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Adventure title.

description.title: Description
description.description: Player-facing introduction written by the adventure's author, or `""` when none is set.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.description: Plot hooks giving the party reasons to undertake the adventure.

party.description:
Recommended character levels and party size as osrlib's `PartySpec`, or `null` when
unspecified.

town.description: Starting town where new sessions of this adventure begin.

dungeons.title: Dungeons
dungeons.description: Dungeons in the adventure, in document order.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Adventure identifier (`builtin-` prefix for built-in adventures, or `adv_` followed by 22
characters for client uploads), or `null` in the response from `POST /v1/adventures/validate`.

builtin.title: Builtin
builtin.description:
Whether the adventure ships with the server (`true`) rather than belonging to your client
(`false`). Built-in adventures cannot be deleted.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when your client uploaded the adventure (RFC 3339 format, such as
`"2026-11-20T22:01:05Z"`), or `null` for built-in adventures and validation previews.

AdventureInfo.title: AdventureInfo
AdventureInfo.description: Player-visible adventure summary along with storage metadata.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the party sees what it earned.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `adventure_xp_award`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

monster_xp.title: Monster Xp
monster_xp.description: What the defeated creatures were worth, added up across the whole delve.

treasure_xp.title: Treasure Xp
treasure_xp.description:
What the recovered treasure was worth, one experience point per gold piece of value gained
since the party left town, and never less than zero.

share.title: Share
share.description:
What each survivor receives: the total divided by the number of survivors, rounded down.
When it rounds down to zero, no `XpAwardedEvent` follows.

survivors.title: Survivors
survivors.description:
The members who made it back, in marching order. The dead count toward the treasure that
came home but take no share.

AdventureXpAwardEvent.title: AdventureXpAwardEvent
AdventureXpAwardEvent.description:
The experience award for a trip to the dungeon: what the party earned and what each survivor gets.

Emitted by `TravelToTown` under the default
ruleset, where experience is awarded for making it back. Each survivor's
`XpAwardedEvent` follows it, each followed by
a `CharacterLeveledUpEvent` when that
member gains a level.

Treasure counts as the gain in the value of the party's coins, gems, and jewellery
since it left town, so goods still lying in the dungeon are worth nothing yet. The session
emits no event when nobody came back alive or when the delve earned nothing.

Alignment.title: Alignment
Alignment.description:
The cosmic principle a creature follows: law, neutrality, or chaos.

Use a member by name (`Alignment.LAWFUL`) when you write the value yourself, and call
the enum on a string (`Alignment("lawful")`) when the value comes from saved data or
from a player's input. A string that isn't one of the three values raises
`ValueError`. Each member compares equal to its lowercase string, so
`Alignment.LAWFUL == "lawful"` is true.

osrlib applies no mechanical penalty for acting against alignment. The SRD leaves
that to the referee. What osrlib does use is the alignment tongue that comes from the
value, and the alignment comparisons in the rules for some spells and magic items.

Characters and saved games contain the lowercase values, and they stay fixed within a
`schema_version`, the version stamp that identifies a serialized model's format.

options.title: Options
options.description:
The alignments this creature may have, at least one. A troll is always chaotic. A creature the SRD prints
as any alignment has all three here.

usual.description:
Which of the options the creature usually has, when the SRD gives one. `null` when it doesn't.

A creature with several options and no usual one spawns with no alignment unless you pass one to
`spawn_monster`.

AlignmentSpec.title: AlignmentSpec
AlignmentSpec.description:
Which alignments a monster may have, and which it usually has.

Read it as `MonsterTemplate.alignment`.
`spawn_monster` gives each creature it spawns one
alignment, because the wards that depend on alignment, like *protection from evil*, need one
alignment to test against. Frozen.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The catalog id, for example `"arrows"`. Get every id from `load_equipment`, or see
[the equipment id index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/equipment/).

name.title: Name
name.description: The display name as the price list prints it, which includes the lot: `"Arrows (quiver of 20)"`.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description:
What to call one unit of this ammunition in a sentence, like `"arrow"` or `"crossbow bolt"`.

It names one of the units that `ItemInstance.quantity`
counts, not the lot, so `"Arrows (quiver of 20)"` is `"arrow"`, and a full quiver reads "20 arrows".
It's lowercase unless a word is a proper noun or an abbreviation, and it has no article.
`PlayerView.item_names` gives it to the players' client.

A template you write that leaves it out gets its `name`.

display_name_plural.title: Display Name Plural
display_name_plural.description:
What to call two or more units, like `"arrows"` or `"crossbow bolts"`.

`PlayerView.item_names_plural` gives it to the players' client. A
template you write that leaves it out gets `display_name` with the regular English ending on the word that names the
item: the last word before the first `of`, `with`, or `vs`, a comma, a bonus like `+1`, a closing Roman numeral, or
an opening parenthesis, or the last word when the name has none of them. So `"Idol of the drowned saint"` becomes
`"Idols of the drowned saint"`, and `"Lantern (hooded)"` becomes `"Lanterns (hooded)"`. The ending is `s`, or `es`
after `s`, `x`, `z`, `ch`, or `sh`, or `ies` in place of a `y` that follows a consonant, and `staff` becomes
`staves` with its capital kept, so `"Staff of the Magi"` becomes `"Staves of the Magi"`. The connecting words count
in any case, so `"Staff Of Power"` becomes `"Staves Of Power"`, and any spaces after the word stay after the ending.
The compiled plural of every built-in template follows the same rule. Set it yourself when the name is already
plural, like `"Torches (6)"`, or when the plural is irregular.

cost_gp.title: Cost Gp
cost_gp.description: The listed price in gold pieces, for one lot. 0 for sling stones.

lot_size.title: Lot Size
lot_size.description: How many units one purchase delivers, for example 20 arrows.

weight_coins.title: Weight Coins
weight_coins.description:
The weight in coins for one unit. 0 on every compiled template. Ammunition you bundle with an adventure can set a
weight, and `equipment_weight_coins` counts it per unit.

material.description:
What the ammunition is made of, for monsters that only silver or magic can hurt. See
`Material`.

overrides_applied.title: Overrides Applied
overrides_applied.description:
Which fields were corrected when this row was compiled from the SRD text, as dotted paths. Empty when none were.
osrlib doesn't read it during play.

AmmunitionTemplate.title: AmmunitionTemplate
AmmunitionTemplate.description:
Ammunition for a missile weapon: arrows, quarrels, sling stones.

Bought like gear, in lots: one purchase at the listed price delivers `lot_size`
units. Compiled ammunition weighs nothing, because the SRD counts the weight of the
ammunition and its container in the missile weapon's listed weight and gives the
ammunition table no weight column. Ammunition can't be equipped: wield the bow, and
the arrows stay in the item list. Sling stones are free, so their compiled cost is 0.

pattern_type.title: Pattern Type
pattern_type.description:
The discriminator value, `area_entered`. It appears in the document, and you
never set it yourself.

dungeon_id.title: Dungeon Id
dungeon_id.description: The id of the dungeon the area belongs to.

level_number.title: Level Number
level_number.description: The 1-based number of the level the area belongs to.

area_id.title: Area Id
area_id.description:
The id of the area, from its `AreaSpec` on that
level.

AreaEnteredPattern.title: AreaEnteredPattern
AreaEnteredPattern.description:
A pattern that matches the party entering a keyed area.

It matches a `LocationEnteredEvent` for
an area. An area id is unique only within its level, so the pattern includes the dungeon,
the level, and the area. Use
`LevelEnteredPattern` to react to the party
arriving anywhere on a level.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The area's id, unique within the level. Events contain it, triggers match on it, and the
overlay stores the state of the area's encounter, treasure, and trap under it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The room's name, to show the player, like `"Guard post"` or `"The abbot's cell"`.

description.title: Description
description.description:
Text to show when the party walks in. Events contain the area's id, not its text, so look the
text up here.

cells.title: Cells
cells.description:
The cells the area covers, at least one. They don't have to touch each other, though a room's
cells usually do. Every cell has to be on the level's grid. The first cell is where the session
puts the encounter's lair hoard. A cell that two areas list belongs to the one listed first in
the level's `areas`. Each area needs at least one cell that no earlier area lists, or the party
can never enter it, and `validate_adventure` reports
an area without one.

encounter.description:
The monsters waiting in the room, or `null` for a room without any. See
`KeyedEncounter`.

features.title: Features
features.description:
The keyed things in the room: treasure caches, construction tricks, and custom features. A
feature here can leave its `cell` unset, and then the party can reach it from any cell of the
area.

trap.description:
A trap over the whole area, or `null`. It has to be a room trap. It can spring when the party
moves into a cell of the area, or, with `trigger="open"`, when the party opens a door on the
edge of one of the area's cells.

treasure.description:
Treasure the session rolls the first time the party enters, for a room with treasure and no
monster guarding it, or `null`. For a room whose treasure belongs to its monsters, use the
encounter's `hoard` flag instead.

AreaSpec.title: AreaSpec
AreaSpec.description:
A keyed room or cave: a named group of cells with content bound to it.

Areas are how you key a dungeon, the way a printed adventure numbers its rooms. Each area covers
some cells of a `LevelSpec`, and a cell outside every area is
corridor. When the party moves into a cell of the area, the session rolls the area's treasure,
rolls for a trap that springs on entering, and spawns the encounter, in that order. Showing the
area's description is up to you.

letters.title: Letters
letters.description:
One or more B/X treasure type letters, like `("C",)`. The session rolls each letter's table
and puts the results in one cache. The letters are `A` to `V`. See
[the treasure type index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/treasure-types/),
or read the `letter` of each entry in the `treasure_types` of
`load_treasure_tables()`.
`validate_adventure` reports any other letter. Set
this or `unguarded`, not both.

unguarded.title: Unguarded
unguarded.description:
Whether to roll on the OSE SRD's table for unguarded treasure instead of listing letters. The
table has a row for each band of dungeon levels, and the session uses the row for the number of
the level the area is on, so the treasure is bigger on deeper levels. Set this or `letters`, not
both.

AreaTreasureSpec.title: AreaTreasureSpec
AreaTreasureSpec.description:
Treasure the session rolls for an area, with no monster guarding it.

Put one on an `AreaSpec` when you want the room to contain treasure
but don't want to choose it. The session rolls it the first time the party enters the area, and
puts the result on the cell where the party entered, as a
`GeneratedCache`. The party takes it with
`TakeTreasure`. If the roll comes up empty, the session
puts nothing down. Rolled treasure is never trapped. To trap treasure, write a
`FeatureSpec` with a trap.

When the treasure belongs to the monsters in the room, use the `hoard` flag of the area's
`KeyedEncounter` instead. The session then rolls the
monsters' lair treasure.

ArmourCategory.title: ArmourCategory
ArmourCategory.description:
How bulky a suit of body armour is, for the basic encumbrance rates.

Under basic encumbrance, a character's movement rate depends on the armour they wear
rather than on the weight they carry.
`movement_rate_feet` reads the category of the
armour in the worn slot to pick the rate. No member stands for wearing nothing: an empty
worn slot means the unarmoured rate. The shield has no category. A character in
enchanted armour moves at the rate of the mundane armour it's made from, because
enchantment halves a suit's weight without making it less bulky.

The values `"light"` and `"heavy"` appear in the compiled equipment data.

kind.description: Which armour the class may wear. See `ArmourPolicyKind`.

shields_allowed.title: Shields Allowed
shields_allowed.description: Whether the class may use a shield. It must be False when `kind` is `"none"`.

ArmourPolicy.title: ArmourPolicy
ArmourPolicy.description:
Which armour and shields a class may use.

Read it from `ClassDefinition.armour`.
`validate_equip` checks a character's armour and shield
against it. Among the built-in classes, the magic-user wears no armour, the thief wears leather
only, and the other classes may wear any armour. Frozen.

ArmourPolicyKind.title: ArmourPolicyKind
ArmourPolicyKind.description:
Which armour a class may wear.

Read it from `ArmourPolicy.kind`.
`validate_equip` checks it when a character puts armour
on. The values are the strings `"any"`, `"leather_only"`, and `"none"`.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The catalog id, for example `"plate_mail"`. Get every id from
`load_equipment`, or see [the equipment id
index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/equipment/).

name.title: Name
name.description: The display name.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description:
What to call one of these in a sentence, like `"shield"` or `"suit of chainmail"`.

Body armour is named as a suit, so a count reads "2 suits of chainmail". It's lowercase unless a
word is a proper noun or an abbreviation, and it has no article, so put a number or an article in
front of it. `PlayerView.item_names` gives it to the players' client.

A template you write that leaves it out gets its `name`.

display_name_plural.title: Display Name Plural
display_name_plural.description:
What to call two or more of these, like `"shields"` or `"suits of chainmail"`.

`PlayerView.item_names_plural` gives it to the players' client. A
template you write that leaves it out gets `display_name` with the regular English ending on the word that names the
item: the last word before the first `of`, `with`, or `vs`, a comma, a bonus like `+1`, a closing Roman numeral, or
an opening parenthesis, or the last word when the name has none of them. So `"Idol of the drowned saint"` becomes
`"Idols of the drowned saint"`, and `"Lantern (hooded)"` becomes `"Lanterns (hooded)"`. The ending is `s`, or `es`
after `s`, `x`, `z`, `ch`, or `sh`, or `ies` in place of a `y` that follows a consonant, and `staff` becomes
`staves` with its capital kept, so `"Staff of the Magi"` becomes `"Staves of the Magi"`. The connecting words count
in any case, so `"Staff Of Power"` becomes `"Staves Of Power"`, and any spaces after the word stay after the ending.
The compiled plural of every built-in template follows the same rule. Set it yourself when the name is already
plural, like `"Torches (6)"`, or when the plural is irregular.

cost_gp.title: Cost Gp
cost_gp.description: The listed price in gold pieces.

weight_coins.title: Weight Coins
weight_coins.description: The weight in coins. Enchanted armour weighs half this.

ac.title: Ac
ac.description: Body armour's armour class on the descending scale. `null` on the shield.

ac_ascending.title: Ac Ascending
ac_ascending.description: The same protection on the ascending scale. `null` on the shield.

ac_bonus.title: Ac Bonus
ac_bonus.description:
The shield's bonus to armour class, 1 on the compiled shield. It lowers descending AC and raises ascending AC
by that much. `null` on body armour.

category.description:
How bulky the suit is, for the basic encumbrance movement rates. See
`ArmourCategory`. `null` on the shield.

overrides_applied.title: Overrides Applied
overrides_applied.description:
Which fields were corrected when this row was compiled from the SRD text, as dotted paths. Empty when none were.
osrlib doesn't read it during play.

ArmourTemplate.title: ArmourTemplate
ArmourTemplate.description:
A suit of body armour or the shield, from the SRD's armour table.

Body armour sets a wearer's armour class outright and a shield adds a bonus to it, so
one of the two field groups is filled and the other is empty: body armour has `ac`,
`ac_ascending`, and `category`, while the shield has `ac_bonus` alone. Use
`is_shield` to tell which kind you have
instead of testing the fields. Get one from
`EquipmentCatalog.get`, buy it with
`purchase`, and put it on with
`equip`, which routes body armour to the worn slot and the
shield to the shield slot.

Both armour class formats are here because the tabletop rules print both: the
descending scale, where lower is better and unarmoured is 9, and the ascending scale in
brackets, where higher is better and unarmoured is 10. You choose which one to show
players. The rules give the same result either way.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: The rows, weakest attacker first. Each row's THAC0 is lower than the row before it.

AttackMatrix.title: AttackMatrix
AttackMatrix.description:
The SRD's attack matrix: the roll each kind of attacker needs against each armour class.

Read it from `CombatTables.attack_matrix`
to display the table. To find a roll, call `to_hit_ac`,
which gives the same result for any THAC0 and any armour class.

hd_label.title: Hd Label
hd_label.description:
The attacker the row is for, as the SRD labels it: `"NH"` for a normal human, then ranges of Hit Dice like
`"1+ to 2"`.

thac0.title: Thac0
thac0.description: The roll this attacker needs to hit armour class 0. Every cell in `by_ac` is computed from it.

attack_bonus.title: Attack Bonus
attack_bonus.description: The attacker's bonus for ascending armour class, which is 19 minus `thac0`.

by_ac.title: By Ac
by_ac.description:
The roll needed against each descending armour class from −3 to 9, keyed by armour class, as printed.

Every value is `thac0` minus the armour class, limited to 2 to 20.

AttackMatrixRow.title: AttackMatrixRow
AttackMatrixRow.description:
One row of the attack matrix: the roll one kind of attacker needs against each armour class.

Read the rows to display the matrix. To find the roll an attacker needs, call
`to_hit_ac` instead, which works for any armour class,
not only the printed ones.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: attack rolls happen in the open.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

attacker_id.title: Attacker Id
attacker_id.description: The entity id of whoever attacked.

defender_id.title: Defender Id
defender_id.description: The entity id of whoever was attacked.

attack_name.title: Attack Name
attack_name.description:
The name of what the attacker used: a weapon, a gear item, a magic item, or a monster's attack. It's
`"unarmed"` for an unarmed attack, and `"improvised"` for an attack with a gear item's combat stats alone. In a
session, an NPC adventurer's unidentified magic weapon is named by the mundane weapon underneath, such as
`"Sword"`, because the players never identify an NPC's items.

roll.title: Roll
roll.description: The d20 as it landed, before modifiers. `null` on an automatic hit.

modifier.title: Modifier
modifier.description:
The sum of everything added to the roll, like STR, range, magic, spells, and your situational modifier. It
can be negative.

total.title: Total
total.description: The roll plus the modifier, which is the number compared with `required`. `null` on an automatic hit.

required.title: Required
required.description:
The total the attacker needed to hit, from its THAC0 and the defender's armour class. `null` on an
automatic hit.

defender_ac.title: Defender Ac
defender_ac.description:
The defender's armour class as the roll used it, after its shield, spells, and the situation. `null` on
an automatic hit.

natural.title: Natural
natural.description:
1 or 20 when the d20 alone decided the outcome, and `null` otherwise.

A natural 20 always hits and a natural 1 always misses. This field is set only when that rule changed the
outcome: a 20 whose total was below `required`, or a 1 whose total reached it.

back_stab.title: Back Stab
back_stab.description:
True when the attack was a thief's back-stab, so your game can say so.

`attack_roll` sets it when the attack's
`AttackContext` sets both `behind_target` and `target_unaware`, and the
attacker's class has the `back_stab` ability. The back-stab's bonus to hit is part of `modifier`, and the damage
that follows is doubled. It's true on an automatic hit too, because the damage still doubles. A
`GameSession` makes that attack for a member who declares
`BattleDeclaration.back_stab`.

AttackRolledEvent.title: AttackRolledEvent
AttackRolledEvent.description:
One attack roll and everything that went into it.

`attack_roll` reports one of these for every attack, and
`resolve_attack` reports it before the damage that follows. Read `code`
for the outcome, and the number fields to show the arithmetic.

An automatic hit has no roll. A melee attack hits a paralysed, sleeping, or petrified defender automatically, and
any attack hits a monster with no armour class, like green slime. On an automatic hit, `roll`, `total`,
`required`, and `defender_ac` are `null`.

attacks.title: Attacks
attacks.description: The attacks the routine makes, at least one. See `MonsterAttack`.

use.description:
When the monster uses this routine. See `RoutineUse`.

The first routine of a template is `PRIMARY`. In the built-in catalog, every later routine has
one of the other values, taken from the OSE SRD's text for that monster. In a template of your
own, set `use` on each later routine. A routine you leave unset is `PRIMARY` too, so the default
policy picks it as often as the first.

AttackRoutine.title: AttackRoutine
AttackRoutine.description:
One set of attacks a monster can make in a round, chosen as a whole.

Read them from `MonsterTemplate.attacks`. Most
creatures have one. A creature with more than one uses one of them in a round, not all of them:
a dragon either claws and bites or breathes. Each attack in the routine is a
`MonsterAttack`. The routine's `use` says when the OSE SRD
lets the monster use it. In battle, an `ActionPolicy` picks
one each round. The model is frozen (immutable).

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"award_xp"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
The member who receives the experience, by
`MemberView.id`. A command you issue yourself has a
member id here, and the session refuses any other value with `session.command.unknown_member`.
A consequence or a reward in an adventure document has a party selector instead,
`"@party"` for every living member or `"@first"` for the first living member, because the
session assigns member ids when it starts. The trigger and quest interpreter replaces the selector
with member ids before it issues the command.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description:
The award before the class's prime-requisite adjustment. B/X grants at most one level
per award. XP that would raise the character two levels stops one point short of the
second level, and the rest is lost. Send another award to raise the character further.

AwardXP.title: AwardXP
AwardXP.description:
Referee: give one character experience points, apart from the XP the session awards.

Use it for a quest reward or for any other XP you grant. This command is legal in
every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included, so you can grant an adventure's rewards after the
session has ended. The class's prime-requisite bonus or penalty applies to the award,
and the award can raise the character a level.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.unknown_member` - `character_id` matches no party member.

**Events:**

`XpAwardedEvent` with the award, the
adjusted award, and the level after. When the award reaches the next level, a
`CharacterLeveledUpEvent`
follows with the levels, the hit points gained, and the new title.

declaration.description:
The declaration to judge, complete except for its target.

Leave the field that `target_field` names at its default: `target_group_id` at `null`, or
`targets` empty. Its `character_id` names the member, who has to be in
`EncounterView.declarers`. The member doesn't need
a declaration in the plan. When they have one, the candidate takes its place.

The field that `target_field` doesn't name keeps the value you give it, and the session judges
the declaration with both. So a `cast` candidate with `target_field="targets"` whose
declaration also sets `target_group_id` is judged with both set, as the same declaration in the
plan would be.

target_field.title: Target Field
target_field.description:
Which field of the declaration each target id goes in. With `"target_group_id"`, the id is
the declaration's `target_group_id`. With `"targets"`, the declaration's `targets` contains
only that id.

target_ids.title: Target Ids
target_ids.description:
The ids to judge the declaration at, with no id repeated: group ids from
`EncounterView.groups`, or the ids of members,
monsters, or NPCs from the player view.

An id that names nothing gets the rejection the session would give the same declaration in the
plan, such as `battle.declaration.unknown_group`. An empty tuple is allowed, and its judgement
has no entries.

BattleCandidate.title: BattleCandidate
BattleCandidate.description:
One action a member could declare, to be judged at each of several targets before the player picks one.

Pass these to `preview_battle_round` in `candidates` to
learn which targets each action on a battle screen's menu reaches, in one call. The preview judges
the candidate once for each id in `target_ids`, with that id set in `target_field`, and returns a
`BattleCandidateJudgement` for it. You list the
candidates from the player view, and the session decides whether each one works, so the answers
reveal nothing the view masks.

Build one candidate for each choice on the menu:

- A melee attack is an `attack` with `weapon_id`, at group ids in `target_group_id`.
- A close and attack is the same `attack` with `move="close"`.
- Each missile weapon the member wields is an `attack` of its own with that `weapon_id`.
- A spell is a `cast` with `spell_id`, `spell_mode`, and `reversed`. Use `target_group_id` for a
  spell aimed at a group, and `targets` for one aimed at a member, a monster, or an NPC.
- A potion given to another member, or a touch with an item such as a staff of healing, is a
  `use_item` with `item_id`, at member ids in `targets`.
- Handing over an item is a `give_item` with `item_id`, at member ids in `targets`.

Name `weapon_id` in every `attack` candidate. When you leave it out, the session picks the
weapon at the member's projected distance to each group, so an accepted answer doesn't say
which weapon it judged. The judgement's `attack_kinds` still says whether that attack is a
melee or a missile attack.

A `fighting_withdrawal` or a `retreat` can't be a candidate, because it takes no target and can
turn the plan into a formation move. Judge one as a planned declaration in `declarations`
instead.

The model is frozen.

candidate.description: The candidate, as you passed it.

rejections.title: Rejections
rejections.description:
Every reason the session would refuse the candidate at each target, keyed by target id.

There's one entry for each id in the candidate's `target_ids`, in that order. An empty tuple
means the session would accept that declaration. Each tuple is exactly what
`BattleRoundPreview.rejections` would hold
for the member if you previewed the plan with their declaration replaced by
`candidate.declaration_for(target_id)`. It has the same codes and params, and every rejection has
the member's id as its `character` param. A rejection that doesn't depend on the target, such as
`battle.declaration.weapon_not_wielded`, appears under every target.

attack_kinds.title: Attack Kinds
attack_kinds.description:
Whether an `attack` candidate would be a melee or a missile attack at each target, keyed by
target id, in the order of `target_ids`.

It's the decision the session makes when it accepts the round, at the same projected distance
the rejections are judged at. A weapon with only the `missile` quality, such as a bow, always
makes a missile attack, and one with only the `melee` quality, such as a sword, always makes a
melee attack. A weapon with both, such as a dagger, makes a melee attack within 5' of the group
and a missile attack beyond. So a close and attack with a dagger that stops short of the group
is a missile attack: the member closes part way, then throws. With no `weapon_id`, it's the kind
of attack the session makes with the weapon it picks.

A target has an entry when the session's checks get as far as that decision. Every target the
session would accept has one. A target refused by a check that comes after the decision has
one too. Examples are a refusal for reach, for the front rank, for range, or for ammunition,
`battle.declaration.back_stab_not_melee` with a `"missile"` entry, and
`battle.declaration.no_mirror`. A target has no entry when the session refuses the attack before it
decides, because the group is unknown or has fled, the group has no monster to strike, the
weapon isn't wielded or can't attack, the member can't move for a close, or a check of
`back_stab` or `move` that comes before the group check refuses it. A candidate that isn't an
`attack` has no entries.

The decision can change when the monsters act first. A group that moves before the attack
comes up changes the distance. So a dagger judged as a throw can resolve as a melee attack, and
a dagger judged as a melee attack can resolve as a throw. A melee attack that closes from
beyond 5' into reach stays a melee attack wherever the member ends up. An attack with a weapon
that has only the `missile` quality, such as a bow, stays a missile attack after a close, even
one that takes the member within 5'.

A judgement without `attack_kinds` parses with it empty.

BattleCandidateJudgement.title: BattleCandidateJudgement
BattleCandidateJudgement.description:
The session's answer for one `BattleCandidate` at each of its targets.

`BattleRoundPreview.candidates` holds one for
each candidate you passed to `preview_battle_round`.
Read `rejections` to enable or disable each target of the action, and show the rejection codes
as the reason a target is disabled. Read `attack_kinds` to label an attack by how the member
would make it. The model is frozen.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
Whose declaration this is, by
`MemberView.id`. It has to be one of the ids in
`EncounterView.declarers`, and each of those
members needs a separate declaration in the same round.

action.title: Action
action.description:
What this member does. `attack` strikes or shoots at a group, after a `close` when the
declaration sets one, `cast` casts a spell, `turn_undead` presents a holy symbol, `move` moves
the member toward the monsters or away from them, `use_item` uses a magic item or throws an
item, `give_item` hands an item to another member, `hide` has a thief try to hide in shadows,
and `hold` does nothing. This field determines which other fields apply, and `hide` and `hold`
need none of them.

A `hide` is open to a member whose class has thief skills, as the thief's does, and who doesn't
stand in the party's front rank: the first row of the ranks toward any group that hasn't fled
and has a living member. The session judges that where the members will stand once the round's
declared moves are made, as it judges a melee attack. It refuses a `hide` by a member whose
class has no thief skills with `battle.declaration.hide_not_a_thief`, and a `hide` from the
front rank with `battle.declaration.hide_in_front_rank`, in that order, after the back-stab
checks and the check of `move`. Each has the member's id as its `character` param.

The hide resolves in the party's movement step, after the members' moves, in marching order
whatever order the declarations came in. A member who can't act or is confused when the step
comes doesn't hide, and the session draws nothing for them. Otherwise the session rolls the
member's hide in shadows skill, which only the referee sees, in a
`DetectionRolledEvent` of kind `"hide_in_shadows"`.
This roll, and the move silently roll of a back-stab from hiding, draw from the combat stream,
`COMBAT_STREAM`, with the rest of the round's resolution, so
a battle replays from its own streams. A session's thief checks outside a battle, like
`PickLock`, draw from the exploration stream instead. The
players see a
`HideAttemptedEvent`, which doesn't say whether the
roll passed. The member is then hiding, as
`EncounterView.hiding` shows, until the attempt ends.
A `hide` by a member who is already hiding replaces the attempt with a new roll, and a member
can hide again in a later round after an attempt has ended.

Hiding is a battle declaration only. A thief can't enter a battle already hiding, because
nothing outside a battle makes a member hide, and every battle starts with nobody hiding. The
back-stab in the party's free round after it surprises the monsters needs no `hide`.

target_group_id.title: Target Group Id
target_group_id.description:
Which monster group the action is aimed at, by
`EncounterGroupView.id` from
`EncounterView.groups`.

These declarations need it: an `attack`, a `close`, a thrown item, a wand, staff, or rod
that strikes or covers an area, and a `cast` of a spell whose area covers creatures. A use of
the staff of power or wizardry without it is one of the staff's other powers, not a strike. An area
spell aimed at a group isn't placed at a point, because the range track has no positions
inside a group. It covers the group's living members in the order they were spawned, as many
as its size and the party's rank width allow.

Some spell modes affect a total number of Hit Dice, like *sleep*'s. Their targeting mode is
`hd_budget`. A `cast` in such a mode can set either this field or `targets`. With this field,
the session collects the group's living members in spawn order. When the mode also has an
area, like *death spell*'s 60' cube, it collects only the members inside the area, as for any
area spell. The spell then spends its Hit Dice budget on the members it collected, fewest Hit
Dice first.

The session refuses a group that isn't in the encounter, or one whose
`EncounterGroupView.fled` is true, with
`battle.declaration.unknown_group`.

weapon_id.title: Weapon Id
weapon_id.description:
Which wielded weapon to attack with, or `null` to have the session choose one.

Name a mundane weapon by its catalog id, or a magic weapon by its per-instance id. The weapon
has to be equipped already, so equip it with `EquipItem`
before the fight. The session refuses a weapon that's only carried with
`battle.declaration.weapon_not_wielded`, and a wielded magic item with no weapon stats, like a
wand, with `battle.declaration.item_unusable`. Every magic staff is a staff, so a member who
wields one can attack with it. Whether the attack is melee or missile depends on the
weapon's qualities and the group's distance.

With `null`, the member attacks with the wielded weapon that suits the attack. The member's
distance to the group decides the attack: melee at 5' or less, and missile beyond 5'. It's the
distance when the session accepts the round, after the member's own `close` when the
declaration sets one. So a member who closes into reach with a dagger strikes with it, and a
member who stays 20' away throws it. The session chooses the weapon this way:

- It looks through the member's wielded items in the order they were equipped. It takes the
  first one with the `melee` quality for a melee attack, or the `missile` quality for a
  missile attack.
- A real weapon comes before an improvised one, whatever order they were equipped in. An
  improvised weapon is a gear item, like a torch, that has the `melee` quality. So a member
  who lit a torch and then drew a sword swings the sword. The torch counts only when nothing
  else suits the attack.
- For a missile attack, it takes the first weapon whose long range reaches the group. When
  none reaches, it takes the first missile weapon, and the session refuses the round with
  `combat.attack.out_of_range` before any of it resolves.
- A splash weapon, like a flask of oil or a vial of holy water, never counts, because a
  `use_item` declaration throws it. A wand, or another magic item with no base weapon, has
  no weapon stats, so it never counts either.
- A member with no weapon that suits the attack strikes unarmed.

The session makes this choice once, when it accepts the round. The attack resolves with that
weapon even when the distance changes before the attack resolves. The attack's
`AttackRolledEvent` reports the choice in
`attack_name`: the weapon's name, `"improvised"` for a gear item like a torch, or
`"unarmed"`.

spell_id.title: Spell Id
spell_id.description:
Which spell a `cast` declaration casts, by its id in
`GameSession.effective_spells`: a
built-in spell (see the
[spell id index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/spells/)) or one
the adventure bundles. For a `use_item` that reads a scroll, it's which spell to read off the
scroll, and `null` reads the first one left. The session refuses a `cast` with no spell named
with `battle.declaration.missing_spell`.

spell_mode.title: Spell Mode
spell_mode.description:
Which of the spell's usages to cast, by that usage's
`SpellMode.key`. A `cast` declaration has to name one, or
the session refuses it with `battle.declaration.missing_spell`. A scroll read can leave it `null` to
take the spell's first usage.

reversed.title: Reversed
reversed.description:
Cast the reversed form of the spell, on the same terms as
`CastSpell.reversed`: an arcane caster needs a
reversed copy memorized, and a divine caster chooses the form here.

targets.title: Targets
targets.description:
The spell or scroll's targets: party member ids from
`PlayerView.party`, enemy ids from
`EncounterGroupView.members`, or, for a
spell that affects a place, a cell reference like
`cell:crypt:1:3,4` that `cell_ref` builds. Leave it empty
for a spell whose area covers creatures, which takes `target_group_id` instead.

An enemy must be a living monster or NPC in a current encounter group that hasn't fled.
An unknown id, an enemy outside the current groups, a dead enemy, or an enemy in a fled
group gets `magic.cast.unknown_target`, whose `target` param is the id you supplied.
Refresh the player view and choose an `"alive"` member. A running group remains targetable
until it leaves. A refused round changes no state, draws no randomness, and spends no time.
A cell reference has to name a cell of the level the party stands on, or the session refuses
it with `magic.cast.unknown_target`, as it does a reference that doesn't parse. Party member
and cell targets otherwise retain the spell mode's existing checks.

For a mode that affects a total number of Hit Dice (`hd_budget`), you can leave this empty
and set `target_group_id` instead. The session then collects the targets from the group, as
`target_group_id` describes. When
you set both fields, the session uses this one.

The session refuses an invisible target with `battle.declaration.invisible_target`. It checks
a spell's range against the distance from the caster to each target: to the group of a
targeted monster, or to a targeted member, where that member stands once the round's moves
are made. A touch spell, like *cure light wounds*, reaches 5', so the session refuses it at a
member who moves away from the caster this round with `magic.cast.out_of_range`. A touch
spell on a monster follows the rule for melee, because the OSE SRD's touch needs a melee
attack roll. The caster has to stand in the party's front rank toward the monster's group, or
the session refuses the cast with `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank`. The monster has to
be one of its group's first living monsters, as many as
`EncounterView.formation_width`, or the
session refuses the cast with `combat.attack.out_of_reach`, whose `target` param is the
monster's id.

Three other declarations read one id from this field. The session refuses a declaration of
one of them with any other number of ids with `battle.declaration.target_count`, whose
`expected` param is 1 and whose `supplied` param is the number of ids you gave. A potion
and a staff of healing take an empty field as the member who uses them, and a `give_item`
needs exactly one id.

- For a `use_item` of a potion, it's the id of the member who drinks it. Leave it empty, or
  give the carrier's id, and the carrier drinks. The session refuses an id that isn't a party
  member's with `items.use.target_not_allowed`, a member who is dead or turned to
  stone with `items.use.target_cannot_drink`, and a member out of reach with
  `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach`. A member who is asleep or paralysed can be given
  a potion to drink.
- For a `use_item` of a staff of healing, it's the id of the creature the staff touches.
  Leave it empty, and the member using it is healed. The session refuses an id that matches no
  creature with `items.use.unknown_target`, a creature that's dead or turned to stone with
  `items.use.target_cannot_be_healed`, another creature that's invisible with
  `items.use.invisible_target`, a creature the staff already healed today with
  `items.use.target_healed_today`, and another member out of reach with
  `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach`. A monster's group has to stand within 5' of the
  member, or the use gets `combat.attack.out_of_reach`. A touch on a monster then follows the
  rule for melee, as a touch spell's does.
- For a `give_item`, it's the id of the member who takes the item. The session refuses the giver with
  `exploration.give.same_member`, an id that isn't a party member's with
  `session.command.unknown_member`, a member who can't act with
  `session.command.member_incapacitated`, and a member out of reach with
  `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach`.

`battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach` and `battle.declaration.target_count` have the
declaring member's id as their `character` param. The first has the named member's id as
`target`, and so do a `give_item`'s `session.command.unknown_member` and
`session.command.member_incapacitated`.

move.title: Move
move.description:
Which movement this member makes this round, with a `move` action or, for `close` only, with an
`attack`.

A battle measures distance on the range track. Each group stands at a distance from the party
line, where the party stood when the encounter opened. Each member stands at an advance forward
of that line, in `EncounterView.advance_feet`,
and starts the battle on it. A member's distance to a group is the group's distance minus their
advance. A member moves at their own encounter movement rate,
`MemberView.encounter_rate_feet`: a third of
their movement rate after encumbrance, doubled by *haste* on that member.

`close` moves this member toward `target_group_id` at their rate, and nobody else. The member
stops 5' from that group, and stops sooner rather than come within 5' of another group that's
still in the fight. A member already within 5' of the group doesn't move.

- With a `move` action, the member only moves.
- With an `attack`, the member moves in the party's movement step and attacks in the missile
  or the melee step of the same round. The session judges the attack as if the move had
  already happened. The member's distance after the move decides whether it's a melee or a
  missile attack, and a melee attack needs the member to be within 5' of the group and in its
  front rank after every move the round declares. A member who can't get that close this round
  gets `combat.attack.out_of_reach`, with that distance as `distance_feet`, and a member who
  gets close but finds no place left in the front rank gets
  `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank`.

The monsters can act before the party, and the party's missiles and spells come before its
melee. A melee attack resolves only if, at the party's melee step, the group still has a living
monster the member can see, and the member stands in the group's front rank within 5' of it.
A group that has started to flee is the one exception to the position check. A member who stood
within 5' of it when the round was accepted still gets the attack, with the bonus against a
retreating combatant, unless the group runs out of the battle. Otherwise the member makes no
attack, and the session reports a
`DeclarationFizzledEvent` at
`battle.melee.fizzled`, with the group's id as `group_id`. Its `reason` is one of these:

- `battle.declaration.no_target` when the group has no such monster left, for example
  because the party's archers or casters killed them earlier in the round. The session
  checks this first, so the member gets it whether or not they closed, and wherever they
  stand.
- `combat.attack.out_of_reach` when the member is farther than 5' from the group, or the
  group ran out of the battle.
- `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank` when the member is within 5' but not in its front
  rank.

`fighting_withdrawal` and `retreat` take a member away from the monsters, with a `move` action.
A `fighting_withdrawal` backs away at half the member's encounter rate, facing the monsters, and
a `retreat` turns and runs at the full rate. The member makes no attack that round. Each one is
either a formation move or a move the member makes alone:

- When every member in `declarers` declares the same one, it's a formation move: the whole
  party moves as one body. That includes a round with only one declarer. The party moves at the
  slowest living member's encounter rate, halved for a `fighting_withdrawal`. Every group's
  distance grows by that much, and no member's advance changes, so members who stand apart
  stay apart. A formation `retreat` ends the battle. If no monster can pursue the party, the
  party gets away and the encounter closes. Otherwise the session goes back to `encounter` mode
  with a pursuit, which `PursuitState` describes. The
  pursuit's starting gap is the smallest distance from any living member to any group that can
  follow, after the move. So a member who stood forward of the others starts the chase nearest
  the pursuers. Send
  `Wait` to run each round of it, or
  `EngageBattle` to turn and fight.
- Otherwise, the member moves back alone, and their advance goes down. It can go below zero,
  behind the line, because the way the party came is clear. When that leaves every member the
  monsters can see behind the line, the line moves back to the foremost of them at the end of
  the movement step. Every advance and every group's distance grow by the same amount, so no
  distance between a member and a group changes, as
  `BattleState.advance_feet` describes. Any
  member can fall back alone, wherever they stand, and nobody else moves. It doesn't end the
  battle, even when it's a `retreat`. Once the member has moved, the members who are now
  nearest each group form its front rank.

A member who retreats, alone or with the formation, is easier to hit for the whole round,
whichever side acts first. Attackers get +2 against them and ignore the retreating member's
shield.

The session refuses a `move` action with no `move` with `battle.declaration.missing_move`, a
`close` at a group that isn't in the encounter or has fled with
`battle.declaration.unknown_group`, and any move by a member in
`EncounterView.immobile` with
`battle.declaration.cannot_move`. An `attack` takes only `close`, and gets
`battle.declaration.move_not_combinable` with a `fighting_withdrawal` or a `retreat`. A `cast`
that sets any move gets `battle.declaration.cast_cannot_move`, because the OSE SRD says "The
spell caster cannot move and cast a spell in the same round". A `turn_undead`, a `use_item`, a
`give_item`, a `hide`, or a `hold` that sets any move gets `battle.declaration.move_not_combinable`. Each
of these two codes has the member's id as its `character` param. The session checks for them
after the back-stab checks and before the action's own checks.
[The adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/)
describes these rules in full.

replacement_id.title: Replacement Id
replacement_id.description:
A member to trade places with in the marching order, for a `fighting_withdrawal` or a
`retreat` this member makes alone, by `MemberView.id`.

Leave it `null` for every other declaration, a formation move included. A member who falls
back alone doesn't need to name anyone. Nobody else moves, and the members who are then nearest
each group form its front rank.

The trade changes only the marching order. It happens in the party's movement step, right
after the withdrawing member's move, and a
`MemberWithdrewEvent` reports it. Marching order
decides who stands in front among members at the same distance from a group who got there in
the same round. So when the withdrawing member steps out of a front rank, naming a member who
stands at the same distance brings that member to the front. The trade doesn't move the named
member. A member who stands farther back reaches the front rank only with a `close` of their
own. The new marching order stays after the battle.

The named member has to be in
`EncounterView.declarers`, can't be the
withdrawing member, can't be making a `fighting_withdrawal` or a `retreat` of their own, and
can't already be named by a withdrawing member earlier in marching order. Otherwise the session
refuses the declaration with `battle.declaration.replacement_unavailable`, with the withdrawing
member's id as the `character` param and the named id as `replacement`. A declaration in a
formation move that sets this field gets the same code, because every member is moving.

The trade happens only when the withdrawing member's move happens, and only while both members
are alive. A withdrawing member who can no longer move when the movement step comes stays where
they are, and the two keep their places in the marching order.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description:
Which item a `use_item` declaration uses: a magic item's per-instance id for a potion, a
scroll, a wand, a staff, or a rod, or a mundane item's catalog id for a splash weapon thrown
at a group, like a flask of oil or a vial of holy water. The session refuses any other
mundane item, like a torch or a rope, an item the member doesn't carry, or a magic item that
can't be used in battle, with `battle.declaration.item_unusable`. It judges the item before
the group, so a declaration with no `target_group_id` and an item the member can't throw
gets this code, not `battle.declaration.unknown_group`. To swing a torch, wield it and
declare an `attack`.

For a `give_item` declaration, it's the item to hand over, named as in
`GiveItems.item_ids`: a mundane item's catalog id,
which hands over one unit of the stack, or a per-instance id for a magic item, a gem, or a piece
of jewellery. The session refuses an item the giver doesn't carry, or no item, with
`exploration.item.not_carried`, and a magic item whose curse has been revealed with
`items.curse.stuck`.

gaze_defense.title: Gaze Defense
gaze_defense.description:
How this member guards against a petrifying gaze this round, or `null` for no guard.

A petrifying gaze, like a basilisk's or a medusa's, reaches each member who stands in the
gazer's group's `front_rank`, within 5' of
it, once a round. The session rolls a saving throw
versus paralysis for each member it reaches, with no declaration needed. A member who fails
turns to stone. The OSE SRD's basilisk entry says "Unless averting eyes or using
a mirror, characters in melee are affected each round". This field picks one of those two
guards:

- `avert_eyes`: the gaze passes the member by, and the session gives them the
  `averted_eyes` condition for the round. The basilisk's and the medusa's entries set the
  cost: "-4 penalty to-hit; the basilisk gains a +2 bonus to attack". Every attack roll the
  member makes this round takes −4, whatever it's aimed at. Each attack a gazing monster
  makes on the member this round gains +2. Other monsters' attacks gain nothing, because
  the OSE SRD gives the bonus only to the gazer.
- `mirror`: the member fights by watching a mirror, and the gaze passes them by. The
  basilisk's entry says "The reflection of a basilisk is harmless. Fighting by looking in a
  mirror incurs a -1 penalty to attack." Every attack roll the member makes this round takes
  −1, whatever it's aimed at, and no monster gains a bonus. The member has to carry a
  `mirror` from the equipment catalog, or the session refuses the declaration with
  `battle.declaration.no_mirror`. The OSE SRD also says that a gazer that sees its own
  reflection saves or turns to stone. osrlib doesn't apply that rule. If your game uses it,
  your game or the referee decides when it applies and resolves the gazer's save.

You can set a guard with any `action`. It lasts from when the session accepts the round
until the round ends. It makes no random roll and emits no event. The command log records it
with the declaration.

A member outside the gazer's group's front rank doesn't need a guard, because the gaze
doesn't reach them.
Neither does a member who can't act and so doesn't declare, because the gaze passes them by.

A basilisk that surprises the party turns its gaze on every member once as the encounter
opens, before the party can declare anything, as the OSE SRD's "Characters surprised by a
basilisk meet its gaze" says. No guard protects against that gaze.
[The adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/) describes the
gaze in full.

back_stab.title: Back Stab
back_stab.description:
Make this `attack` a back-stab, or leave it `false` for an ordinary attack.

The OSE SRD's thief entry says "When attacking an unaware opponent from behind, a thief
receives a +4 bonus to hit and doubles any damage dealt." osrlib has no facing in battle, so
the session reads an unaware opponent from behind in one of two ways: a monster the party
surprised, in the round it can't act, or a monster a hiding thief strikes unnoticed. Set this
field only when all of these are true:

- The action is `attack`.
- The member's class has the `back_stab` ability, as a thief's does.
- The monsters can't act this round because the party surprised them, or the member is
  hiding. The first is the party's free round, while
  `BattleState.monsters_hold_rounds`
  is above zero. The second holds while the member is in
  `EncounterView.hiding`. The session reads both
  when it accepts the round.
- The attack is a melee attack. The weapon and the member's distance to the group after their
  `close`, if the declaration sets one, decide that, as
  `weapon_id` describes.

You don't need to combine the second and third conditions yourself.
`EncounterView.can_back_stab` lists the members
who meet both this round, and
`BattleRoundPreview.can_back_stab` lists
them beside a planned round. The first and last conditions depend on the declaration, so check
them with `preview_battle_round`.

A thief can close on a group and back-stab in the same round: declare `attack` with
`move="close"` and `back_stab=True`. The session judges the back-stab at the distance the move
will reach. So a thief reaches a group up to their encounter rate plus 5' away. That's 35' for a
thief in leather armour under the ruleset's default `basic` encumbrance, and 45' for one in no
armour. *Haste* doubles the rate.

An accepted back-stab in the free round is always a back-stab. It hits the same monster an
ordinary melee attack would. It gets +4 to hit, the defender's shield doesn't count, and its
damage is doubled: the whole sum of the weapon's dice and the member's modifiers, not the dice
alone. The bonus and the doubling come from the class's `back_stab` ability. Every attack roll
the declaration makes in the round is a back-stab, even when the monsters win initiative, and
the attack's `AttackRolledEvent` has `back_stab` set to
true, so your game can say so.

A back-stab from hiding works differently, because the session rolls the thief's skills in
secret, as the OSE SRD's "The referee should roll for hear noise, hide in shadows and move
silently on the player’s behalf" says:

- A hiding member's back-stab doesn't need the group's front rank, so
  `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank` doesn't apply to it, when the session accepts the
  round or when the attack comes up. Every other melee check does, `combat.attack.out_of_reach`
  among them, so the group has to be within 5' of the member, or the declaration has to set
  `move="close"` to bring it within 5'. The attack hits the monster an ordinary melee attack
  would. Without a `close`, the member strikes from where they stand, and their place in the
  ranks doesn't change.
- A `close` on the back-stab is part of the approach. The member closes in the party's
  movement step with the round's other moves, the move doesn't end the attempt, and the move
  silently roll at the attack is the roll for that approach. After the attack the member stands
  where the close took them, as any member who closes does.
- When the attack comes up, before its first attack roll, the session rolls the member's move
  silently skill, which only the referee sees, in a
  `DetectionRolledEvent` of kind
  `"move_silently"`. It makes this roll for every such attack by a hiding member, whatever the
  hide in shadows roll was and whichever way the ruleset is set, so the draws are the same
  under both settings. An attack that fizzles makes no roll. A back-stab with a slow weapon,
  like a battle axe, comes up when its blow resolves, after both sides' blocks, so the session
  makes the roll then. The member is still hiding through the monsters' block before it, and the
  monsters pass over them there if their hide in shadows roll passed.
- The attack is a back-stab when the two rolls pass the test the ruleset's
  `back_stab_needs_both_skills`
  sets: both rolls by default, or either roll with the flag off. Then every attack roll the
  declaration makes is a back-stab, with the bonus and the doubling of the free round. Under
  *haste*, the declaration's two swings share the one move silently roll, made before the
  first, so both are back-stabs or neither is, as both are in the free round. Otherwise it's
  an ordinary melee attack. The attack's `AttackRolledEvent.back_stab` is how
  the players learn which.
- The attempt ends when the attack comes up, whatever happens.

A member stays hiding from the `hide` until the first of these:

- The member's next declaration other than `hold` or `hide` comes up in its step of the round.
  A `hold` keeps the attempt, so a thief can stay hidden for several rounds. A second `hide`
  replaces it with a new hide in shadows roll. An `attack` comes up in the missile or the melee
  step, not in the movement step, so a `close` on any attack, a back-stab or an ordinary one,
  doesn't end the attempt. An attack with a slow weapon, a back-stab or an ordinary one, comes
  up when its blow resolves after both sides' blocks, so the member is still hiding through the
  monsters' block before it, and passed over there if their hide in shadows roll passed.
- The member takes damage: a `DamageDealtEvent` on them
  with an `amount` above 0. One with an `amount` of 0 doesn't end the attempt, because the
  member took no damage.
- A monster or an NPC adventurer attacks the member, shoots at them, or casts a spell at them
  alone, when that action resolves.
- The member can't act, or is confused, at the end of a round.
- The battle ends.

A back-stab declared from hiding whose attempt ended before the attack came up, because the
member took damage or was attacked, stays a melee attack without the front rank check. It's an
ordinary attack, and the session makes no move silently roll for it.

While a member is hiding, the monsters' choice of targets reads only the hide in shadows roll,
under both settings. When the session or a built-in policy picks one member for a monster or
an NPC adventurer to attack, shoot at, cast at, or breathe on, it passes over a hiding member
whose hide in shadows roll passed while it could pick another member. That covers the built-in
policies, a confused monster's attack on the party, and a breath that hits one target. A member
turned to stone is never another member it could pick: the session passes over statues first,
as it does for any target, so when every other member in reach is stone, the hiding member is
the only one it could pick. When that member is the only one it could pick, the monster finds
them and attacks, which ends the attempt. A member
whose roll failed has been noticed, as the OSE SRD's "If a hide in shadows or move silently
roll fails, the referee knows that the thief has been noticed" says, and can be picked like
any other. A policy of your own reads
`BattleState.hiding` to do the same. Hiding changes only
the choice of a target. A group still closes on the nearest member it can see, a hiding member
included, and an area, like a red dragon's breath, covers a hiding member as it covers anyone in
its ranks.

The session refuses a back-stab with the first of these that applies, in this order. Each
of the four back-stab codes has the member's id as its `character` param.

1. `battle.declaration.back_stab_not_attack`: the action isn't `attack`. The session checks
   this before any other check on the declaration.
2. `battle.declaration.back_stab_no_ability`: the member's class has no `back_stab` ability.
3. `battle.declaration.back_stab_target_aware`: the monsters aren't surprised this round, and
   the member isn't hiding.
4. The checks of an ordinary attack on its group and weapon:
   `battle.declaration.unknown_group`, `battle.declaration.no_target`,
   `battle.declaration.weapon_not_wielded`, and `battle.declaration.item_unusable`.
5. `battle.declaration.back_stab_not_melee`: the attack the session would resolve is a
   missile attack. That's a missile weapon like a bow, or a weapon that's both melee and
   missile, like a dagger, aimed at a group more than 5' from the member after their
   `close`.
6. The rest of an ordinary melee attack's checks, like
   `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank` and `combat.attack.out_of_reach`, judged after the
   round's declared moves. A hiding member's back-stab skips `not_in_front_rank`.

A declaration that leaves this field `false` resolves exactly as it would without it. A hiding
member's attack without it is an ordinary attack with every check, the front rank's included,
and it ends the attempt.
[The adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/) describes the
back-stab in full.

BattleDeclaration.title: BattleDeclaration
BattleDeclaration.description:
One party member's declared action for a battle round.

You construct these yourself, one for each member who has to declare, and pass them all
in one `ResolveBattleRound`.
`EncounterView.declarers` lists the
members who have to declare this round. To offer only choices the session accepts, read
these from the same player view:

- Each group's
  `front_rank`, the members who can
  attack it in melee this round without moving, and its
  `member_distance_feet`,
  each member's distance to it.
- Each member's
  `encounter_rate_feet`, how far
  they can move this round. A member can close on a group and attack it in the same round
  when their distance to it is at most that rate plus 5'.
- `immobile` and `reloading` on the encounter view: who can't move, and who can't fire a
  reloading weapon this round.
- Each group's `members`, the individual
  monster or NPC ids and their coarse statuses. Use an `"alive"` entry's id to select a
  creature for a single-target or `up_to_n` spell or scroll.
- `advance_feet` on the encounter view,
  each member's place on the range track. Two members reach each other when their advances
  differ by 5' or less. A member needs to reach another to hand them an item, to give them a
  potion to drink, or to touch them with a staff of healing or a touch spell, like *cure
  light wounds*.

To check one member's choice against the choices already made for the round, call
`preview_battle_round` with them. To check
every target of each choice on a member's menu in the same call, pass the choices in its
`candidates` argument, each a `BattleCandidate`
with the target ids to try.

`action` decides which other fields apply. Leave the others at their defaults.

- `attack` uses `target_group_id` and, optionally, `weapon_id`, `move`, and `back_stab`.
  With no `weapon_id`, the member attacks with the wielded weapon that suits the attack,
  or with bare hands when they wield none. Set `move="close"` to close on the group first
  and attack it in the same round. Set `back_stab` for a thief's melee attack in the free
  round the party gets when it surprises the monsters, or from hiding after a `hide`.
- `cast` uses `spell_id`, `spell_mode`, `reversed`, and `targets`. `spell_id` is a spell
  id, like `"sleep"`. `spell_mode` is the key of one of the spell's modes, and `reversed`
  picks the spell's reversed form. A caster can't move in the round they cast, so leave
  `move` at `null`.
- `move` uses the `move` field, which is `close`, `fighting_withdrawal`, or `retreat`. A
  `close` moves this member toward the group in `target_group_id`, and nobody else. A
  `fighting_withdrawal` backs this member away slowly, facing the monsters, and a
  `retreat` turns and runs. When every member in `declarers` makes the same
  `fighting_withdrawal` or `retreat`, it's a formation move instead: the whole party moves
  as one body, and every group's distance changes.
- `use_item` uses `item_id`. The member drinks a potion, reads a scroll, uses a wand,
  staff, or rod, or throws a splash weapon, like a flask of oil, at `target_group_id`. The
  staves of power, striking, and wizardry strike the group in `target_group_id` for a
  charge, and a strike is a melee attack, so only a member in the group's `front_rank` can
  strike with one. A staff is slow, so the strike comes after both sides' blocks, as an
  `attack` with the staff does, and it spends the charge then. A use of the staff of power
  or wizardry with no `target_group_id` is one of their other powers instead, like the cone
  of cold: it spends a charge, and its `ItemUsedEvent` has the staff's text in `manual` for
  the referee to rule on. The staff of
  striking has no other power, so the session refuses a use of it with no `target_group_id`,
  and the code is `battle.declaration.unknown_group`. To swing a staff without spending a
  charge, declare an `attack` with it. To give a potion to another member to drink, or to
  touch another member with a staff of healing, name that member as the one id in
  `targets`. The two members have to reach each other once the round's moves are made. It's
  the action of the member who carries the item, and the potion's effect lands on the
  drinker. A scroll read uses `spell_id`, `spell_mode`, and `targets`, or `target_group_id`
  for a group-targeted spell, on the same terms as a `cast`.
- `give_item` uses `item_id` and `targets`. The member hands one item, or one unit of a
  stack, to the member named as the one id in `targets`. It's the giver's action for the
  round, and it resolves in the party's magic phase with the round's other item uses. The
  session checks it as `GiveItems` is checked, and the
  two members have to reach each other once the round's moves are made. The session refuses
  the `GiveItems` command in a battle.
- `turn_undead` uses nothing else. It reaches every living monster in the groups that
  haven't fled when it resolves. Turning resolves with the spells in the round. A hit
  can't disrupt it, because it's a class ability, not a spell.
- `hide` uses nothing else. A thief tries to hide in shadows, which takes their action for
  the round. The member is then hiding until the attempt ends, and a hiding member can
  back-stab without a place in the front rank, as
  `back_stab` describes.
  `EncounterView.can_hide` lists the members who
  can hide this round.
- `hold` does nothing. A member with no legal action declares it, because every member
  in `declarers` needs a declaration.

Only `attack` and `move` take a `move`. The session refuses a `cast` that sets one with
`battle.declaration.cast_cannot_move`, and a `turn_undead`, `use_item`, `give_item`, `hide`,
or `hold` that sets one with `battle.declaration.move_not_combinable`.

`gaze_defense` goes with any action. It guards the member against a petrifying gaze, like
a basilisk's or a medusa's, for this round only. Its values are `avert_eyes` and `mirror`.

For a fight that opens and runs with declared attacks until it ends, see the
`ResolveBattleRound` example.

code.title: Code
code.description:
