What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the party is in the fight and sees how it ends.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `battle_ended`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

BattleEndedEvent.title: BattleEndedEvent
BattleEndedEvent.description:
The battle is over: won, quit, or lost.

Emitted by `ResolveBattleRound`. A
battle can also end in the command that opened it, before any
`ResolveBattleRound`: every group's morale is too low to fight, or the monsters'
free round leaves no party member standing.

A victory ends the encounter in the same result. After a retreat, monsters able to
give chase start a chase, and the session goes back to `encounter` mode. Otherwise
the encounter ends. A defeat means nobody is left standing, and a
`GameOverEvent` follows in the same result.

visibility.description: Player visibility: everyone knows which round it is.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `battle_round`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

round.title: Round
round.description: Which round of this battle is starting, counting from one.

BattleRoundEvent.title: BattleRoundEvent
BattleRoundEvent.description:
A battle round began.

Emitted first by every
`ResolveBattleRound`, before the
declared spells and the initiative roll. In a transcript, group the rest of the
round's events under it.

rejections.title: Rejections
rejections.description:
Every reason the session would refuse each planned declaration, keyed by the declaring member's
id. There's one entry for each declaration you passed. An empty tuple means the session would
accept that declaration.

The codes and params are the ones
`ResolveBattleRound` returns for the same declarations.
`battle.declaration.roster_mismatch` never appears, because a plan with members still missing
would always get it.

advance_feet.title: Advance Feet
advance_feet.description:
Where each living member would stand once the planned moves are made, keyed by member id, in feet
forward of the party line, as in
`BattleState.advance_feet`. Every living member has
an entry. A member with no planned move keeps their current advance, and a member on the line has
zero. When the planned moves would leave every member the monsters can see behind the line, the
values are the ones after the line moves back, as the round would leave them.

front_rank.title: Front Rank
front_rank.description:
For each group that hasn't fled, keyed by group id, the members who would stand in its front rank
within 5' of it once the planned moves are made, in marching order. It means what
`EncounterGroupView.front_rank` means, after the
moves.

can_hide.title: Can Hide
can_hide.description:
The declarers who could declare `hide` in this round beside the other planned declarations, in
marching order. It's what `EncounterView.can_hide`
means, judged where the members would stand once the other members' planned moves are made, as
the session judges a `hide`. So a thief in the front rank is here once another member's planned
`close` takes their place in it, and a thief behind the front rank isn't here once another
member's planned fighting withdrawal leaves them in it.

A member declares one action in a round, so each member is judged as if the `hide` took the
place of their own planned declaration. A member's own planned move never takes them out of the
list, and a member whose planned declaration is the `hide` is here exactly when `rejections`
accepts it. For every declarer, membership matches what this function returns for the same plan
with that member's declaration replaced by a `hide`: the member is here exactly when that
preview has no rejection for them. When the plan makes no move, the list is the view's
`can_hide`.

can_back_stab.title: Can Back Stab
can_back_stab.description:
The declarers who could declare an `attack` with
`BattleDeclaration.back_stab` in this round
beside the other planned declarations, in marching order. It's what
`EncounterView.can_back_stab` means, and the
same rejection codes bound it: a member here never gets `battle.declaration.back_stab_no_ability`
or `battle.declaration.back_stab_target_aware`, and a declarer outside it always gets one of
them.

The session judges every declaration of a round before any of them resolves, and neither check
reads where the members stand, so the planned declarations don't change the list and it's
always the view's `can_back_stab`. A member whose planned declaration is a `hide` hasn't hidden
yet, so outside the party's free round they're here only when they were already hiding. A
hiding member whose planned move will end the attempt when it comes up is still here.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description:
The session's answer for each candidate you passed to
`preview_battle_round`, in the order you passed them.
It's empty when you passed none.

A member declares one action in a round, so each candidate is judged as `can_hide` judges a
`hide`: as if it took the place of the member's own planned declaration, where the other
members' planned moves would leave the party. The member's own planned move is never made
first, so a candidate that closes is judged from where the member stands now. For each
candidate and each of its targets, the entry matches what this function returns for the same
plan with that member's declaration replaced by `candidate.declaration_for(target_id)`: the
judgement's `rejections` entry is that preview's `rejections` for the member.

BattleRoundPreview.title: BattleRoundPreview
BattleRoundPreview.description:
What a battle round would do with the declarations planned so far, worked out without playing it.

`preview_battle_round` returns one. Read `rejections`
to grey out a choice the session would refuse, and read `advance_feet` and `front_rank` to show
where the members would stand once their declared moves are made. Read `can_hide` and
`can_back_stab` to offer a member a `hide` or a back-stab the session would accept beside the
choices already made, and read `candidates` for the answers to the candidates you passed. The
model is frozen. A preview without `can_hide` or `can_back_stab`, like one built by osrlib
2.7.0, parses with each of them empty, and a preview without `candidates`, like one built by
osrlib 2.10.0, parses with it empty.

declarations.title: Declarations
declarations.description:
osrlib `BattleDeclaration` objects, at most one for each member ID in `encounter.declarers` of the player view,
in any order. Pass any subset of the declarers, including none (`[]`). At most 20 entries.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description:
osrlib `BattleCandidate` objects: the actions a member could declare, each to be judged at every id in its
`target_ids`. The response's `candidates` has one judgement for each, in the order you send them. Omit the field,
or send `[]`, for a preview without candidates. At most 64 entries, with at most 256 target IDs counted over every
candidate's `target_ids`.

Build each candidate from a declaration that leaves its target out: set `declaration` to a `BattleDeclaration`
for a member in `encounter.declarers`, with the field that `target_field` names left at its default
(`target_group_id` `null`, or `targets` empty). Set `target_field` to `"target_group_id"` to judge group IDs from
`encounter.groups`, or to `"targets"` to judge member, monster, or NPC IDs, and list the IDs in `target_ids`
with none repeated.

BattleRoundPreviewRequest.title: BattleRoundPreviewRequest
BattleRoundPreviewRequest.description: The planned declarations and the candidate actions for `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/battle-round/preview`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the party is in it.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `battle_started`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

BattleStartedEvent.title: BattleStartedEvent
BattleStartedEvent.description:
The encounter became a battle.

Emitted when a fight opens: by `EngageBattle`
when the party attacks, and by whichever command is running when the monsters attack.
The monsters can attack the moment an encounter opens, when a parley goes wrong, when
a hostile or uncertain stance turns to attack on a later round, when undead are
presented with a holy symbol and not turned, or when a chase ends in capture.

The session mode becomes `battle`, where
`ResolveBattleRound` is the only play
command the session accepts. In battle, the session doesn't place monsters on cells. Each
monster group has a distance from the party, and closing in or pulling back changes it.

round.title: Round
round.description:
The number of rounds resolved so far. It's 0 between
`start_battle` and the first
`ResolveBattleRound`, unless the monsters had a free
round, which counts as round 1.

started_round.title: Started Round
started_round.description: The session clock's round count when the battle opened.

monsters_hold_rounds.title: Monsters Hold Rounds
monsters_hold_rounds.description:
The rounds in which the monsters still can't act because the party surprised them.

In each round while this is above zero, the monsters do nothing, and the count goes down by one.

morale.description:
The `MoraleTracker` for this battle. It counts each group's
passed morale checks, and a group that has passed two doesn't check again.

morale_acted.title: Morale Acted
morale_acted.description:
The morale triggers each group has already checked for, keyed by group id. A group checks morale
once per trigger per battle, so a group that has checked on losing its leader doesn't check again
for the same reason.

fired_last_round.title: Fired Last Round
fired_last_round.description:
The ids of the party members who, in the last round, fired a weapon that has to be reloaded.
`validate_attack` reads it to apply the reload rule under the
ruleset's `weapon_reload` flag, so the session rejects a second shot in a row.

melee_engagements.title: Melee Engagements
melee_engagements.description:
For each party member id, the monsters that member has attacked in melee. When *protection from
evil* bars a monster from attacking a character, the monster can attack that character anyway once
it's on this list, as the spell's text in the SRD says.

concentration.title: Concentration
concentration.description:
For each caster id, the effect ids of the concentration spell that caster maintains. A caster
maintains one at a time. The effects end when any of these happens:

- The caster declares an action other than `cast` or `hold`. A `turn_undead` counts.
- The caster's next spell is disrupted or fizzles.
- The caster casts another concentration spell.

advance_feet.title: Advance Feet
advance_feet.description:
Each party member's place on the range track, in feet forward of the party line, keyed by member id.

The party line is where the party stood when the encounter opened. Each group's
`distance_feet` is measured from it. A member
with no entry stands on the line, at zero. A positive advance is toward the monsters, and a negative
one is behind the line. A member's distance to a group is the group's distance minus the member's
advance, and `member_distance_feet` works it out for you.

The session changes it in the party's movement step. A member's `close` raises their advance, and a
`fighting_withdrawal` or a `retreat` the member makes alone lowers it. A formation move leaves every
advance as it is and moves the groups instead.

The party line moves back when the party has fallen back behind it. At the end of the party's
movement step, when every living member who isn't invisible stands behind the line, the session
moves the line back to the foremost of them. Every member's advance and every group's distance grow
by the same number of feet, so no distance between a member and a group changes, and the session
emits no event for it. The views show the moved values. The foremost members then stand on the line,
at zero, and a group can close on them as usual, because a group's distance never goes below zero.
When every living member is invisible, the line stays where it is.

The line also moves back when a group closes on a member who stands behind it and the group's
stopping point would be behind the line. That happens when a member the group can see still
stands forward of the line, so the movement step left the line where it was. The line moves back
by the shortfall in the same way, with no event, and the group then stands on the line.

Every member starts a battle on the line, and the
advances end with the battle, so the party stands on its cell as one body again once the fight is
over. A save written mid-battle keeps them, and a save from before they existed loads with every
member on the line.

arrived_round.title: Arrived Round
arrived_round.description:
The battle round in which each member reached their current advance, keyed by member id.

A member with no entry has stood where they are since the battle opened, which counts as round
zero. The session uses it to order members who stand at the same distance from a group: the member
who got there in an earlier round stands in front, and marching order settles a tie. So a member
already fighting keeps their place in the front rank when others arrive beside them.

hiding.title: Hiding
hiding.description:
The members who are hiding, keyed by member id, each with whether their hide in shadows roll passed.

A member enters it when their `hide` declaration resolves, and leaves it when the attempt ends, as
`BattleDeclaration.back_stab` lists. A second
`hide` replaces the value with the new roll's. The value is the referee's secret. The players see
only who is hiding, in `EncounterView.hiding`, and learn
how the attempt went from the back-stab's
`AttackRolledEvent.back_stab`.

A member whose value is true has hidden unseen. The built-in policies pass them over while they can
pick another member, and a policy of your own reads this to do the same. A member whose value is
false has been noticed, and the monsters can pick them. Under the ruleset's
`back_stab_needs_both_skills` flag off,
such a member can still back-stab if the move silently roll passes. Both rolls draw from the
`COMBAT_STREAM`. The field starts empty with each battle, and a
save from before it existed loads with nobody hiding.

BattleState.title: BattleState
BattleState.description:
A battle in progress: the round count and what the session tracks from one round to the next.

You get this from `session.battle`, which is None whenever no battle is running. A battle
doesn't replace the encounter. The monster groups, their distances, and their treasure stay on
`session.encounter`, and this model contains only what the fight adds. It's saved with the
session, so a saved game resumes in the middle of a battle. Read it to show the battle. The
session updates every field as it resolves each round.

To change a fight while it runs, execute a referee command from
`osrlib.crawl.commands` instead of writing to this model. Referee
commands are allowed in `battle` mode, so a referee can grant an item, award experience, set a
flag, or advance the clock during a fight. The command log records the command, so a replay
reproduces the change. `SpawnMonsters` adds a new
monster group to the fight between rounds, and the group acts from the next round.

`SpawnNpcParty` and
`PlaceParty` aren't legal in `battle`, so the session refuses
them with `session.command.wrong_mode`. An NPC party can't join a fight, and you can't move the
party out of one.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"cast_spell"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
The caster, by `MemberView.id`. The caster needs a
memorized copy of the spell, and casting uses it up.

spell_id.title: Spell Id
spell_id.description:
The spell to cast, by its id in
`GameSession.effective_spells`: a
built-in spell (see the
[spell id index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/spells/)) or one
the adventure bundles. The session refuses a caster with no memorized copy with
`magic.cast.not_memorized`, and refuses a member who can't cast spells at all the same way.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description:
Which of the spell's usages to cast, by that usage's
`SpellMode.key` on the form you're casting. A spell with
several usages, like *light*, has one mode for each. For a spell with one usage, you still name
its one key. The session refuses a key the form doesn't have with `magic.cast.unknown_mode`.

reversed.title: Reversed
reversed.description:
Cast the reversed form, like *cause light wounds* for *cure light wounds*. An arcane
caster fixes the form when memorizing, so a reversed cast needs a reversed copy memorized.
A divine caster memorizes the normal form and chooses the form here, when casting. The session
refuses `reversed` on a spell with no reversed form, with `magic.cast.not_reversible`.

targets.title: Targets
targets.description:
Who or what the spell targets: a party member's
`MemberView.id`, in any state, or, for a spell that
affects a place rather than a creature, a cell reference in the
`cell:{dungeon}:{level}:{x},{y}` form that `cell_ref`
builds. A dead or petrified member can be named, so *raise dead* and *stone to flesh* work on
them. The session refuses any other id with `magic.cast.unknown_target`, a monster's or an NPC
adventurer's included, even one an earlier event named. A cell reference has to name a cell of
the level the party stands on. The session refuses one that doesn't parse, names no cell of the
adventure, or names a cell of another level or another dungeon with `magic.cast.unknown_target`,
and in town it refuses every cell reference that way. A member who is invisible is still a
target. The mode's targeting sets how many targets it takes, and the session refuses the
wrong number with `magic.cast.target_count`.
The session refuses a cell reference for a mode that works only on creatures with
`magic.cast.target_must_be_creature`.

CastSpell.title: CastSpell
CastSpell.description:
Cast a memorized spell outside battle (one round).

The caster needs a memorized copy of the spell, which
`PrepareSpells` gives them, and casting uses the
copy up. Each target is an entity id, or a `cell:` reference for a spell that affects a
place. This command isn't legal during an encounter or a battle. To cast at monsters the
party has met, open battle with
`EngageBattle` and declare a `cast`
`BattleDeclaration` in the round.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - an encounter or battle is underway, or the
  session has ended.
- `session.command.unknown_member` - `character_id` matches no party member.
- `session.command.member_incapacitated` - the member can't act.
- `magic.cast.unknown_spell` - `spell_id` matches no spell in the session's catalog.
- `magic.cast.silenced_area` - a *silence* effect covers the party's cell.
- `magic.cast.unknown_target` - a target id isn't a party member's. No encounter is open
  in this command's modes, so the party can act on no other creature. A monster or an NPC
  adventurer of an encounter that has ended gets this code, with the same params as an id
  that matches nothing. A cell reference gets it too when it doesn't name a cell of the
  level the party stands on, and every cell reference gets it in town.
- `magic.cast.not_memorized` - the caster has no memorized copy. A member who
  can't cast spells at all gets this code too.
- `magic.cast.caster_incapacitated`, `magic.cast.caster_restrained`,
  `magic.cast.anti_magic_shell` - the caster can't cast right now.
- `magic.cast.not_reversible` - `reversed` is set on a spell with no reversed
  form.
- `magic.cast.unknown_mode` - `mode` matches no mode of the spell.
- `magic.cast.target_count` - the number of targets is wrong for the mode.
- `magic.cast.target_must_be_creature` - a target is a cell reference, and the
  mode works only on creatures, like *fire ball*'s or *sleep*'s.
- `magic.cast.out_of_range` - a target is beyond the spell's range.

**Events:**

`SpellCastEvent`, then the events of the
spell's resolution: saving throws, damage, healing, and effects attached, each a
separate event. One round passes.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The character's id within a game, like `"character-0001"`, or `null` before a session assigns one.

`GameSession.new` assigns an id from the session's
`IdAllocator` to each party member whose id is `null`.
`AddMember` does the same for a character who joins during play. Commands refer
to a character by this id. An event about a character with no id uses the character's `name` instead.

name.title: Name
name.description: The character's name, for display. It can't be empty.

class_id.title: Class Id
class_id.description:
The id of the character's class, like `"fighter"`.

For a class osrlib includes, the id comes from `load_classes` and is listed in
[the class id index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/classes/). For a class you wrote,
it's the `id` of the definition in `custom_class`. Read
`definition` for the class itself.

custom_class.description:
The definition of the character's class when it's a class you wrote, or `null` for a class osrlib includes.

Set it to your `ClassDefinition`, and set `class_id` to the definition's
`id`. `definition` returns it, so the kernel functions and a
`GameSession` play the character under your class.
`create_character` sets it when you pass `custom_class`.

The model refuses a definition whose `id` isn't `class_id`. It also refuses a definition whose `id` is the id of a
built-in class, because a class id refers to one class. Give a variant of a built-in class a different id.

The definition is part of the character, so `to_document`,
`party_to_document`, and `save_game`
include it, and loading the document gives it back. Your game doesn't supply the class again to load one.

race.title: Race
race.description:
The character's race, like `"human"` or `"dwarf"`, as a lowercase identifier.

Creation copies it from the class's `race`. No rules function reads it.
What a race can do, like a dwarf's infravision, comes from the class's
`abilities`.

level.title: Level
level.description: The experience level, 1 through the class's maximum.

xp.title: Xp
xp.description:
The character's total experience points.

Award experience with `apply_xp`, which adds to this total and levels the character
up when it reaches the next level's threshold. Assigning a new total here doesn't change the level.

scores.title: Scores
scores.description:
The six ability scores, each 3 through 18, keyed by `AbilityScore`. All six
must be present.

They're the scores the character rolled, after any adjustment at creation. A STR that an item sets, like the 18 of
gauntlets of ogre power, doesn't change them. Read
`effective_strength` for the STR the rules use during play.

alignment.description:
Lawful, neutral, or chaotic. It sets the secret language in
`alignment_tongue`.

extra_languages.title: Extra Languages
extra_languages.description:
The language ids chosen at creation because of a high INT. Check the choice with
`validate_extra_languages` before you store it.

current_hp.title: Current Hp
current_hp.description:
Current hit points, from 0 up to `max_hp`.

A character at 0 hit points is out of the fight. Whether a character is dead is the `dead` condition, which
`kill` applies, not a hit point value.

nonregen_damage.title: Nonregen Damage
nonregen_damage.description:
The fire and acid damage that a worn ring of regeneration can't heal, up to `max_hp`.

While the character wears the ring, `deal_damage` adds fire and acid damage
here. The ring heals the character only up to `max_hp` less this amount. Other healing, like a potion, heals this
damage too. So each time the character takes damage while wearing the ring, `deal_damage` first lowers this value
to the damage the character had before that hit. It's 0 for a character who has never worn the ring.

inventory.description:
Everything the character carries, wears, and wields, and their coins. See
`Inventory` and the buying and equipping functions in
`osrlib.core.items`.

carrying_treasure.title: Carrying Treasure
carrying_treasure.description:
Whether the character is carrying enough treasure to slow them down, under basic encumbrance.

The basic encumbrance rules leave the amount to the referee, so osrlib leaves it to you. Set this flag, and
`movement_rate` drops the character to the next slower rate.
The other encumbrance modes ignore it.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description:
The conditions in effect, like poisoned or paralysed.

Apply and clear them with the functions in `osrlib.core.effects`. Test for one with
`has_condition`.

stat_modifiers.title: Stat Modifiers
stat_modifiers.description:
Timed bonuses and penalties from spells and items. The functions in
`osrlib.core.effects` apply and remove them.

spell_book.title: Spell Book
spell_book.description:
The spell ids in an arcane caster's spell book, in the order they were added.

An arcane caster memorizes spells only from this book. It's empty for divine casters like the cleric, who memorize
from their whole class list, and for classes that cast no spells.

memorized_spells.title: Memorized Spells
memorized_spells.description:
The spells the caster has memorized and can cast, as `MemorizedSpell`
records in the order they were memorized.

Fill it with `memorize_spells`. Casting spends the first matching copy in
the list, and energy drain removes copies from the end. How many spells of each level fit comes from the class's
progression row for the current level, so it changes when the level does.

Character.title: Character
Character.description:
A player character: the stored state of one character, and the values derived from it.

Get one from `create_character`, or from
`from_document` when you load a stored
character. Construct one directly when you create a character step by step with the other
creation functions in this module, or when you already have every value, as in a test.

Put characters in a `Party` to explore with them. Pass one to the
functions in `osrlib.core.combat` as an attacker or a target, to the
functions in `osrlib.core.spells` as a caster, and to
`apply_xp` or `level_up` to
advance it. A `MonsterInstance` has the same combat
attributes, so the combat functions take either.

The model is mutable and validates on assignment. Setting a field to a value that breaks a rule
raises a pydantic `ValidationError`, and every field still has the value it had before the
assignment. Validation is structural only. It checks that the six scores
are present and in range, that `class_id` is the id of a class in
`load_classes` or of the definition in
`custom_class`, that the level is within the
class's maximum, and that current hit points don't exceed maximum hit points. It doesn't check
that the character was created legally, because a finished character has no record of how it was
created.

Nothing derived is stored. THAC0, attack bonus, saving throws, ability modifiers, both armour
classes, and the language list are properties recomputed from the stored fields each time you
read them, so a level change or a swapped piece of armour shows up at once.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the new level goes on the character's sheet.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `leveled_up`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description: The member who gained the level.

level_before.title: Level Before
level_before.description: The member's level before the award.

level_after.title: Level After
level_after.description: The member's level after the award, one higher.

hp_gained.title: Hp Gained
hp_gained.description:
How many hit points were added, the die and the constitution adjustment together, or the
flat bonus past the class's last Hit Die.

hp_roll.title: Hp Roll
hp_roll.description:
The hit die that was rolled, or `null` past the class's last Hit Die, where levels bring a
flat bonus and no die.

con_applied.title: Con Applied
con_applied.description: Whether the constitution adjustment was applied, which happens only when a die was rolled.

title.title: Title
title.description: The class's title for the new level, or `null` past the printed list of titles.

CharacterLeveledUpEvent.title: CharacterLeveledUpEvent
CharacterLeveledUpEvent.description:
A character crossed a threshold and gained a level.

Emitted right after that member's
`XpAwardedEvent`, for whichever award crossed
the threshold. A character gains at most one level per award.

character.description:
osrlib `Character` model that `POST /v1/characters` stores for the same roll and choices, with
`id` set to `null`.

derived.description: Combat, saving throw, modifier, and language values computed by osrlib from `character`.

rolls.description: Individual dice rolled for the roll's ability scores, the hit points, and the starting gold.

CharacterPreview.title: CharacterPreview
CharacterPreview.description: Unstored first-level character that `POST /v1/characters` would create from an ability roll, with its dice.

name.title: Name
name.description: Character name, 1 to 100 characters, without control characters such as tabs or newlines.

class_id.title: Class Id
class_id.description:
Character class `id` from `GET /v1/rules/classes`, such as `fighter`. Must meet the class's
ability score requirements (`eligible_class_ids` on `POST /v1/ability-rolls`).

adjustment.description:
Optional point trade between ability scores before rolling hit points, as osrlib's
`AbilityAdjustment`. Map abilities to lower in `lowered` and abilities to raise in `raised`
using keys `str`, `int`, `wis`, `dex`, `con`, and `cha`. osrlib's descriptions of `lowered` and
`raised` name `ADJUSTMENT_FLOOR` and `MAX_SCORE`, which are osrlib's Python constants for the
lowest and the highest score a trade can leave. For the scores a trade can reach from a stored
ability roll with this class, and the reason for each limit, call
`GET /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/adjustment-limits`. If osrlib refuses the trade, creation fails with 422
`character_invalid` and `rejections`. Omit or set to `null` to keep the rolled scores.

starting_spell_ids.title: Starting Spell Ids
starting_spell_ids.description:
First-level spell `id` values from `GET /v1/rules/spells` for an arcane caster's starting
spell book. A first-level `magic_user` or `elf` requires exactly one first-level `magic_user`
spell. Leave empty (`[]`) for every other class.

extra_languages.title: Extra Languages
extra_languages.description:
Extra language `id` values from `GET /v1/rules/languages` (entries with `choosable` set to
`true`), up to the bonus languages granted by the character's adjusted Intelligence score.

purchases.title: Purchases
purchases.description:
Starting equipment bought in list order from rolled starting gold (3d6 x 10 gp). To show the
player their gold before they shop, call `POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview` with the
same roll, class, and `ruleset`, and read `rolls.gold_roll.total`. The purchases don't change
the gold roll.

equip_item_ids.title: Equip Item Ids
equip_item_ids.description:
Purchased item `id` values to wear or wield, applied in list order. Each entry equips one
purchased stack from `purchases` and must be permitted for `class_id`.

ruleset.description:
Optional rules for the creation rolls, as osrlib's `Ruleset`. Send the ruleset of the table
the character is for, the one you pass to `POST /v1/sessions`. Creation reads three of its
fields, and the others change nothing here:

- `ability_score_method`: `"3d6"` (the default) or `"4d6_drop_lowest"`. With an ability roll,
  it must be the method the roll was made with, or the request gets 409
  `ability_roll_ruleset_mismatch`.
- `hp_reroll_at_first_level`: reroll a first-level hit die that shows 1 or 2.
- `max_hp_at_first_level`: count the first-level hit die as its maximum.

Omit or set to `null` for the rules as written.

CharacterPreviewRequest.title: CharacterPreviewRequest
CharacterPreviewRequest.description:
Choices for previewing the character `POST /v1/characters` would create from an ability roll.

The body has every member `POST /v1/characters` accepts except `ability_roll_id`, because the
path names the roll, and `seed`, because the roll's seed decides the dice.

name.title: Name
name.description: Character name, 1 to 100 characters, without control characters such as tabs or newlines.

class_id.title: Class Id
class_id.description:
Character class `id` from `GET /v1/rules/classes`, such as `fighter`. Must meet the class's
ability score requirements (`eligible_class_ids` on `POST /v1/ability-rolls`).

adjustment.description:
Optional point trade between ability scores before rolling hit points, as osrlib's
`AbilityAdjustment`. Map abilities to lower in `lowered` and abilities to raise in `raised`
using keys `str`, `int`, `wis`, `dex`, `con`, and `cha`. osrlib's descriptions of `lowered` and
`raised` name `ADJUSTMENT_FLOOR` and `MAX_SCORE`, which are osrlib's Python constants for the
lowest and the highest score a trade can leave. For the scores a trade can reach from a stored
ability roll with this class, and the reason for each limit, call
`GET /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/adjustment-limits`. If osrlib refuses the trade, creation fails with 422
`character_invalid` and `rejections`. Omit or set to `null` to keep the rolled scores.

starting_spell_ids.title: Starting Spell Ids
starting_spell_ids.description:
First-level spell `id` values from `GET /v1/rules/spells` for an arcane caster's starting
spell book. A first-level `magic_user` or `elf` requires exactly one first-level `magic_user`
spell. Leave empty (`[]`) for every other class.

extra_languages.title: Extra Languages
extra_languages.description:
Extra language `id` values from `GET /v1/rules/languages` (entries with `choosable` set to
`true`), up to the bonus languages granted by the character's adjusted Intelligence score.

purchases.title: Purchases
purchases.description:
Starting equipment bought in list order from rolled starting gold (3d6 x 10 gp). To show the
player their gold before they shop, call `POST /v1/ability-rolls/{roll_id}/preview` with the
same roll, class, and `ruleset`, and read `rolls.gold_roll.total`. The purchases don't change
the gold roll.

equip_item_ids.title: Equip Item Ids
equip_item_ids.description:
Purchased item `id` values to wear or wield, applied in list order. Each entry equips one
purchased stack from `purchases` and must be permitted for `class_id`.

ruleset.description:
Optional rules for the creation rolls, as osrlib's `Ruleset`. Send the ruleset of the table
the character is for, the one you pass to `POST /v1/sessions`. Creation reads three of its
fields, and the others change nothing here:

- `ability_score_method`: `"3d6"` (the default) or `"4d6_drop_lowest"`. With an ability roll,
  it must be the method the roll was made with, or the request gets 409
  `ability_roll_ruleset_mismatch`.
- `hp_reroll_at_first_level`: reroll a first-level hit die that shows 1 or 2.
- `max_hp_at_first_level`: count the first-level hit die as its maximum.

Omit or set to `null` for the rules as written.

ability_roll_id.title: Ability Roll Id
ability_roll_id.description:
Unused ability roll `id` from `POST /v1/ability-rolls` to take scores, hit points, and
starting gold from. Omit to roll fresh ability scores during this request. Mutually exclusive
with `seed`.

anyOf.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

seed.title: Seed
seed.description:
Referee only. Seed (0 to 2^53 - 1) for all creation rolls when you omit `ability_roll_id`.
Mutually exclusive with `ability_roll_id`. The server never returns `seed`.

CharacterRequest.title: CharacterRequest
CharacterRequest.description: Choices and optional ability roll or referee seed for `POST /v1/characters`.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Character identifier (`chr_` followed by 22 characters). Pass to
`GET /v1/characters/{character_id}` or in `character_ids` on `POST /v1/sessions`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Character name.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when the server stored the character, in RFC 3339 format such as
`"2026-11-20T22:01:05Z"`.

CharacterSummary.title: CharacterSummary
CharacterSummary.description: Summary fields returned for each character in `GET /v1/characters`.

min_score.title: Min Score
min_score.description: The lowest score this row covers.

max_score.title: Max Score
max_score.description: The highest score this row covers. Equal to `min_score` on a one-score row.

npc_reactions.title: Npc Reactions
npc_reactions.description: What to add to the reaction roll that sets how monsters or NPCs respond when they meet the party.

max_retainers.title: Max Retainers
max_retainers.description: How many retainers, hired followers, the character may have at once. osrlib's rules don't use it.

retainer_loyalty.title: Retainer Loyalty
retainer_loyalty.description: The loyalty score a retainer of this character starts with. osrlib's rules don't use it.

CharismaRow.title: CharismaRow
CharismaRow.description:
One row of the charisma table: a band of scores, with its reaction modifier and retainer limits.

Read the rows from `AbilityTables.charisma` to draw
the table. To look up one score, call
`npc_reaction_modifier`,
`max_retainers`, or
`retainer_loyalty` instead.

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: The identifier the rules functions match, like `"infravision"`, `"detect_secret_doors"`, or `"back_stab"`.

name.title: Name
name.description: The ability's name as the SRD prints it, for display.

prose.title: Prose
prose.description: The SRD's description of the ability, to show a player or the referee.

manual.title: Manual
manual.description: True when osrlib doesn't apply this ability, and the referee applies it from `prose`.

params.title: Params
params.description:
The values the rules functions read, like `{"range_feet": 60}` for infravision or `{"chance_in_six": 2}` for a
detection ability. Empty when the ability has none.

A `divine_magic` or `arcane_magic` ability has a `spell_list`, the id of the spell list the class casts from, like
`"magic_user"`. `ClassDefinition` refuses a casting ability without one.

ClassAbility.title: ClassAbility
ClassAbility.description:
One thing a class can do, like a dwarf's infravision: a tag the rules functions match, its numbers, and its text.

Read a class's abilities from
`ClassDefinition.abilities`. The combat,
magic, and exploration functions look for the tags they recognize and read the numbers from
`params`. They ignore a tag they don't recognize. Frozen.

An ability osrlib doesn't apply has `manual` set. Show its `prose` to the referee, who applies
it.

id.title: Id
id.description: The class id, like `"fighter"`. A character stores it in `class_id`.

name.title: Name
name.description: The class's name as the SRD prints it, like `"Magic-User"`, for display.

race.title: Race
race.description:
The race of the class's characters, as a lowercase identifier, like `"human"` or `"dwarf"`.

Creation copies it onto the character. No rules function reads it. What a race can do comes from `abilities`.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.description:
The lowest ability score a character needs in each listed ability to take this class.

`validate_class_choice` checks them. Empty for the human classes.
The dwarf, the elf, and the halfling each require a 9 in one or two abilities.

prime_requisites.title: Prime Requisites
prime_requisites.description:
The abilities the class depends on most. There's one for most classes, and two for the elf and the halfling.

The ability-score adjustment at creation can raise only these, and can't lower them. The experience modifier in
`xp_tiers` usually depends on them.

xp_tiers.title: Xp Tiers
xp_tiers.description:
The experience-modifier tiers, highest percentage first.
`xp_modifier_pct` reads them.

hit_die.title: Hit Die
hit_die.description: The number of sides on the class's hit die. It's 4, 6, or 8 for the built-in classes.

max_level.title: Max Level
max_level.description:
The highest level a character of this class can reach. It's 14 for the human classes, 12 for the dwarf, 10 for
the elf, and 8 for the halfling.

armour.description: Which armour and shields the class may use. See `ArmourPolicy`.

weapons.description: Which weapons the class may wield. See `WeaponPolicy`.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description:
The ids of the languages every character of this class speaks, starting with `"common"`.

A character's full list, with the alignment tongue and any extra languages, is
`Character.languages`.

may_not_lower.title: May Not Lower
may_not_lower.description:
Abilities the ability-score adjustment at creation can't lower, besides the prime requisites. The thief's is
STR.

abilities.title: Abilities
abilities.description:
What the class can do, as tags the rules functions read.

See `ClassAbility`.

thief_skills.title: Thief Skills
thief_skills.description:
The thief's skill chances, one row per level from 1 to `max_level`. Empty for every built-in class but the thief.
See `ThiefSkillRow`.

level_titles.title: Level Titles
level_titles.description:
The title of a character at each level, starting with level 1, like `"Veteran"` for a first-level fighter.

The SRD prints titles only up to name level, so this can be shorter than `progression`. Call
`level_title` to read one, which returns `null` for a level past the end.

progression.title: Progression
progression.description:
One progression row for each level from 1 to `max_level`, in order. Read one with
`row`, which checks the level.

overrides_applied.title: Overrides Applied
overrides_applied.description:
The fields osrlib corrected when it compiled this class from the SRD, like `"xp_tiers"`. Empty when none were.

Read it when you check osrlib's data against the SRD. No rules function reads it.

ClassDefinition.title: ClassDefinition
ClassDefinition.description:
A character class, like the fighter or the elf: its rules, and its values at every level.

Get one from `load_classes().get(class_id)`. For the ids, iterate
`load_classes().classes` or see [the class id
index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/classes/). A
`Character` stores only the class id, and
`Character.definition` returns the definition for it. Pass the
definition to the functions in this module that take one, like `apply_xp`.

A definition is frozen and shared by every character of the class. What changes in play, like
the level and the hit points, is stored on the character. The built-in definitions are compiled
from the SRD's class pages. To write a class of your own, build a `ClassDefinition` with
`model_validate`, which checks it with the same rules as the built-in classes. One of those rules
is that a `divine_magic` or `arcane_magic` ability has a `spell_list` param, so
`caster_profile` always finds the list a casting class uses.
Another is that a class has at most one of those two abilities, because a character casts from one
spell list.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Class identifier, such as `"fighter"`. Pass as `class_id` to `POST /v1/characters` or
`GET /v1/rules/classes/{class_id}`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the class, such as `"Fighter"`.

race.title: Race
race.description: Lowercase race identifier for members of the class, such as `"human"` or `"dwarf"`.

prime_requisites.title: Prime Requisites
prime_requisites.description: Ability scores that determine the class's experience point modifier.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.description:
Minimum score required in each constrained ability to choose the class. Empty (`{}`) when the
class has no minimum ability requirements.

hit_die.title: Hit Die
hit_die.description:
Die size (number of sides, such as `8` for d8) rolled for hit points at first level and up to
name level.

max_level.title: Max Level
max_level.description: Highest level a character of this class can reach, such as `14` or `12`.

ClassSummary.title: ClassSummary
ClassSummary.description: Summary of a character class from osrlib's `ClassDefinition`, for building a class picker.

rounds.title: Rounds
rounds.description: Total elapsed time in 10-second combat rounds.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: Total elapsed time in whole 10-minute exploration turns (`rounds` divided by 60).

days.title: Days
days.description: Total elapsed time in whole 24-hour days (`rounds` divided by 8,640).

Clock.title: Clock
Clock.description: Elapsed in-game time since the adventure began, preserved across saves and restores.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"close_door"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

direction.description:
Which side of the party's cell the door is on. Only a door the party knows about counts,
so this is one of the `door` edges in
`ExploredLevelView.edges`. A wedged door
can't close, and the session refuses it with `exploration.door.wedged`.

CloseDoor.title: CloseDoor
CloseDoor.description:
Close an open door on one side of the party's cell (takes no game time).

The party must be exploring a dungeon (see
`EnterDungeon`). You rarely need this command,
because a door the party opened swings shut by itself once the party walks away from it,
unless it's wedged.

Modes:

`exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the session is not exploring a dungeon.
- `exploration.door.no_door` - no known door on that side of the cell.
- `exploration.door.already_closed` - the door is already closed.
- `exploration.door.wedged` - a wedged door cannot swing.

**Events:**

`DoorEvent` with code
`exploration.door.closed`.

CoinDenomination.title: CoinDenomination
CoinDenomination.description: One of the five B/X coin denominations: `pp` (platinum), `gp` (gold), `ep` (electrum), `sp` (silver), or `cp` (copper). Each value matches the corresponding field name on `Coins`.

ep.title: Ep
ep.description: Electrum pieces, worth half a gold piece each.

sp.title: Sp
sp.description: Silver pieces, ten to the gold piece.

cp.title: Cp
cp.description: Copper pieces, a hundred to the gold piece.

CoinPurse.title: CoinPurse
CoinPurse.description:
The coins a character is carrying, by denomination.

Every `Inventory` has one. Unlike
`Coins`, it's mutable, because this is the money that gets
spent. Call `can_afford` before
you charge, and `spend` to charge. Both work in
whole gold pieces, the unit the equipment lists price in.

Paying takes the smallest coins first, and change comes back as the fewest coins that
make it up. Each coin weighs 1 whatever its metal, so spending small coins first
lightens the purse. A purse full of copper slows a character down.

dice.title: Dice
dice.description: How many, as a dice expression.

CoinQuantity.title: CoinQuantity
CoinQuantity.description:
How many coins of one denomination a treasure entry yields.

The printed multiplier is part of the dice expression, so an entry that reads
`1d6 × 1,000 gp` arrives here as dice of `1d6×1000` and a denomination of gold. Roll it
with `roll` if you're generating by hand. The generation
functions do it for you.

ep.title: Ep
ep.description: Electrum pieces, worth half a gold piece each.

sp.title: Sp
sp.description: Silver pieces, ten to the gold piece.

cp.title: Cp
cp.description: Copper pieces, a hundred to the gold piece.

Coins.title: Coins
Coins.description:
A fixed pile of coins, like generated treasure, the contents of a chest, or a pile dropped on the floor.

Frozen, unlike the `CoinPurse` a character carries.
`generate_treasure` returns its coins in this
form, and a dungeon feature contains its coins this way until someone picks them up. To
give the coins to a character, add each denomination to their purse.

damage.title: Damage
damage.description: The damage dealt, as a dice expression.

qualities.title: Qualities
qualities.description:
What the item can do when used as a weapon. See `WeaponQuality`. Holy water
and burning oil have the splash quality, which makes them damage the target again the following round.

missile_ranges.description: The three range bands, present exactly when `qualities` includes the missile quality.

CombatFacet.title: CombatFacet
CombatFacet.description:
The combat statistics of a piece of gear that can also be used as a weapon.

Torch, holy water, and burning oil are printed on both the SRD's weapon table and its
gear list. osrlib compiles each as one gear item whose `combat` field contains this facet,
so the item has a single id and a single weight. Attack resolution reads the facet's
damage, qualities, and ranges as it reads those of a
`WeaponTemplate`. Class weapon policies don't apply
to it, so a cleric may throw holy water and a magic-user may swing a torch. That
exemption is an adaptation, a reading osrlib chooses where the rules are unclear (see
the [adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/)).

attack_matrix.description: The attack matrix: the roll each kind of attacker needs against each armour class.

monster_saves.title: Monster Saves
monster_saves.description:
The monster saving throw bands, from the fewest Hit Dice to the most. Find one by label with
`save_band`.

xp_awards.title: Xp Awards
xp_awards.description:
The experience points a defeated monster is worth, one row for each Hit Dice label. Find one by label with
`xp_row`.

turning.description: The table for turning undead: what a cleric can do to undead, by the cleric's level and the undead's Hit Dice.

reaction.description: The monster reaction table, which turns a 2d6 total into how monsters respond to the party.

CombatTables.title: CombatTables
CombatTables.description:
The tables the combat rules read, loaded together.

Get it from `load_combat_tables`. Read the table you
want from its field, or pass it to `monster_xp`. Pass
`reaction` to `reaction_result`, and call
`turning.result` to look up turning undead.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description:
The name that identifies the command class in serialized data. Each command class fixes
it to a distinct snake_case string, like `"move_party"` or `"open_door"`. In Python,
constructing the class sets it, so you don't pass it.
`parse_command` and the
`AnyCommand` union use it to rebuild the right class
from a serialized mapping, so a mapping you pass to either one has to include it, like
the JSON body of a request. A class's value never changes between releases.

source.title: Source
source.description:
Who or what issued the command on whose behalf: an authored trigger or quest id, or the
name of one of your game's systems. The engine never reads it, so a command with a
`source` does exactly what the same command without one does. The session logs and
replays it with the command, so the log alone shows why something happened. Leave it
`null` when there's nothing to record. An empty string fails validation when the command
is constructed.

Command.title: Command
Command.description:
The base class of every command.

You don't construct this class. Construct one of the command classes, which all inherit
`source` and `command_type` from it, and pass the command to
`GameSession.execute`. Annotate a parameter
with `Command` when it takes any command object. Annotate it with
`AnyCommand` when pydantic has to build the command
from serialized data.

Commands are frozen: you can't change a field after construction. The session logs an
accepted command exactly as it arrived, and replaying the log replays the game.
Parsing a command ignores fields its class doesn't define, so a command from a newer
engine still parses on an older one.

Don't subclass this class to add your own actions. The session has no handler for a
class defined outside osrlib, and
`GameSession.execute` raises `ValueError` for
one. Issue referee commands, or register a
`Listener`, instead.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description:
Command discriminator value, such as `"move_party"`. Pass to
`GET /v1/rules/commands/{command_type}` for its body schema or send in
`POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`.

kind.description: Who may send the command: `"play"` (any caller) or `"referee"` (`referee` role only).

CommandChoice.title: CommandChoice
CommandChoice.description: One command legal in the session's current mode for the caller's role.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description:
Discriminator string to send in `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`, such as
`"move_party"`.

kind.description: Who may send the command: `"play"` (any caller) or `"referee"` (`referee` role only).

allowed_modes.title: Allowed Modes
allowed_modes.description: Session modes in which the command is legal, sorted alphabetically.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One-line description from the opening paragraph of osrlib's command documentation.

json_schema.title: Json Schema
json_schema.description:
Raw JSON Schema generated by pydantic from osrlib's command model. Include `command_type` in
every request body sent to `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands` even though osrlib's raw
schema lists `command_type` with a default instead of inside `required`.

CommandDetail.title: CommandDetail
CommandDetail.description: Summary of a session command, plus the JSON Schema for its request body.

CommandKind.title: CommandKind
CommandKind.description: Who may send a command: `play` for any caller (`player` or `referee`), or `referee` for a `referee` key only.

accepted.title: Accepted
accepted.description:
Whether osrlib accepted and applied the command. When `false`, the session state and
`revision` are unchanged.

rejections.title: Rejections
rejections.description:
Rule rejections (`code` and `params`) explaining why `accepted` is `false`, or `[]` when
`accepted` is `true`.

events.title: Events
events.description:
Ordered events emitted by the command and any triggered adventure logic, filtered to the
requested `visibility` (`player` by default).

messages.title: Messages
messages.description:
Human-readable English summary line for each entry in `events`, in matching order, formatted
by osrlib's `format_message`.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Session revision after the command (incremented by 1 when `accepted` is `true`).

view.title: View
view.description:
Updated `PlayerView` at `revision` (matching `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/view`), with
known map features and encounter member IDs, included only when the request passes
`include=view`.

CommandOutcome.title: CommandOutcome
CommandOutcome.description: Result of executing a command on `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description:
Discriminator string to send in `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`, such as
`"move_party"`.

kind.description: Who may send the command: `"play"` (any caller) or `"referee"` (`referee` role only).

allowed_modes.title: Allowed Modes
allowed_modes.description: Session modes in which the command is legal, sorted alphabetically.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One-line description from the opening paragraph of osrlib's command documentation.

CommandSummary.title: CommandSummary
CommandSummary.description: Summary of one session command defined by osrlib.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"complete_objective"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

quest_id.title: Quest Id
quest_id.description:
Which quest the objective belongs to, by
`QuestSpec.id`. The quest has to be active.

objective_id.title: Objective Id
objective_id.description:
Which objective is complete, by
`ObjectiveSpec.id` within that quest. A hidden
objective is revealed as it completes, so it needs no separate
`RevealObjective`.

CompleteObjective.title: CompleteObjective
CompleteObjective.description:
Referee: mark one objective of an active quest complete.

Completing a hidden objective also reveals it, in one step, with no separate
`RevealObjective`. The command accepts only the
ids the adventure's quest specs define, as
`ActivateQuest` describes, and the `ActivateQuest`
example shows a quest from start to finish.

Completing the last objective a quest needs doesn't complete the quest. Send
`CompleteQuest` for that, so whoever runs the
quests decides when the quest is done. When the objective's author wrote a `progress`
text in its narrative, an accepted completion adds that text to the journal, and the
event includes it. No
`JournalEntryAddedEvent` follows.
This command is legal in every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.unknown_quest` - `quest_id` matches no quest of the
  adventure.
- `session.command.unknown_objective` - `objective_id` matches no objective of
  that quest.
- `session.command.quest_state` - the quest isn't active, or the objective
  is already complete. The rejection includes the quest id and the state
  that caused the refusal.

**Events:**

`ObjectiveCompletedEvent` with
the quest id, the objective id, and the objective's progress text.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"complete_quest"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

quest_id.title: Quest Id
quest_id.description:
Which quest to complete, by
`QuestSpec.id`. It has to be active, and that's the only
check: whoever issues the command decides whether the objectives are done.

CompleteQuest.title: CompleteQuest
CompleteQuest.description:
Referee: complete an active quest, and the adventure when the quest concludes it.

The quest must be active, and that's the only check. The session doesn't check the
quest's objectives or its completion rule, because ruling a quest done is the
referee's call. The trigger and quest interpreter checks the rule before it issues this
command. The command accepts only the quest ids the adventure defines, as
`ActivateQuest` describes, and the `ActivateQuest`
example shows a quest from start to finish.

This command grants no rewards. Whoever completes the quest issues the quest's rewards
afterwards as separate commands, so a completion you send yourself grants nothing
unless you send the rewards too, and every reward granted is in the log. When the
quest's author wrote a `completion` text in its narrative, the completion adds that text
to the journal, and the events include it. No
`JournalEntryAddedEvent` follows.

Completing a quest whose spec sets `concludes_adventure` ends the adventure. The session
closes any open encounter and battle, and switches to `victory`. No other command enters
`victory`. When the session has already ended, in `game_over` or `victory`, the quest
still completes and its text still goes in the journal, but the mode doesn't change and
the session emits no `AdventureCompletedEvent`. This command is legal in every mode,
`game_over` and `victory` included.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.unknown_quest` - `quest_id` matches no quest of the
  adventure.
- `session.command.quest_state` - the quest is inactive or already
  completed. The rejection includes the quest id and its current state.

**Events:**

`QuestCompletedEvent` with the
quest id, the quest's name, and the completion text. An
`AdventureCompletedEvent`
with the same text follows when the quest concludes the adventure and the
session hadn't already ended.

Condition.title: Condition
Condition.description:
The closed set of named states a creature can be in, like asleep, charmed, or dead.

Check whether a creature has a condition with `has_condition`. To put
one on a creature for a while, set it as an `EffectDefinition`'s
`condition` and attach the definition with `EffectsLedger.attach`.
The ledger then takes the condition away when the duration runs out. Use
`grant_condition` only for a state that doesn't come from a timed effect.

Some members change rolls and actions in `osrlib.core.combat` and
`osrlib.core.spells`. Others matter only to the crawl procedures in
`osrlib.crawl` or to your own code. Each member's description lists where osrlib reads it, so
you know whether granting it changes a roll or only what your interface shows.

Immunity applies to every member. A monster whose template lists a condition in its defenses'
`condition_immunities` never takes that condition, whether you call
`grant_condition` or attach an effect that brings it. So even when no
other core rule reads a member, immunity limits which monsters a spell can affect.

The values are the lowercase strings, like `"asleep"`, and creatures and saved games contain them. A value
changes only with a `schema_version` bump.

visibility.description: Player visibility: a creature going rigid or falling asleep is plain to see.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The entity id of the creature that gained the condition.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: The condition, as a `Condition` value like `asleep` or `petrified`.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description:
The id of the effect that gave the condition and takes it away when it ends, or `null` for a condition
that doesn't come from an effect. In the core rules, that's `dead`.

ConditionGainedEvent.title: ConditionGainedEvent
ConditionGainedEvent.description:
A creature has fallen asleep, been turned to stone, or otherwise gained a condition.

A condition is a named state, from `Condition`, that changes what a creature
can do. `grant_condition` reports this, whether you called it yourself
or `EffectsLedger.attach` called it while attaching an effect that
gives a condition. It reports no event for a creature immune to the condition, or for one that already has it
from the same effect.

visibility.description: Player visibility: everyone can see a creature come out of a condition.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The entity id of the creature that lost the condition.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description: The id of the effect that gave the condition, or `null` for a condition that didn't come from an effect.

ConditionRemovedEvent.title: ConditionRemovedEvent
ConditionRemovedEvent.description:
A creature has lost a condition: it's awake again, no longer stone, no longer entangled.

`remove_condition` reports this, whether you called it yourself or an
`EffectsLedger` called it when the effect that gave the condition
expired or was released.

min_score.title: Min Score
min_score.description: The lowest score this row covers.

max_score.title: Max Score
max_score.description: The highest score this row covers. Equal to `min_score` on a one-score row.

hit_points.title: Hit Points
hit_points.description:
What to add to each Hit Die rolled, at creation and when a new level adds a die.

However negative this is, a die gives at least 1 hit point. Levels past name level
add a fixed number of hit points instead of a die, and this modifier doesn't apply to
them.

ConstitutionRow.title: ConstitutionRow
ConstitutionRow.description:
One row of the constitution table: a band of scores, with its hit point modifier.

Constitution grants no other bonus. Read the rows from
`AbilityTables.constitution` to draw the table. To
look up one score, call
`hit_point_modifier` instead.

label.title: Label
label.description:
Optional label for save menus, 1 to 200 characters without control characters, or `null` (the
default) for an unlabeled save.

character_ids.title: Character Ids
character_ids.description:
Stored character `id` values from `POST /v1/characters` or `GET /v1/characters` (1 to 20
entries), in marching order with the front rank first. Required unless `party_document` is set.
Sessions copy each character, so listing the same `id` twice creates two independent copies with
distinct in-session ids.

party_document.description:
Referee only. Party document envelope (`kind` set to `"party"`, `schema_version`,
`engine_version`, and `payload.characters` with 1 to 20 characters) as written by osrlib's
`party_to_document`. Mutually exclusive with `character_ids`.

name.title: Name
name.description:
Optional session display name, 1 to 200 characters without control characters. Defaults to the
adventure's `name` when omitted or `null`.

ruleset.description:
Optional B/X house-rule overrides as osrlib's `Ruleset`. Any omitted field uses the standard
1981 B/X rule as written.

anyOf.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

seed.title: Seed
seed.description:
Referee only. Master random seed (0 to 2^53 - 1) for every roll in the session. Omit to let
the server draw a random seed. Never returned outside a referee save document.

CreateSessionRequest.title: CreateSessionRequest
CreateSessionRequest.description:
Adventure, party, and optional ruleset and seed for starting a session.

Provide either `character_ids` or `party_document`, never both.

ability_rolls.description:
Six ability scores as rolled, before any `adjustment`, with the three dice that count toward
each in `rolls`. With the `4d6_drop_lowest` method, `dropped` has the fourth die of each
ability, and it's empty for a `3d6` roll. `sub_par` is `true` when the scores as rolled are
sub-par under the B/X rule that lets a referee allow a new roll.

hit_point_roll.description:
First-level hit point roll, including any rerolled dice and the Constitution modifier.
`maximized` is `true` when the ruleset's `max_hp_at_first_level` set the hit points to the hit
die's size plus the modifier, and `rolls` still lists every die thrown.

gold_roll.description: Starting gold roll (3d6 x 10 gp). Its `total` is the gold pieces before `purchases`.

CreationRolls.title: CreationRolls
CreationRolls.description: Dice rolled by osrlib while creating a first-level character.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the bearer learns about the curse when it takes hold.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `curse_revealed`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description: The member who has the cursed item.

instance_id.title: Instance Id
instance_id.description: The session-scoped id of the cursed item.

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description: What the item is, as its magic item catalog id.

item_names.title: Item Names
item_names.description:
What to call the item in `instance_id`, keyed by that id, such as `{"magic-item-0003": "ring of weakness"}`.
Each name is the name that `PlayerView.item_names` has for that id,
so an unidentified magic item has its masked name, such as `"potion"` or `"shield with a faint aura"`, and never
its true name. The curse is revealed only on an identified item, so the name is the item's true display name,
which names the item that `template_id` already identifies. A client that replays an event log, or that didn't
keep a view, can name the items from the event. It's empty on an event from a log written before the field
existed.

item_names_plural.title: Item Names Plural
item_names_plural.description:
What to call two or more of each item in `item_names`, with the same keys, such as
`{"magic-item-0003": "rings of weakness"}`, from
`PlayerView.item_names_plural`. Use it with a count of your
own.

CurseRevealedEvent.title: CurseRevealedEvent
CurseRevealedEvent.description:
The curse on a cursed item is now known, and the item can't be taken off.

Emitted when the party learns of a cursed item's curse: when the item is used, or worn
so that its curse takes hold, or when the referee identifies it with
`IdentifyItem`. It comes right after the
`ItemIdentifiedEvent` when the item wasn't
identified yet. From then on the member can't drop, give away, or unequip the item until
a *remove curse* lifts the curse.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the players see the hit land and do nothing.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The entity id of the creature the attack couldn't harm.

attacker_id.title: Attacker Id
attacker_id.description: The entity id of the attacker, or `null` when there was no attacker.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description:
What the target's defenses absorbed: the attack's keys, like `silver` or `magic`, then its element, like `fire`.

A torch and a dragon's fire breath both give `("fire",)`. A steel sword against a werewolf gives `()`, because
steel has no key.

DamageAbsorbedEvent.title: DamageAbsorbedEvent
DamageAbsorbedEvent.description:
A hit that did nothing, because the target can't be harmed by what hit it.

This comes instead of a `DamageDealtEvent` when the target is immune to
the damage, like a creature that only silver or magic can harm hit by a steel sword, or a creature immune to
the breath's element. No damage was rolled. Treat it as a hit that did nothing, not as a miss.

visibility.description: Player visibility: everyone sees how hard a creature was hit.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The entity id of the creature that took the damage.

attacker_id.title: Attacker Id
attacker_id.description: The entity id of the attacker, or `null` when there was no attacker, as for a fall or a trap.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: The hit points the target lost, after all its reductions.

rolls.title: Rolls
rolls.description: Each damage die as rolled, before modifiers. Empty for damage that wasn't rolled, like a dragon's breath.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description:
The keys of the damage that the target's defenses check: keys like `silver`, `magic`, or `holy`, then the
damage's element, like `fire`, when it had one.

non_regenerable.title: Non Regenerable
non_regenerable.description:
True when the target regenerates and this damage's element stops its regeneration.

Fire and acid do that to a troll, and to a character who wears a ring of regeneration. The target's regeneration
can't heal this damage. Once enough of it adds up, a troll stays dead.

DamageDealtEvent.title: DamageDealtEvent
DamageDealtEvent.description:
Damage dealt to a creature.

`deal_damage` reports one of these each time it deals damage, whether the
damage came from a weapon, a spell, or an effect like burning oil.

It reports how much damage was dealt and never how many hit points the target has left, because in B/X only
the referee sees monster hit points. The hit points left are in the
`HitPointsReportedEvent` that follows it, which only the referee
sees.

DamageKey.title: DamageKey
DamageKey.description:
A kind of damage source that a monster's defenses can list.

For a monster that only certain kinds of attack can hurt,
`Defenses.harmed_only_by` lists them. For a
monster that takes reduced damage from a kind,
`DamageReduction.keys` lists it. The damage rules
compare these with the keys and the element of the attack's
`DamageSource`.

`holy` works differently from the others. Holy water presents it, and against an undead target
it gets past any `harmed_only_by` list, because in the SRD holy water harms undead. Without that
exception, the wight's silver-or-magic list would stop holy water. Against a target that isn't
undead, a `holy` source does no damage.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description:
Which sources of damage are reduced.

Empty means every source that gets past `harmed_only_by`, as with the mummy, which takes half
damage from everything. A list of keys limits the reduction to sources that present one of
them, as with the wraith, which takes half damage from silver weapons only.

divisor.title: Divisor
divisor.description: What the damage is divided by, 2 or more. The SRD prints only halving, which is 2.

DamageReduction.title: DamageReduction
DamageReduction.description:
A reduction of the damage a monster takes, applied after the dice are rolled.

Read them from `Defenses.reductions`.
`deal_damage` divides the damage by `divisor` and rounds
down, and a hit that gets through always does at least 1 point. Frozen.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: everyone sees a creature fall.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The entity id of the creature that died.

poison.title: Poison
poison.description:
Whether poison killed the creature, such as a viper's bite, a poison needle, or a potion of poison.

The save versus death covers death ray and poison alike, so a failed save of that category doesn't say which
killed. Read this field instead. The session records a member's death as a poison death when it's True, and
*neutralize poison* revives only a character who died of poison. The event has player visibility, so the players
learn that poison killed the creature, as a referee at the table would tell them that the needle was poisoned.
It's False on an event loaded from a save written before the field existed.

DeathEvent.title: DeathEvent
DeathEvent.description:
A creature has been killed.

`kill` reports this, whether the death came from damage, a failed save, or an
effect running out. It comes after the `ConditionGainedEvent` for
`dead`, and before the `HitPointsReportedEvent`.

`deal_damage` reports a second one, with the code `combat.death.permanent`,
when the damage a dead monster can't regenerate adds up to its maximum hit points. That one
comes after the `HitPointsReportedEvent`, with no condition event, because the monster is already `dead`.

Read the code to know whether the death can be undone. An ordinary death can be, by magic or by regeneration. A
permanent one can't, which is what enough fire and acid do to a troll.

round.title: Round
round.description:
Where the clock stood at the death, in rounds since the session began. Both revival windows
are measured from here.

cause.title: Cause
cause.description:
What killed the character: `"poison"`, `"damage"`, or `"unknown"`.

It's `"poison"` when the character's `DeathEvent` has `poison`
set. Every death by poison sets it: a monster's poison, at once or when its onset runs out, a
sea dragon's spittle, a potion of poison, and a trap whose
`TrapEffect.poison` is set. An effect whose `expiry` is
`"death"` kills by poison only when its `kind`
contains `poison`. A failed save versus death
alone never makes it `"poison"`, because that save covers death ray as well. For any other
death, the session reads the events of the command that killed the character, up to the death.
It's `"damage"` when the character took damage after their last failed saving throw among them, and
`"unknown"` otherwise, as for *finger of death*. Only *neutralize poison* treats `"poison"`
differently from the other causes.

DeathRecord.title: DeathRecord
DeathRecord.description:
When and how one party member died, recorded for the spells that bring the dead back.

The session writes one into
`GameSession.death_records`, keyed by
character id, as soon as a party member dies. The engine reads it when a character casts a
revival spell. *Neutralize poison* works only when poison was the cause, and only within a window
measured in rounds. *Raise dead* counts the days since the death.

The record is frozen. A member who dies again gets a new record, which replaces the old one.

visibility.description: Player visibility: everyone sees the action fail.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

actor_id.title: Actor Id
actor_id.description:
The entity id of the member who declared the device use, the potion, the hand-over, the turning, or the
melee attack.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description:
The item the declaration's `item_id` gave, on a `magic.device.fizzled`, a `magic.potion.fizzled`, or a
`battle.give.fizzled` event: a device's or a potion's instance id, or the id of the item a hand-over moves.

The player already used this id, so it reveals nothing about an item that isn't identified. It's `null` on a
`magic.turning.fizzled` or a `battle.melee.fizzled` event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description:
On a `magic.potion.fizzled` or a `battle.give.fizzled` event, the id of the member the potion or the item
was for, the one id in the declaration's `targets`. It's `null` on the other codes, and on an event from a log
written before the field existed.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description:
On a `battle.melee.fizzled` event, the id of the group the melee attack was aimed at, as the declaration's
`target_group_id` gave it. It's `null` on the other codes.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description:
Why the declaration fizzled: the code of the first check that failed when the session checked it again.
