Any check the declaration passed at the start of the round can fail, so read the code and don't assume a
cause. Some codes you may see:

- `combat.attack.out_of_reach`: the member who declared a melee attack, or a strike with a staff, is farther
  than 5' from its group when the blow comes up. Either one gets it too when its group ran out of the battle,
  wherever the member stood.
- `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank`: the member who declared a melee attack is within 5' of its group
  but not in its front rank when the attack comes up. A melee attack gets this code only when the member is
  within 5', and `combat.attack.out_of_reach` otherwise.
- `battle.declaration.unknown_group`: the group a wand was aimed at left the battle.
- `battle.declaration.no_target`: no living monster is left in the battle for a turning, or no living monster
  the member can see is left in the group a melee attack was aimed at, for example because the party's missiles
  or spells killed them earlier in the round. A melee attack gets this code wherever the member stands, whether
  or not the member closed, because the session checks for a target before it checks the member's position.
- `items.use.target_cannot_drink`: the member a potion was for died or turned to stone earlier in the round.
- `session.command.member_incapacitated`: the member a hand-over was for can no longer act, for example
  because the member died or fell asleep earlier in the round.
- `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach`: the two members of a potion, a hand-over, or a staff of healing's
  touch no longer stand within 5' of each other.
- `items.use.target_cannot_be_healed` and `items.use.target_healed_today`: the creature a staff of healing
  was to touch died or turned to stone, or the staff already healed it today.

Match on it as you match on the code of a `Rejection`.
The rejection code reference explains each code.

item_names.title: Item Names
item_names.description:
What to call the item in `item_id`, keyed by that id, such as `{"magic-item-0003": "wand"}`. Each name is the
name that `PlayerView.item_names` has for that id, so an
unidentified magic item has its masked name, such as `"potion"` or `"shield with a faint aura"`, and never its
true name. A fizzled declaration identifies nothing, so an unidentified item keeps its masked name. It's empty
on a `magic.turning.fizzled` or a `battle.melee.fizzled` event, which has no item, and on a
`battle.give.fizzled` event whose item has left the party. A client that replays an event log, or that didn't
keep a view, can name the items from the event. It's also empty on an event from a log written before the field
existed.

item_names_plural.title: Item Names Plural
item_names_plural.description:
What to call two or more of each item in `item_names`, with the same keys, such as
`{"magic-item-0003": "wands"}`, from
`PlayerView.item_names_plural`. Use it with a count of your
own.

DeclarationFizzledEvent.title: DeclarationFizzledEvent
DeclarationFizzledEvent.description:
A declared item use, hand-over, turning, or melee attack failed before it took effect.

A `GameSession` reports it during a battle round. At the start of each
round, every party member declares an action in a
`BattleDeclaration`. A turning is a cleric's attempt to turn undead.
Device uses, potions, hand-overs, and turnings resolve in the round's magic phase, the step in which the
party's spells, item uses, and turnings take effect. A device is a wand, a staff, or a rod. A staff's strike
is the exception, described below. Just before each one resolves, the session checks it again. If a check the
declaration passed at the start of the round now fails, the declaration fizzles. Something earlier in the
round caused the failure. For example, the group a wand was aimed at left the battle.

A potion that one member gives another to drink fizzles with the code `magic.potion.fizzled` when the drinker
died or turned to stone, or the two members no longer stand within 5' of each other. A potion the carrier
drinks never fizzles. A `give_item` hand-over fizzles with the code `battle.give.fizzled` when the recipient
can no longer act, or the two members no longer stand within 5' of each other. Either event has the item in
`item_id` and the member it was for in `target_id`.

A melee attack fizzles when the party's melee step comes and the attack has nothing left to strike, or the
member stands in the wrong place. The session judges a melee attack before the round starts, as if every move the
round declares had happened. When the attack comes up, it resolves only if its group still has a living monster
the member can see to strike, and the member stands in the group's front rank within 5' of it. Something earlier
in the round can change either. For example, the party's missiles or spells kill every monster in the group, the
monsters win initiative and the group runs before the member's `close`, or a member the session expected to step
back can no longer move. Then the attack fizzles with the code `battle.melee.fizzled`. A group that has started to
flee is an exception to the position check: a member who stood within 5' of it when the round was accepted still
gets the attack, if the group has a monster left to strike and hasn't run out of the battle.

A staff's strike for a charge, with the staff of power, striking, or wizardry, is a melee attack with a slow
weapon. So it doesn't resolve in the magic phase. It comes up after both sides have acted, as a slow attack
does, and it fizzles where a slow melee attack does. The session checks it when the party's melee step comes
and again when the strike comes up, with a melee attack's checks and reasons. A strike is still a device use,
so a strike that fizzles has the code `magic.device.fizzled`, with the staff in `item_id`. For example, the
strike's group ran out of the battle, or a quicker member killed the last monster in it that the member could
see.

The event's `actor_id` is the member who declared the action, `item_id` is the device, the potion, or the item
handed over, `target_id` is the member a potion or a hand-over was for, `group_id` is the group a melee attack
was aimed at, and `reason` is the rejection code of the check that failed.

A fizzled declaration spends nothing and draws nothing. The device wasn't used, so it keeps its charge and isn't
identified. Tell the player the action failed, and that the device still has its charge. A potion that fizzles
stays with the member who carries it and isn't identified, and an item that wasn't handed over stays with the
giver. A fizzled melee attack makes no attack roll, so tell the player why the member didn't swing. When a cast
or a scroll read fizzles, the session reports a `SpellDisruptedEvent`
instead, because the spell is lost.

monster_id.title: Monster Id
monster_id.description: The session id of the creature that was defeated.

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description: What it was: a monster catalog id, or `"npc:<class id>"` for an NPC adventurer.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: How it went out: `"slain"` or `"routed"`. Both count as defeated for the award.

xp.title: Xp
xp.description: What it's worth in experience points.

DefeatedMonsterRecord.title: DefeatedMonsterRecord
DefeatedMonsterRecord.description:
One defeated creature, kept until the session awards its experience.

When an encounter ends, the session appends one for each defeated creature to
`GameSession.defeated_monsters`.
`GameSession.award_adventure_xp`
adds up their `xp` and clears the list when the party returns to town. Under a ruleset that
awards experience immediately, the session awards it and clears the list at the end of each
encounter instead.

Its fields contain the same facts as
`MonsterDefeatedEvent`.

harmed_only_by.title: Harmed Only By
harmed_only_by.description:
The kinds of damage that can hurt this creature at all.

An attack that presents none of them is absorbed, and no damage is rolled. That is how a wight
ignores an ordinary sword. Empty means anything hurts it.

reductions.title: Reductions
reductions.description:
Reductions of the damage that does get through. See
`DamageReduction`.

energy.title: Energy
energy.description:
How the creature resists each kind of energy, keyed by element. See
`EnergyDefense`. An element with no entry hurts it as usual.

condition_immunities.title: Condition Immunities
condition_immunities.description:
Conditions the creature can never be put into, like the undead's immunity to being poisoned, charmed, or put
to sleep. `grant_condition` grants nothing when you try.

Defenses.title: Defenses
Defenses.description:
What a monster resists, in the form the damage rules check.

Read it as `MonsterTemplate.defenses`. Every
time an attack hits, `check_immunity` reads it before any
damage is rolled, and `deal_damage` applies the reductions.
The SRD's wording for the same defenses is in the template's `abilities`, for you to show.
Frozen.

food_days.title: Food Days
food_days.description: Consecutive days this member has gone without food.

water_days.title: Water Days
water_days.description: Consecutive days this member has gone without water.

DeprivationState.title: DeprivationState
DeprivationState.description:
How long one member has gone without food and without water.

The session stores these in
`GameSession.deprivation`. Each time the clock
passes into a new game day, the session updates one for each living member, and creates it on that
member's first day. A day the member eats resets `food_days` to zero, and a day without food
adds one. Water works the same way for `water_days`. Whether the counts bring a
penalty depends on the ruleset option `deprivation_penalties`, described in
[the adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/),
the page that lists where osrlib settles an ambiguous rule or supplies a default.

thac0.title: Thac0
thac0.description: Attack roll needed on 1d20 to hit descending armour class 0.

attack_bonus.title: Attack Bonus
attack_bonus.description: Bonus added to 1d20 attack rolls against ascending armour class, equivalent to `thac0`.

armour_class.title: Armour Class
armour_class.description: Descending armour class, where lower numbers are harder to hit.

armour_class_ascending.title: Armour Class Ascending
armour_class_ascending.description: Ascending armour class, where higher numbers are harder to hit.

saves.description: Target numbers on 1d20 for the five saving throw categories at the character's level.

melee_modifier.title: Melee Modifier
melee_modifier.description: Strength modifier applied to melee attack and damage rolls.

open_doors_chance.title: Open Doors Chance
open_doors_chance.description: Chance on 1d6 (from 1 to 5) of forcing open a stuck door, derived from Strength.

missile_modifier.title: Missile Modifier
missile_modifier.description: Dexterity modifier applied to missile attack rolls.

initiative_modifier.title: Initiative Modifier
initiative_modifier.description: Dexterity modifier applied to individual initiative when `individual_initiative` is enabled.

hit_point_modifier.title: Hit Point Modifier
hit_point_modifier.description: Constitution modifier applied to each hit die roll.

magic_save_modifier.title: Magic Save Modifier
magic_save_modifier.description: Wisdom modifier applied to saving throws against magic.

npc_reaction_modifier.title: Npc Reaction Modifier
npc_reaction_modifier.description: Charisma modifier applied to monster and NPC reaction rolls when this character speaks.

xp_modifier_pct.title: Xp Modifier Pct
xp_modifier_pct.description:
Percentage bonus or penalty applied to earned experience points, such as `10` for +10%,
derived from the class's prime requisites.

level_title.title: Level Title
level_title.description:
Traditional title for the character's class and level, such as `"Veteran"`, or `null` above
title level.

alignment_tongue.title: Alignment Tongue
alignment_tongue.description: Language `id` of the character's alignment tongue, such as `"alignment_lawful"`.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description:
All language `id` values the character speaks: alignment tongue, class languages, and
`extra_languages`.

DerivedValues.title: DerivedValues
DerivedValues.description: Combat, saving throw, modifier, and language values computed by osrlib from a `Character`.

visibility.description: Referee visibility: the roll is the part the referee keeps hidden from the players.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `detection_rolled`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
The member who rolled, or `null` for a check that isn't a member's, like a trap's chance to
go off.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
What was being checked: `"listening"`, one of the search kinds
(`"secret_doors"`, `"room_traps"`, `"construction"`), `"open_locks"`, `"treasure_traps"`,
`"hide_in_shadows"`, `"move_silently"`, or `"trap_spring"` for a trap's chance to fire.

chance.title: Chance
chance.description:
The number the roll had to come in at or under. The listening, search, and trap-spring
kinds are X-in-6 chances rolled on a d6. The thief skills `open_locks`, `treasure_traps`,
`hide_in_shadows`, and `move_silently` are percentages rolled on d100. The default message
from `format_message` gives a percentage as one, like
`38 vs 45%`, and an X-in-6 chance as one, like `1 vs 2-in-6`.

roll.title: Roll
roll.description:
What came up, or `null` when the chance was zero and no die was rolled, as for a character
with no chance at all of noticing construction tricks.

passed.title: Passed
passed.description:
Whether the check succeeded. From the player's side, a failed check and a cell with nothing
in it look the same.

DetectionRolledEvent.title: DetectionRolledEvent
DetectionRolledEvent.description:
A hidden die roll for a search, a listen, a thief skill, or a trap's chance to spring.

Emitted by `Search`,
`ListenAtDoor`,
`PickLock`,
`InspectTreasure`, and
`RemoveTreasureTrap`, ahead of any
player-visible result, and whenever a trap gets its chance to spring.
`ResolveBattleRound` emits it for a thief's
hide in shadows roll when a `hide` resolves, and for the move silently roll when a
back-stab from hiding comes up.

The session rolls the die for a search or a listen whether or not there's anything to
find, so a failed roll and an empty cell look the same to the players. That is why this
event has referee visibility: showing it to players would tell them whether the roll
failed. A referee front end, or an LLM running the game, reads it to know what happened.

min_score.title: Min Score
min_score.description: The lowest score this row covers.

max_score.title: Max Score
max_score.description: The highest score this row covers. Equal to `min_score` on a one-score row.

ac.title: Ac
ac.description: The armour class bonus. Subtract it from a descending armour class, or add it to an ascending one.

missile.title: Missile
missile.description: What to add to a missile attack roll. It doesn't change missile damage.

initiative.title: Initiative
initiative.description:
What to add to an individual initiative roll.

It applies only when the `individual_initiative` flag on
`Ruleset` is on. Otherwise each side rolls initiative
once.

DexterityRow.title: DexterityRow
DexterityRow.description:
One row of the dexterity table: a band of scores, with its armour class, missile, and initiative modifiers.

Read the rows from `AbilityTables.dexterity` to draw
the table. To look up one score, call
`ac_modifier`,
`missile_modifier`, or
`initiative_modifier` instead.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description:
Dice expression such as `3d6`, `d%`, `1d6+1`, or `2d6+1x10`.

Format: `[count]d<sides>[+|-<modifier>][x|×|*<multiplier>]`. `count` is 1 to 999 (defaults to
1). `sides` is `2`, `3`, `4`, `6`, `8`, `10`, `12`, `20`, `100`, or `%` (`d100`). `modifier` is
at most 999,999 in magnitude and applies before `multiplier` (1 to 999,999), so `2d6+1x10`
computes `(2d6 + 1) × 10`. osrlib ignores leading and trailing whitespace and letter case, while
rejecting internal spaces and leading zeros with 422 `content_invalid`.

times.title: Times
times.description: Number of independent rolls of `expression` to make, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 1.

anyOf.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

seed.title: Seed
seed.description:
Optional seed (0 to 2^53 - 1) for deterministic results. Pass the `seed` from an earlier
response with the same `expression` and `times` to repeat the roll, or omit it to let the
server draw a random seed.

DiceRollRequest.title: DiceRollRequest
DiceRollRequest.description: Dice expression, roll count, and optional seed for a stateless roll.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: Dice expression from the request, unchanged.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

rolls.title: Rolls
rolls.description:
One `RollResult` per roll (`times` entries in roll order), each containing individual die
values in `rolls`, `modifier`, `multiplier`, and `total`.

DiceRollResponse.title: DiceRollResponse
DiceRollResponse.description: Rolled dice results and the seed that produced them.

visibility.description: Referee visibility: the referee decides what to share.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `dice_rolled`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: What was rolled, as the dice expression that was asked for, like `"2d6+1"`.

total.title: Total
total.description: The result, dice and modifier together.

rolls.title: Rolls
rolls.description:
Each die's result, in roll order, so you can show the dice in a transcript rather than
only the sum.

DiceRolledEvent.title: DiceRolledEvent
DiceRolledEvent.description:
The referee rolled dice for something the rules don't cover.

Emitted by `RollDice`. The dice come from
`ADJUDICATION_STREAM`, which the session
uses for no other roll, so a referee rolling for weather or a rumour never changes the
dice for a later attack or save.

It has referee visibility, because a referee's roll may be secret. Show it to the
players yourself when you roll in the open.

Direction.title: Direction
Direction.description:
The four grid directions the party faces and moves in.

You use these for the way `MoveParty` steps, the side of a
cell `OpenDoor` works on, and the way a transition turns the
party on arrival. There is no up or down. A
`TransitionSpec` moves the party between levels.

The values are lowercase strings, like `"north"`, and they appear in commands, events, and saves.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility, except on an event from the referee's `SetDoorState`, which is referee.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `door`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

x.title: X
x.description:
The column of the cell the door is named from. For a door command it's the party's cell,
for `SetDoorState` it's the cell given in the command, and for a door swinging shut it's the cell
on the door's south or east side.

y.title: Y
y.description: The row of the cell the door is named from, chosen the same way as `x`.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description:
Which side of that cell the door is on, as a lowercase
`Direction` value.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
The member who forced the door, failed to force it, or picked its lock. `null` for the other
codes, where the party acts as one or nobody acts.

narrative.title: Narrative
narrative.description:
The success text the author wrote on the door's gate, when opening the door passed one, or
`null`. The author wrote this text, not the engine, and
`format_message` adds it after the line it builds from the
code.

DoorEvent.title: DoorEvent
DoorEvent.description:
A door changed state. The event identifies the door by a cell and the side of the cell it's on.

Emitted by the door commands,
`OpenDoor`,
`CloseDoor`,
`ForceDoor`,
`PickLock`, and
`WedgeDoor`. A door the party opened swings shut
once the party walks away from it, unless it's wedged, so a command that moves the
party, like `MoveParty`,
`UseStairs`, or
`TravelToTown`, can emit it too. A referee's
`SetDoorState` emits it at referee visibility
when it opens or closes a door, because the party didn't see that happen.

A door belongs to the edge between two cells, so you can refer to the same door from
either side. Redraw the door from `x`, `y`, and `direction` rather than keeping your
own record of which door is which.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
`"normal"` for a door the party can see, or `"secret"` for one it has to find. A secret door is
hidden until the party finds it with a `Search` for secret
doors, which sets `discovered` in the door's `DoorState`. Until then the party
can't open it, listen at it, or walk through it, and the player view shows the edge as a wall.

stuck.title: Stuck
stuck.description:
Whether the door is stuck shut. The session refuses `OpenDoor`
on a stuck door, so the party has to force it open with
`ForceDoor`. Forcing is a Strength-based roll, and it makes
noise whether or not it works. The session refuses `ForceDoor` on a door that isn't stuck.

locked.title: Locked
locked.description:
Whether the door is locked. The session refuses both `OpenDoor`
and `ForceDoor` on a locked door until it is unlocked, by a
thief's `PickLock` or by a referee's
`SetDoorState`. A door that is both locked and stuck has to
be unlocked and then forced.

starts_open.title: Starts Open
starts_open.description:
Whether the door stands open at the start of the game. Doors that the party opens swing shut
behind it as it walks on, but a door that starts open doesn't, because the party didn't open it.
The party can still close it with `CloseDoor`.

requires.description:
A gate on opening the door, or `null` for a door that opens without one. A gate
(`GateSpec`) is a condition, like carrying a key, that the
session checks each time the party tries to open or force the door. The session checks it last,
after every other reason to refuse the command. It is separate from `locked`: to open a locked door with a gate,
the party has to unlock it and meet the gate's condition. `PickLock` deals only
with the lock, and `SetDoorState` changes the door without
checking the gate. The gate guards opening the door, not passing through it, so the party walks
through a door that stands open without a check. Once the door is closed again, the gate applies
to the next opening.

DoorSpec.title: DoorSpec
DoorSpec.description:
A door on an edge, as you wrote it.

Put one in the `door` field of an `Edge` whose `kind` is `door`.
Every field is the door's state at the start of the game, and play never changes it. What the
party does to the door goes into a `DoorState` in the overlay
instead, so read the overlay to find out whether a door is open now.

open.title: Open
open.description:
Whether the door stands open now. The party walks through an open door without opening it. A
door whose spec sets `starts_open` is open until something closes it.

wedged.title: Wedged
wedged.description:
Whether an iron spike holds the door, from `WedgeDoor`. A
wedged door doesn't swing shut behind the party, and the party can't close it.

discovered.title: Discovered
discovered.description:
Whether the party has found a secret door. Until a `Search`
for secret doors sets it, a `secret` door is a wall to the party. It has no effect on a normal
door.

unlocked.title: Unlocked
unlocked.description:
Whether a locked door has been unlocked, by a thief's
`PickLock` or by a referee's
`SetDoorState`. Closing the door doesn't lock it again. Only a
`SetDoorState` can.

opened_by_party.title: Opened By Party
opened_by_party.description:
Whether the party opened this door, with `OpenDoor` or
`ForceDoor`. Only a door the party opened swings shut behind
it, so a door that starts open, or that a referee opened, stays open.

DoorState.title: DoorState
DoorState.description:
What has happened to one door in play: open, wedged, discovered, unlocked.

This is the part of a door that changes. The `DoorSpec` is how
you wrote the door, and it never changes. A `DoorState` records what the party and the referee
have done to it since. Get one from `DungeonState.door`
with the door's `edge_ref`.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"drop_items"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
The member whose pack and purse the goods leave, by
`MemberView.id`.

item_ids.title: Item Ids
item_ids.description:
What to drop, one unit per entry, so repeat an id to drop more than one. Name a mundane
item by its catalog id, like `torch` or `rope_hemp`. Name a magic item, a gem, or a piece
of jewellery by the per-instance id it has in
`MemberView.inventory`. The session refuses
the same magic item, gem, or piece of jewellery named twice with
`exploration.item.not_carried`, because the whole item leaves with the first entry. A cursed
item whose curse has been revealed can't be dropped.

coins.description:
Coins to drop with the items, by denomination. The default drops none. Coins dropped on
the cell go into its pile with everything else, and the party can pick them back up with
`TakeTreasure` naming `"pile"`.

DropItems.title: DropItems
DropItems.description:
Drop items and coins from one member onto the party's cell, or behind a fleeing party.

It's legal while exploring a dungeon and during an encounter. Goods dropped on the cell
go into its pile, and `TakeTreasure` with
`feature_id="pile"` picks them back up. While exploring, a drop takes no time.

During an encounter, the drop uses up the encounter round, and the monsters then act on
their reaction to the party, as for a `Wait`. While
monsters pursue the party after an
`Evade`, dropped goods scatter behind the party instead of
landing in a pile, and can't be picked back up. Dropped coins tempt intelligent pursuers
and dropped rations tempt unintelligent ones, which can end the pursuit.

Modes:

`exploring`, `encounter`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the session is in town or in battle, or has
  ended.
- `session.command.unknown_member` - `character_id` matches no party member.
- `session.command.member_incapacitated` - the member can't act.
- `items.curse.stuck` - a cursed item whose curse has been revealed can't be
  dropped.
- `exploration.item.not_carried` - the member doesn't carry one of the items, or
  enough of the coins.
- `encounter.none_active` - a second check behind the mode gate, which normal
  play never reaches.

**Events:**

`ItemsDroppedEvent` with what
was dropped. In an encounter, the encounter round's events follow. During a pursuit,
a `PursuitEvent` round follows instead, with
the drop as bait.

items.title: Items
items.description: The ordinary items lying here, one stack for each template id.

coins.description: The coins lying here, by denomination.

valuables.title: Valuables
valuables.description: The gems and jewellery lying here, each with the id it had before it was dropped.

magic_items.title: Magic Items
magic_items.description: The magic items lying here, each with the charges or quantity it had before it was dropped.

DropPile.title: DropPile
DropPile.description:
What lies on one cell's floor, waiting to be picked up.

Loose goods end up in piles: gear the party drops with
`DropItems`, what slain monsters leave at the end of an
encounter, and the part of a cache the party couldn't carry. The party picks up a whole pile with
`TakeTreasure` and the feature id `"pile"`, which is why no
feature you write can use that id. Goods the party drops to distract monsters that chase it are
the exception: they are gone, not dropped in a pile.

The session keeps piles in `DungeonState.piles`, keyed
by `cell_ref`. A pile forms only on a cell where the party has
stood, so the party knows about every pile.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The item's template id, from the built-in equipment catalog or the adventure's `items`.

quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.description:
How many are in the stack, at least 1. The session removes a stack from the pile when it runs
out.

DroppedItem.title: DroppedItem
DroppedItem.description:
One stack of an ordinary item lying on the floor.

A `DropPile` contains these. Identical items stack, so five iron
spikes are one entry with a quantity of 5, not five entries.

pattern_type.title: Pattern Type
pattern_type.description:
The discriminator value, `dungeon_entered`. It appears in the document, and you
never set it yourself.

dungeon_id.title: Dungeon Id
dungeon_id.description: The id of the dungeon the party crossed into.

DungeonEnteredPattern.title: DungeonEnteredPattern
DungeonEnteredPattern.description:
A pattern that matches the party crossing into a dungeon, from town or another dungeon.

It matches a `LocationEnteredEvent` for a
dungeon. Use it to react to the party entering the dungeon, and
`LevelEnteredPattern` to react to the party
reaching a particular level.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Dungeon identifier within the adventure. Pass as `dungeon_id` in the `enter_dungeon` command
on `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Dungeon display name, or `""` when none is set.

DungeonInfo.title: DungeonInfo
DungeonInfo.description: Player-visible summary of one dungeon in an adventure, omitting level counts and maps.

id.title: Id
id.description: The dungeon id from the adventure.

name.title: Name
name.description: The dungeon's display name.

DungeonNameView.title: DungeonNameView
DungeonNameView.description: The public identity of a dungeon the party has entered.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The dungeon's id, unique within the adventure. You use it in
`EnterDungeon`, the town's `travel_turns`, and transitions
between dungeons, and every reference in the overlay includes it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The dungeon's name, to show the player, like `"The Old Crypt"`.

levels.title: Levels
levels.description:
The dungeon's levels, at least one, each with a unique `number`. Look a level up by its number
with `level`, not by its position in the tuple. Only
`EnterDungeon` depends on the order: it puts the party on the
entrance of the first level in this tuple that has one, facing north.

DungeonSpec.title: DungeonSpec
DungeonSpec.description:
A dungeon: one or more levels joined by transitions.

An `Adventure` contains its dungeons, and
`EnterDungeon` takes the party into one by its id. Build the
levels first, put them in a dungeon, then put the dungeon in an adventure with its town. An
adventure can have several dungeons, and a
`TransitionSpec` can lead to another dungeon's id, so a
stair can lead out of one dungeon and into the next.

A dungeon has no field for its way in. One of its levels needs an `entrance`, and
`validate_adventure` checks that one does.

location.description: Where the party is: in town, or on a dungeon cell. A new session starts in town.

explored.title: Explored
explored.description:
The cells the party has walked into, as lists of positions keyed `"{dungeon}:{level}"`. The
session uses it for movement cost: a step into an explored cell takes a third of the time of a
step into a new one. The player view also shows only the drop piles on explored cells.

seen.title: Seen
seen.description:
The cells the party's light has shown it, as lists of positions keyed `"{dungeon}:{level}"`.
It is what the party remembers of the map. Only the player view reads it, and it never affects
movement cost. `mark_seen` adds new cells in
sorted `(x, y)` order, so the same game always saves the same bytes.

doors.title: Doors
doors.description:
Each door's `DoorState`, keyed by
`edge_ref`. A door gets an entry the first time it changes in
play, so an unchanged door has none. Read one through
`door`.

sprung_traps.title: Sprung Traps
sprung_traps.description:
The traps that have sprung, as area or feature references. A sprung trap never springs
again.

removed_traps.title: Removed Traps
removed_traps.description:
The treasure traps a thief has taken out with
`RemoveTreasureTrap`, as feature references. A removed
trap never springs. Room traps never appear here, because there is no way to disarm one.

found_traps.title: Found Traps
found_traps.description:
The traps the party has found, as area or feature references: room traps from a
`Search`, and treasure traps from a thief's
`InspectTreasure`. A room trap here no longer springs. A
treasure trap here can still spring when the party opens the cache, and it has to be here before
`RemoveTreasureTrap` can take it out.

trap_doors.title: Trap Doors
trap_doors.description:
The doors at which the party learned of an open-trigger room trap, as lists of
`edge_ref` values keyed by the trap's area reference. A
`Search` that finds the trap through a door adds that door, and
opening a door that springs the trap adds that door. The player view reads it for
`EdgeView.trap_state`. A save from osrlib 2.11.0 has
none, so a trap that such a save found or sprung at a door shows on that door only once the party
walks the trapped area's cell beside it.

found_tricks.title: Found Tricks
found_tricks.description:
The construction tricks the party has found with a
`Search` for construction, as feature references.

emptied_caches.title: Emptied Caches
emptied_caches.description:
The caches you wrote that the party has emptied, as feature references. The party gets nothing
more from an emptied cache. A cache the session rolled isn't listed here. The session removes it
from `generated_caches` instead.

piles.title: Piles
piles.description:
What lies on the floor, keyed by `cell_ref`. See
`DropPile`.

generated_caches.title: Generated Caches
generated_caches.description:
Treasure the session rolled, keyed by cache id, like `"cache-0001"`. A
`HoardGeneratedEvent` reports the id,
`TakeTreasure` with that id takes the cache, and taking it
removes the entry. See `GeneratedCache`.

generated_treasure_areas.title: Generated Treasure Areas
generated_treasure_areas.description:
The areas whose `AreaTreasureSpec` the session has
already rolled, as area references, so the session doesn't roll a room's treasure again when the
party enters it a second time.

generated_lair_hoards.title: Generated Lair Hoards
generated_lair_hoards.description:
The areas whose `KeyedEncounter` hoard the session has
already rolled, as area references.

The session rolls a lair's hoard the first time the party meets its monsters. If the party leaves
and comes back, the monsters spawn again, but the session doesn't roll the hoard again. The party
finds the cache from the first visit, or nothing if it took that cache.

resolved_encounters.title: Resolved Encounters
resolved_encounters.description:
The areas whose keyed encounter ended with every monster slain or routed, as area references.
When the party enters one of these areas again, no monsters spawn.

listen_attempts.title: Listen Attempts
listen_attempts.description:
Which characters have listened at each door, as lists of character ids keyed by
`edge_ref`. Each character gets one try at each door, so a bad
roll stands.

search_attempts.title: Search Attempts
search_attempts.description:
Which characters have searched each cell for each kind of thing, as lists of character ids
keyed `"{cell_ref}:{kind}"`. The kind is the `kind` of the
`Search`, like `"cell:crypt:1:2,3:secret_doors"`. Each character
gets one try for each kind on each cell.

inspect_attempts.title: Inspect Attempts
inspect_attempts.description:
Which characters have inspected each cache for traps, as lists of character ids keyed by
feature reference. Each character gets one try at each cache.

removal_attempts.title: Removal Attempts
removal_attempts.description:
Which characters have tried to remove each treasure trap, as lists of character ids keyed by
feature reference. Each character gets one try at each trap. A failed try springs the trap, unless
`Ruleset.failed_trap_removal_springs` is off.

lock_failures.title: Lock Failures
lock_failures.description:
Which thieves failed to pick each lock, keyed by `edge_ref`.
Each value maps a character id to the thief's level at the time. A thief who failed a lock can
try it again after gaining a level, so the session records the level.

DungeonState.title: DungeonState
DungeonState.description:
Everything that play has changed in the dungeons: the overlay the session keeps beside the content.

The adventure you wrote never changes. The running session records what happens to it here, and
a save contains it. `GameSession.new` creates one, and the
command handlers change it. Read it through
`GameSession.view` instead of reading the session's
copy, so each audience sees only what it is allowed to see. The referee view's `dungeon_state`
is a copy of it.

The overlay refers to content by strings, not by object, so it serializes as flat data and never
repeats the adventure. It uses four formats of key:

- `"{dungeon}:{level}"` keys `explored` and `seen`, like `"crypt:1"`.
- `edge_ref` keys doors, like `"crypt:1:1,0:west"`.
- `"{dungeon}:{level}:{id}"` is an *area reference* or a *feature reference*, to an area or a
  feature you wrote, like `"crypt:1:shrine"`.
- `cell_ref` keys drop piles, like `"cell:crypt:1:2,3"`.

`explored` and `seen` are both maps of cells, and they mean different things. `explored` contains
the cells the party has walked into, and the session uses it for movement cost. `seen` contains the
cells the party's light has shown it, and only the player view reads it, so a map can still show
a room the party looked into and walked past.

The attempt records are here because they are game state that a save has to include: who has
listened at a door, who has searched a cell for a kind of thing, and which thief failed a lock,
at what level.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
Which kind of duration this is.

- `instant`: the spell resolves and is over.
- `permanent`: the effect never ends on its own.
- `concentration`: the effect lasts while the caster concentrates. Casting attaches it with no
  end, and you release it from the ledger when the caster stops.
- `fixed`: a length counted in `unit`.
- `special`: the printed line has no structure osrlib can read. Casting attaches the effect
  with no end, and you release it when the printed line describes.

unit.description:
The time unit a `fixed` duration counts in: rounds, turns, or days. `null` on every other kind.

See `TimeUnit`.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description:
How many `unit` a `fixed` duration lasts, before the per-level bonus.

`null` when the length is rolled with `dice`. When `amount` and `dice` are both `null`, the
length is `per_level` times the caster's level.

dice.title: Dice
dice.description:
A dice expression for a rolled length, in place of `amount`.

*Sleep* lasts `"4d4"` turns. osrlib rolls the dice on the effects stream when the effect attaches.

per_level.title: Per Level
per_level.description:
How many extra `unit` the duration lasts per caster level.

Casting adds it to `amount`, or to the modifier of `dice`. *Light* prints `6 turns +1 per
level`, so `amount` is 6 and `per_level` is 1, and a 3rd-level caster's light lasts 9 turns.

concentration_cap_unit.description:
The unit of the longest a `concentration` duration can last, when the page prints a limit.

*Insect plague* prints `Concentration (up to 1 day)`, so this is days and
`concentration_cap_amount` is 1. `null` when the page prints no limit. Casting doesn't apply the
limit.

concentration_cap_amount.title: Concentration Cap Amount
concentration_cap_amount.description: How many `concentration_cap_unit` a `concentration` duration can last. `null` when the page prints no limit.

DurationSpec.title: DurationSpec
DurationSpec.description:
How long a spell lasts, parsed out of the printed duration line.

Read one from `SpellTemplate.duration_spec`,
or from `ReversedForm.duration_spec` when the
reverse lasts a different length. Casting reads it for you and turns it into the duration of
the effect it attaches to the ledger. You need this model when you show a spell, sort or filter
spells by how long they last, or write a spell of your own.

The printed line is the template's `duration`, and that's what you show a player. A printed
duration that has no structure osrlib can read, like `"Special"`, is stored here as
`kind="special"` with no other field set.

Constructing one raises `pydantic.ValidationError` when `dice` isn't a valid dice expression,
or when a `fixed` duration has no `unit`, or has no `amount`, `dice`, or `per_level`.

kind.description: Whether the edge is open, a wall, or a door.

door.description: The door on this edge when `kind` is `door`, and `null` for every other kind.

Edge.title: Edge
Edge.description:
One entry in a level's `edges` map: what stands on the edge between two cells.

Put these in `LevelSpec.edges`, keyed by
`edge_key`. You need entries only for edges that aren't walls,
because an edge with no entry is a wall. Read an edge back with
`LevelSpec.edge`, which returns a wall for an edge with no
entry and for the level's boundary.

EdgeKind.title: EdgeKind
EdgeKind.description:
What stands on an edge between two cells: nothing, a wall, or a door.

It is the `kind` of an `Edge`, and it sets whether the party can
cross the edge.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
What occupies the edge: `"open"`, `"wall"`, or `"door"`, the serialized values of
`EdgeKind`. For an undiscovered secret door, it's `"wall"`.
On a cell side that has a passage, it's `"open"`. A passage is a level transition that leads
through a wall: the level's edges have a wall there, but a
`MoveParty` across that side takes the party to the
passage's destination.

door_open.title: Door Open
door_open.description: Whether the door stands open. `null` on an edge that is not a door.

door_wedged.title: Door Wedged
door_wedged.description:
Whether the door has been wedged with an iron spike. `null` on an edge that is not
a door.

trap_state.title: Trap State
trap_state.description:
The state of a room trap the party knows is on this door, with the values and meaning of
`MapFeatureView.trap_state`: `"found"` once a
`Search` has found it, and `"sprung"` once it has gone off. No
command removes a room trap, so a door never shows `"removed"`.

Only a room trap that springs when someone opens a door of its area
(`TrapSpec.trigger` `"open"`) shows on a door, and only
on a door of the trapped area where the party has learned of the trap:

- the door a `Search` found the trap through, which is the door in the
  `TrapEvent.direction` of the find. The edge is the
  same from both sides of the door.
- the door whose opening sprang the trap.
- any door on a cell of the trapped area that the party has walked, which
  `EnteredAreaView.cells` lists. Once the party enters
  the area, the doors on its walked cells show the area's `trap_state`, however the party got in
  and wherever it found the trap. The exception is a door whose other side is a second trapped
  area whose trap the party also knows of, where the rule below for two known traps decides.

A trapped area's other doors stay `null` until the party walks the area's cell beside them,
because the party can't yet know that they lead into the same area. When a door has known traps
of the areas on both of its sides, `"sprung"` wins over `"found"`. The field never names or
describes the area. It's `null` on every edge that isn't a door, including an undiscovered
secret door, which the view shows as a wall.

EdgeView.title: EdgeView
EdgeView.description:
One visible edge: what occupies it, and a door's state.

You get these from `ExploredLevelView.edges`.
An undiscovered secret door appears as a wall, so if you draw what the view contains, you
never reveal one.

condition_type.title: Condition Type
condition_type.description:
The discriminator value, `effect_active`. It appears in every document that
includes this condition, and you never set it yourself.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
The effect kind to look for, like `"fatigue"`, or the `kind` of an
`EffectDefinition` you wrote. Effect kinds
come from data, not from a fixed list, so osrlib doesn't check this value against a
catalog. A misspelled kind never matches.

EffectActiveCondition.title: EffectActiveCondition
EffectActiveCondition.description:
A condition that holds when an active effect of `kind` is attached to a party member.

Use it when the party has to invoke an item, not only carry it: the item grants an
effect, and the gate requires that effect. To evaluate it, `condition_holds` reads the
session's effects ledger (`EffectsLedger`), which
records every active effect. An effect attached to a location doesn't count, because
`condition_holds` checks only party members for this condition.

visibility.description:
Referee visibility: this is the ledger's record. The players notice the condition the effect gives, which
a separate event reports.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description: The id the ledger gave the effect, like `effect-0001`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The effect's kind, from its definition, like `"sleep"`, `"regeneration"`, or `"light"`.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description:
What the effect is attached to: an entity id for a creature, or a location string for an effect in a
place.

expires_round.title: Expires Round
expires_round.description:
The round the effect is due to end, counted from the start of the game clock, like
`GameClock.rounds`. `null` when the effect has no duration or is
permanent.

EffectAttachedEvent.title: EffectAttachedEvent
EffectAttachedEvent.description:
An effect has started on a creature, an item, or a location.

An effect is a lasting change the rules make, like a spell's *sleep* or a troll's regeneration, which an
`EffectsLedger` tracks until it ends.
`EffectsLedger.attach` reports this first, before any condition the
effect gives. Keep the `effect_id` if you plan to end the effect early with
`EffectsLedger.release`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
The effect's name, like `"sleep"` or `"regeneration"`. The model accepts any non-empty string. The ledger
compares kinds on the same target for `stacking`, and
`EffectsLedger.active_on` filters on the kind, so give each kind of
effect one name and use it everywhere. A kind that contains `poison`, such as `"poison"` or `"spider_poison"`,
makes a `"death"` expiry a death by poison.

duration_unit.description:
The unit the duration is counted in: rounds, turns, or days. `null` means the effect has no duration and
runs until you release it. A unit needs either `duration_amount` or `duration_dice`.

duration_amount.title: Duration Amount
duration_amount.description: A fixed duration, counted in `duration_unit`. Use this or `duration_dice`, not both, and only with a unit.

duration_dice.title: Duration Dice
duration_dice.description:
A dice expression rolled once at attach time to set the duration, like `"2d6"`. The roll comes from the
effects stream, so attaching a definition with dice and no `stream` raises `ValueError`. osrlib checks the
expression with `parse` when you construct the definition, and a malformed one raises
`ContentValidationError`.

permanent.title: Permanent
permanent.description:
True means the effect never expires on its own, so a permanent definition has no duration. That's how
petrification lasts until someone casts *stone to flesh*. Set `dispellable` to choose whether *dispel magic*
can end the effect.

tick.title: Tick
tick.description:
The name of a periodic behavior the ledger runs while the effect lasts, or `null` for none.
`"regeneration"` heals the bearer and can bring a troll back from death. `"charm_resave"` rolls the bearer's
saving throw versus spells and releases the effect when it passes.

tick_interval_rounds.title: Tick Interval Rounds
tick_interval_rounds.description:
How many rounds pass between ticks. The default of 1 ticks every round. For a charm,
`cast_spell` sets it from the subject's INT: every 30 days for INT 8 or
lower, every 7 days for INT 9 to 12, and every day for INT 13 or higher. A monster has no INT score and
saves every 7 days.

stacking.title: Stacking
stacking.description:
What happens when you attach this kind to a target that already has an effect of the same kind.
`"stack"` adds a second effect. `"refresh"` restarts the existing effect's duration and adds nothing.
`"ignore"` changes nothing, and the attach returns no effect.

expiry.title: Expiry
expiry.description:
The name of an outcome the ledger resolves when the duration runs out, or `null` for none.

The outcome adds to the ordinary ending and doesn't replace it. The ledger removes the effect, emits the
`EffectExpiredEvent`, and takes off the condition and modifiers.
Then it runs the outcome on the bearer:

- `"death"` kills the bearer, which is how a delayed poison works. The death is a death by poison, with
  `DeathEvent.poison` set, only when the effect's `kind` contains
  `poison`. Name a delayed poison's kind that way, because a session revives a character with
  *neutralize poison* only after a death by poison. A kind such as `"venom"` kills, but not by poison.
- `"splash_damage"` deals the second round of damage from burning oil or holy water. It rolls the `dice`
  param, which the definition needs.
- `"weakness_strength_set"` attaches the Ring of Weakness curse when its onset ends. Pass an `allocator` to
  the ledger's `advance` for it.

An effect on a location has no bearer, so its outcome never runs.

condition.description:
A `Condition` granted when the effect attaches and taken back when it
expires or is released. When the target is immune to the condition, nothing attaches, and the attach
returns no effect.

modifiers.title: Modifiers
modifiers.description:
The `ModifierSpec` adjustments granted while the effect lasts and
taken back when it ends.

dispellable.title: Dispellable
dispellable.description:
True marks the effect as one *dispel magic* can end. Everything
`cast_spell` attaches is dispellable, permanent effects included. What a
monster inflicts isn't.

params.title: Params
params.description:
Any other values the effect's tick, its expiry outcome, or other code that reads the effect needs. The keys
osrlib reads include these:

- For the `"regeneration"` tick: `per_round`, `delay_rounds`, `revive`, and `while_alive`, as
  `regeneration_definition` describes them.
- For the `"splash_damage"` outcome: `dice`, the damage roll, `element`, and `keys`, the damage keys.
- For the `"weakness_strength_set"` outcome: `strength_set`, the strength score the curse sets.
- For `natural_healing`: `healing_rest_days`, the number of rest days
  for each natural heal.

Constructing a definition raises `pydantic.ValidationError` when one of these integer params is present and
isn't a whole number: `per_round` and `delay_rounds` on a regeneration tick, which can't be negative either,
`strength_set` on a `weakness_strength_set` expiry, and `healing_rest_days`, which has to be at least 1.

osrlib ignores any key it doesn't read, so you can store your own values here.

EffectDefinition.title: EffectDefinition
EffectDefinition.description:
The blueprint for an effect: how long it lasts, what it does while it lasts, and what happens when it ends.

Write one of these for each spell, ability, or hazard you want to put on a creature or a place. Then pass it
to `EffectsLedger.attach` with the entity id or location it applies
to. Attaching creates a running `ActiveEffect` from the blueprint. The
blueprint is frozen, so one definition serves every target you attach it to. You don't write definitions
for the spells in `load_spells`:
`cast_spell` builds and attaches those for you. Write your own when you
author something new, or run the rules without a session.

Give the effect a duration with `duration_unit` and either `duration_amount` or `duration_dice`. Leave all three
out and the effect runs until you release it. Set `permanent`, with no duration, for an effect that only magic
undoes.

Constructing one raises `pydantic.ValidationError` when the definition can't run:

- The duration isn't a unit with exactly one of `duration_amount` and `duration_dice`.
- `permanent` is set and the definition has a duration.
- `tick` or `expiry` isn't a name osrlib defines.
- The `"splash_damage"` expiry has no `dice` param.

A malformed dice expression in `duration_dice`, in the `"splash_damage"` expiry's `dice` param, or in the
`"regeneration"` tick's `revive` param raises `ContentValidationError`.
So a mistake in a definition shows up when you construct it, not when the effect attaches, ticks, or expires.

visibility.description:
Referee visibility: this is the ledger's record. When a light source burns out, a session also reports a
separate event the players see.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description: The id of the effect that ended.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The effect's kind, from its definition.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description: The entity id or location string the effect was attached to.

round.title: Round
round.description: The round the effect ended on, counted from the start of the game clock.

EffectExpiredEvent.title: EffectExpiredEvent
EffectExpiredEvent.description:
An effect ran out of time and ended.

`EffectsLedger.advance` reports this when the clock reaches the
round an effect ends on. This event comes first. Then the effect's condition and modifiers come off. Last, an
effect that does something when it ends does it, like the second hit of thrown oil. When you end an effect early,
the ledger reports an `EffectReleasedEvent` instead.

visibility.description: Referee visibility: this is the ledger's record.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

effect_id.title: Effect Id
effect_id.description: The id of the effect that was ended.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The effect's kind, from its definition.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description: The entity id or location string the effect was attached to.

EffectReleasedEvent.title: EffectReleasedEvent
EffectReleasedEvent.description:
An effect was ended early, before its time was up.

`EffectsLedger.release` reports this, as when a *dispel magic*
ends a spell, a charmed creature makes its save, or someone puts out a torch. For an effect that ran out of time,
the ledger reports an `EffectExpiredEvent` instead.

visibility.description: Referee visibility: this is the ledger's record.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The effect's kind, from its definition.

target_ref.title: Target Ref
target_ref.description: The entity id or location string the effect is attached to.

round.title: Round
round.description: The round the effect acted on, counted from the start of the game clock.

EffectTickedEvent.title: EffectTickedEvent
EffectTickedEvent.description:
An effect did what it does at regular intervals, like a troll's regeneration healing it.

`EffectsLedger.advance` reports this each time a regeneration
heals or a charmed creature rolls its repeated save, and
`pop_mirror_image` reports it when an attack destroys one image. What
the effect did is in the events next to this one: healing, a saving throw, or a release.

effects.title: Effects
effects.description:
Every running `ActiveEffect`, in the order they were attached. Read it
to see everything running at once. To find the effects on one target, call
`active_on`. `attach`, `release`, and `advance` update the
list.

EffectsLedger.title: EffectsLedger
EffectsLedger.description:
The object that contains every running effect and resolves each one as the game clock moves.

One ledger covers a whole game. A `GameSession` creates one and keeps it
as `session.ledger` for the life of the session. When you run the rules without a session, construct one with
`EffectsLedger()` and keep it beside your `GameClock`. It's a pydantic model,
so you save it with `model_dump` and restore it with `model_validate`, along with the clock and the creatures.

Its methods:

- `attach` puts an effect on a target.
- `advance` moves the clock and resolves every expiry and tick
  in the time that passes.
- `release` ends an effect early.
- `active_on` lists the effects on one target.

Only `advance` ends an effect when its time runs out. If you move the clock any other way, effects that should
have expired stay in place, so always move the clock through the ledger.

Element.title: Element
Element.description:
A kind of energy that a breath weapon, an attack, or a spell can deal, and a monster can resist.

A dragon's breath has one of these elements, and so does each entry in
`Defenses.energy`. Before any damage is rolled, the
combat functions look up the attack's element there to decide whether the attack hurts the monster
at all.

code.title: Code
code.description: The message code, always `encounter.ended`. The ending is in `outcome`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the party knows the encounter is behind it.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `encounter_ended`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description:
How it ended:

- `"victory"`: the monsters were beaten.
- `"evaded"`: the party got away before or during a fight.
- `"escaped"`: the party got away at the end of a chase.
- `"turned"`: undead were driven off.
- `"parley"`: the party talked or paid its way past, through an
  `EndEncounter`.
- `"departed"`: the party walked away from monsters that let it go, through an `EndEncounter`.

EncounterEndedEvent.title: EncounterEndedEvent
EncounterEndedEvent.description:
The encounter is over, however it went.

Emitted when the monsters are beaten or turned, or when the party gets away from them.
The session goes back to `exploring`. The session then advances the clock to the start
of the next turn, and to at least one full turn after the encounter opened, so time
passes after this event even when the fight was short. The
`MonsterDefeatedEvent`s and the
`LootDroppedEvent` come before it.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The group's id, like `group-0001`. The session assigns it, and it's unique within the
session. A battle declaration's `target_group_id` refers to this id.

label.title: Label
label.description:
What to call one member of the group in a sentence, like `"goblin"` or `"giant centipede"`.

A group the session makes from monster templates gets their
`display_name`: a keyed group, a group from
`SpawnMonsters`, and a wandering group. A wandering group
whose members come from more than one family gets the encounter table row's name instead. A party of
NPC adventurers is `"adventurer"`. A group you open with
`start_encounter` gets the label you pass.

It's display text, so don't match on its words. To tell what kind of creature a group is, read
`EncounterGroupView.family_id`.

label_plural.title: Label Plural
label_plural.description:
What to call two or more members of the group, like `"goblins"` or `"wolves"`.

It comes from where `label` comes from: the templates'
`display_name_plural`, or
`"adventurers"`. A wandering group whose label is the encounter table row's name gets the row's name
here too, because the author of a row with several kinds of creature writes its name for the whole
band, like `"Tomb guardians"`. A label you pass to
`start_encounter` gets the templates' plural when it's
their display name. Any other label you pass gets the regular English ending that
`display_name_plural` describes, and so does a group loaded from a save that has no plural.

monster_ids.title: Monster Ids
monster_ids.description:
The members' ids in the order they were spawned. Pass an id to
`GameSession.combatant` to get the monster. Dead
members stay in the list, so check each monster for the dead condition to find the living
ones.

distance_feet.title: Distance Feet
distance_feet.description:
The distance between the party line and this group, in feet. The party line is where the party
stood when the encounter opened. In a battle, each member stands at their own advance from that
line, in `BattleState.advance_feet`, and monsters
close at their encounter movement rate until they're within
`MELEE_RANGE_FEET` of the nearest member they can see. A
routed group moves away. When every member the monsters can see has fallen back behind the line,
the line moves back to the foremost of them, and every group's distance grows by the same amount,
as `BattleState.advance_feet` describes.

During a pursuit, the party runs as one body, and this is the group's distance from the party. A
pursuing group's distance changes each round as
`PursuitState.gap_feet` describes. A group that
doesn't pursue stands where it is, so its distance grows by the party's running rate each round.
A device used during the chase measures its reach from this distance.

fleeing.title: Fleeing
fleeing.description:
True once the group has failed a morale check and turned to run. Until it gets away, the
party can still attack it.

fled.title: Fled
fled.description:
True once the group has run past `FLEE_EXIT_FEET` and left
the fight, or when its morale score is 2 and it ran as it entered the battle. It also becomes true
when a battle ends with the group's living members all turned or afraid and the group past
`FLEE_EXIT_FEET` without a move of its own, so the group ends the encounter routed, as a group
that ran out does. The session refuses
every battle declaration aimed at the group, whether an attack, a move to close, an item, or a
spell, with `battle.declaration.unknown_group`.

The session emits a `MonsterEscapedEvent` for the
group in the command result in which this becomes true, and in no other result. For a group
that runs past `FLEE_EXIT_FEET`, the event comes right after the group's
`GroupMovedEvent`. For a group of morale 2, it comes
right after the group's `MonsterFledEvent`. For a group
marked fled as the battle ends, it comes right before the
`BattleEndedEvent`.

member_treasure.title: Member Treasure
member_treasure.description:
The treasure each member carries, keyed by monster id. The session rolls it when it spawns the
monster, from the treasure types for individuals (P through T). When the encounter closes, a slain
member's treasure drops on the party's cell, and a routed member takes its treasure away.

group_treasure.description:
The treasure the group shares, rolled at spawn from the treasure types for groups (U and V), or
None when the group has none. It drops on the party's cell only when every member is slain. If
any member routed, the group's treasure goes with the runners. When a turning or a fear effect
catches only some members of a group, the group's treasure stays with the members who fight on.

EncounterGroup.title: EncounterGroup
EncounterGroup.description:
One monster group in an encounter: its members, its distance, and the treasure it carries.

You get these from `session.encounter.groups`. The session creates them when an encounter
opens, or when a `SpawnMonsters` adds a group to it. It
updates them during the battle, and loading a save restores them, so you don't construct one
yourself. Much of a fight works by group instead of by monster. When a group fails its morale
check, the whole group flees at once. A party member's attack names its target group in the
`target_group_id` of a `BattleDeclaration`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the party sees the new monsters arrive.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `encounter_group_joined`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description:
The new group's id, the same as its
`EncounterGroupView.id` in the player view. To
attack the group, put this id in a battle declaration's `target_group_id`.

label.title: Label
label.description:
The group's `label`: what the party would call one
of its members, like `"goblin"`.

label_plural.title: Label Plural
label_plural.description:
The group's `label_plural`, like
`"goblins"`, for a line like "2 goblins". An event loaded from a save that has no plural gets `label`
with the regular English ending.

count.title: Count
count.description: How many creatures are in the group.

distance_feet.title: Distance Feet
distance_feet.description: How far away the group is, in feet, when it joins.

EncounterGroupJoinedEvent.title: EncounterGroupJoinedEvent
EncounterGroupJoinedEvent.description:
A new monster group joined the open encounter or battle, with what the party can see of it.

Emitted by `SpawnMonsters` when an encounter or a
battle is open, after the `MonstersSpawnedEvent`
for the same monsters. The players learn of the new group from this event, as they learn of
the first groups from `EncounterStartedEvent`.
The session rolls no surprise or reaction for the group. The group acts from the next round.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The group's id, like `"group-0001"`. You put it in the `target_group_id` of a battle
declaration, so a remote client needs it to fight at all. It's a session id that counts up,
not a secret, the same as a `MemberView.id`.

label.title: Label
label.description:
What to call one member of the group in a sentence, like `"goblin"`. It's the same as
`EncounterGroup.label`, which lists where each kind
of group gets its label. It's display text, so don't match on its words. To tell what kind of
creature the group is, read `family_id` and `categories`.

label_plural.title: Label Plural
label_plural.description:
What to call two or more members of the group, like `"goblins"` or `"wolves"`. It's the same as
`EncounterGroup.label_plural`.

family_id.title: Family Id
family_id.description:
What kind of monster the group is, as the
`family_id` its members' templates share, like
`"fire_beetle"` or `"hellhound"`. `null` for a party of NPC adventurers, and for a group whose
members come from more than one family.

The value is the same however the group came to be: from a keyed area, a wandering monster check, or
a `SpawnMonsters`. So match on it, not on the words in
`label`.

The players see this value. A family is the creature the players see, and it's shared by
every form the players can't tell apart, so a group of hellhounds is `"hellhound"` whatever their
Hit Dice. For a template the adventure bundles in
`Adventure.monsters`, the value is the template's `id`
unless its author set `family_id`. An author who disguises a creature as another, like a
doppelganger the players see as a goblin, sets the template's `family_id` to the family the players
should see, `"goblin"`, as well as its `display_name`. The players also see the template's
`categories`. A group your code opens with
`start_encounter` under a label of its own still reports
its templates' family here.

To read what the players' rulebook says about the creature, pass the value to
`MonsterCatalog.family` on
`load_monsters`. A family that only the adventure bundles has no entry
in the rulebook, so it isn't in `load_monsters()`, and `family` raises `ValueError` for it. A session
finds it in `GameSession.effective_monsters`.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description:
The categories every member of the group has, like `("undead",)`, as in
`MonsterTemplate.categories`. A party of NPC
adventurers is `("person",)`, because *hold person* and *charm person* affect any character.

Use it to offer what works only against one kind of creature. Turning and holy water affect a group
with `"undead"`, and *hold person* affects a group with `"person"`. The players see these categories,
as they see `family_id`.

count.title: Count
count.description: How many of the group are still alive.

distance_feet.title: Distance Feet
distance_feet.description: How far away the group is on the range track, in feet.

visible_conditions.title: Visible Conditions
visible_conditions.description:
The conditions visible on the living members of the group, as
`Condition` serialized values, sorted and deduplicated so
the same condition on six goblins appears once. `condition_counts` says how many members have
each one.

condition_counts.title: Condition Counts
condition_counts.description:
How many living members of the group have each visible condition, keyed by the condition's
serialized value. Its keys are the values in `visible_conditions`, in the same order.

When *sleep* takes 4 of 11 orcs, `count` is 11 and this is `{"asleep": 4}`, so you can show "4 of 11
orcs asleep" and tell whether a second *sleep* is worth casting.

fled.title: Fled
fled.description:
True once the group has run away and left the battle, as in
`EncounterGroup.fled`.

A fled group stays in `EncounterView.groups`, but the
session refuses group-targeted declarations with `battle.declaration.unknown_group`. A spell or
scroll that names one of its members in `targets` gets `magic.cast.unknown_target`. Don't offer
the group or its members as targets. A group that's running but hasn't got away yet isn't fled.
You can still close on it, shoot at it, or cast at it.

The session emits a `MonsterEscapedEvent` for the
group in the command result in which `fled` becomes true, and in no other result. You can show
the group getting away from the event stream, and then drop it from your target lists.

fleeing.title: Fleeing
fleeing.description:
True once the group has failed a morale check and turned to run, as in
`EncounterGroup.fleeing`.

It stays true after the group gets away, when `fled` becomes true as well. A group that's
`fleeing` and not `fled` is running and still in the battle, so you can show it running and
still offer it as a target.

member_distance_feet.title: Member Distance Feet
member_distance_feet.description:
Each living party member's distance to this group, in feet, keyed by member id. Empty outside a
battle.

A battle measures each group's `distance_feet` from the party line, where the party stood when
the encounter opened or where the line has moved back to since, and each member stands at their
own advance from that line, in
`EncounterView.advance_feet`. This is the group's
distance minus the member's advance. At 5' or less, the member and the group can reach each other
in melee. Beyond that, a member attacks the group with a missile weapon, or declares
`move="close"` to move toward it first. A missile's range band and a spell's range are measured
from this distance.

front_rank.title: Front Rank
front_rank.description:
The members who can make a melee attack on this group this round without moving, and whom this
group's melee reaches, in marching order. Empty outside a battle, and empty while nobody stands
within 5' of the group.

These are the members in the party's front rank toward this group who stand within 5' of it. The
ranks toward a group are the living members sorted by their distance to it, nearest first, and cut
into rows of `EncounterView.formation_width`.
A row never mixes distances. Arrival order, then marching order, decides who is in the front row,
so the member who got there in an earlier round stands in front of one who arrives later. This
tuple then lists that row's members in marching order. It's always the same value as
`group_front_rank` for this group.

The session refuses a melee attack on this group by any other member with
`battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank`, or with `combat.attack.out_of_reach` when the member is
farther than 5' away, unless the same declaration's `move="close"` brings them into it. When this
tuple has fewer members than `formation_width`, a member who can reach the group this round can
still take a place in it. `preview_battle_round`
answers that for a plan you're building.

Each of this group's monsters picks its melee target from these members, leaving out invisible
members and members whose *protection from evil* bars it. A monster with a missile attack closes
and uses it at 5' too, so the members behind this rank are out of a monster group's reach. NPC
adventurers with missile weapons shoot from farther away, at the members in the first row of the
party's ranks toward their group.

Only the monsters' front rank makes melee attacks on these members: the group's first living
monsters, as many as
`EncounterView.formation_width`. So six
skeletons in a 10' corridor strike with two at most, the smaller of `count` and the width. A
monster in front that's asleep, paralysed, or turned to stone keeps its place and doesn't attack,
so fewer can strike. `condition_counts` counts those conditions across the whole group, so it
doesn't say whether they fall on the monsters in front. With the ruleset's
`formation_width_limit` flag off, every living monster can attack.

lit.title: Lit
lit.description:
Whether a light the party carries reaches this group, or `null` outside a battle.

The group is lit when a living member with a burning light, like a torch or a lantern, stands
within that light's radius of it, 30' for a torch or a lantern. A darkness effect that puts out
the party's light, as `GameSession.party_light`
reports, leaves every group unlit. The session refuses no declaration because a group is unlit, so
use this field and `seen_by` to decide what your game offers or how it describes the fight.

seen_by.title: Seen By
seen_by.description:
The living members who can see this group, in marching order. Empty outside a battle.

A member sees the group when it's `lit`, or when the member has working infravision and the group
is within its range. A dwarf's and an elf's infravision reaches 60', and so does infravision an
effect grants. A darkness effect that stops infravision, as
`GameSession.party_light` reports, leaves it
working for nobody. A blind member sees nothing.

members.title: Members
members.description:
Every member of this group in the group's existing order, including dead and fled members.

Each entry exposes only its session id and coarse status. Use an `"alive"` entry's id in
`BattleDeclaration.targets` for a spell or
scroll aimed at individual creatures. The spell's range, target count, and touch checks still
apply. The tuple defaults to empty when you parse a view written before rosters were available.

EncounterGroupView.title: EncounterGroupView
EncounterGroupView.description:
A monster or NPC group as the players see it: identity, roster, count, distance, and appearance.

You get these from `EncounterView.groups`. Hit
points and other statistics never appear, because the players know only what they can see
across the room.

id.title: Id
id.description:
The creature's existing session id, such as `"monster-0001"` or `"npc-0001"`.

It matches the id in events and stays the same after save/load or a group split. Read the
current group to find where the creature is now.

status.title: Status
status.description:
The creature's coarse status: `"defeated"` when dead, `"fled"` when alive in a group
that has left the encounter, and `"alive"` otherwise. A creature that's running but hasn't
left is still `"alive"`. This doesn't report whether the creature can act or is immune to a spell.

EncounterMemberView.title: EncounterMemberView
EncounterMemberView.description:
One monster or NPC adventurer's public identity and coarse status.

Read these from `EncounterGroupView.members`.
Use `id` in `BattleDeclaration.targets` to
select an individual creature for a spell or scroll before any combat event names it. Hit
points, individual conditions, and other private statistics never appear.

visibility.description: Player visibility: this is the moment the players are told what they have met.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `encounter_started`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

monster_name.title: Monster Name
monster_name.description:
The `label` of the first group in the encounter:
what the party would call one of its members, like `"goblin"`. A party of NPC adventurers appears
as `"adventurer"`, and its roster stays hidden from the players.

monster_name_plural.title: Monster Name Plural
monster_name_plural.description:
The first group's `label_plural`, like
`"goblins"`, for a line like "3 goblins". An event loaded from a save that has no plural gets
`monster_name` with the regular English ending.

count.title: Count
count.description: How many creatures there are across every group in the encounter.

distance_feet.title: Distance Feet
distance_feet.description:
How far away they are, in feet, when the encounter opens. Battle starts from this distance
and closes from there.

party_surprised.title: Party Surprised
party_surprised.description: Whether the party was caught off guard, which can give the monsters a free first round.

monsters_surprised.title: Monsters Surprised
monsters_surprised.description:
Whether the monsters were caught off guard, which gives the party a free round if the fight
starts.

group_labels.title: Group Labels
group_labels.description:
The `label` of each group in the encounter, in
the order of `EncounterState.groups`. The first
entry is `monster_name`. `group_labels_plural` and `group_counts` line up with this tuple, and
the counts add up to `count`. The three tuples have the same length, and an event whose tuples
differ in length is refused when it's built or loaded. An event loaded from a save written before
the field existed has an empty tuple in all three.

group_labels_plural.title: Group Labels Plural
group_labels_plural.description:
Each group's `label_plural`, like
`"goblins"`, in the order of `group_labels`.

group_counts.title: Group Counts
group_counts.description: How many creatures each group has when the encounter opens, in the order of `group_labels`.

EncounterStartedEvent.title: EncounterStartedEvent
EncounterStartedEvent.description:
The party met monsters, with what the party can see of them.

Emitted when an encounter opens, whichever way it opened: the party stepping into an
area whose author placed monsters there, with
`MoveParty`, or arriving in one with
`EnterDungeon` or
`UseStairs`, a wandering-monster check that hits,
or a referee's `SpawnMonsters` or
`SpawnNpcParty`. The session mode becomes
`encounter`, where the party can talk, run, wait, or fight.

It contains only what the party can see: a name and a count for each group, and a distance.
The dice behind the meeting are on the
