skills can try, and each member gets one attempt at each trap. A failed attempt springs
the trap on the thief who tried, unless
`Ruleset.failed_trap_removal_springs`
is off. With the flag off, the trap stays armed and found, and another thief in the party
can try. Once the trap is removed,
`TakeTreasure` empties the cache safely.

Modes:

`exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the session is not exploring a dungeon.
- `session.command.unknown_member` - `character_id` matches no party member.
- `session.command.member_incapacitated` - the member cannot act.
- `exploration.trap.not_a_thief` - the member has no thief skills.
- `exploration.feature.unknown` - `feature_id` is malformed, stale, or
  ambiguous, matches no available trapped cache on this cell, names a cache
  with no trap, or names a trap the party hasn't found.
- `exploration.trap.already_resolved` - the trap was already removed or has
  already sprung.
- `exploration.action.requires_light` - the party has no light. Infravision
  isn't enough to remove a trap.
- `exploration.search.already_tried` - this member already tried to remove
  this trap.

**Events:**

`DetectionRolledEvent` with the
skill roll, then a `TrapEvent`:
`exploration.trap.removed` on success. A failure gives `exploration.trap.sprung`, or
`exploration.trap.removal_failed` when `failed_trap_removal_springs` is off.
The sprung trap resolves at once against the thief, or against every living
member when the trap catches the whole party. Each step is a separate event:
a `SavingThrowRolledEvent` when
the trap allows a save,
`DamageDealtEvent` and
`HitPointsReportedEvent` for
damage, `EffectAttachedEvent` and
`ConditionGainedEvent` for a
condition, `DeathEvent` when it kills
outright, and
`LocationEnteredEvent`, `via`
`"trap"`, when it drops the party somewhere else. One turn passes.

name.title: Name
name.description: New session name, 1 to 200 characters without control characters such as tabs or newlines.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"reorder_party"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

order.title: Order
order.description:
Every current member's id, dead members included, each exactly once, with the front of
the marching order first. The ids are the
`MemberView.id` values in
`PlayerView.party`. Marching order determines who a
door trap springs on, who reaches into a cache, and who stands in the front rank when a
fight starts. The session refuses any other list with `exploration.party.bad_order`.

ReorderParty.title: ReorderParty
ReorderParty.description:
Set the party's marching order.

Marching order is the order the members walk in, front first. It determines who a door trap
springs on, who reaches into a treasure cache, and who stands in the front rank when a
fight starts. Pass the new order in `order`, a tuple of every member's id, front first.
Send this command in town or while exploring. The session refuses it once an encounter or
a battle has begun.

During a battle, the order changes only when a member withdraws or retreats alone. That
member trades places with the member named in
`BattleDeclaration.replacement_id`.
The new order stays after the battle, until you send this command again.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - an encounter or battle is underway, or the
  session has ended.
- `exploration.party.bad_order` - `order` doesn't list exactly the current
  members, each once.

**Events:**

A `PartyReorderedEvent` with the new order.
`PlayerView.party` lists the members in the same
order.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"resolve_battle_round"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

declarations.title: Declarations
declarations.description:
One `BattleDeclaration` for each member in
`EncounterView.declarers`, and none for
anyone else. The session refuses any other set of members
with `battle.declaration.roster_mismatch`. If a single declaration is bad, the session
refuses the whole command, not only that member's part of the round. The order of the declarations doesn't change
who acts first, because initiative and the order of the round's phases do. It doesn't change
where anyone moves either, because each member's move is their own.

ResolveBattleRound.title: ResolveBattleRound
ResolveBattleRound.description:
Resolve one battle round from one declaration per party member able to act.

A battle must be underway (see
`EngageBattle`). Each round, get a new player
view from `GameSession.view` and read who has
to declare from
`EncounterView.declarers`. Construct a
`BattleDeclaration` for each of them, and
send them all in one command. Repeat until the session leaves `battle`. It moves to
`exploring` when the battle and its encounter end, to `encounter` when a retreat turns
into a pursuit, and to `game_over` when every party member is dead or turned to stone.

The session accepts or refuses a round as a whole. It checks every declaration before
it resolves any of them, against where the members will stand once the moves the round
declares are made. If a single declaration is bad, the session refuses the command, and
the result lists every rejection found. A refused round costs nothing: no random number,
no game time, and no change to the session. Fix the declarations and send the round
again. To check declarations before you send them, call
`preview_battle_round`, which runs the same
checks without playing the round.

Modes:

`battle`

**Rejections:**

The round as a whole:

- `session.command.wrong_mode` or `battle.none_active` - no battle is underway.
- `battle.declaration.roster_mismatch` - the declarations don't name exactly the
  members in `EncounterView.declarers`, each once. The session checks this first
  and reports nothing else when it fails.
- `battle.declaration.unknown_action` - an `action` the session doesn't
  recognize. Constructing a `BattleDeclaration` with one already fails validation.

Each declaration, by its `action`. Every rejection of a declaration has the declaring
member's id as its `character` param, including the kernel's `combat.attack.*` and
`magic.cast.*` checks, so a client with several players can tell whose declaration
to change:

- Any action: `battle.declaration.no_mirror` when the member declares a
  `gaze_defense` of `mirror` and carries no mirror.
- Move declarations: `battle.declaration.missing_move`,
  `battle.declaration.unknown_group`, and `battle.declaration.cannot_move`.
- A `move` set on an action that can't take it: `battle.declaration.cast_cannot_move`
  on a `cast`, and `battle.declaration.move_not_combinable` on a `turn_undead`, a
  `use_item`, a `give_item`, a `hide`, or a `hold`, and on an `attack` with a
  `fighting_withdrawal` or a `retreat`. Each has the member's id as its `character` param.
  The session checks for them after the back-stab checks and before the action's own
  checks.
- `battle.declaration.replacement_unavailable` when a member who makes a
  `fighting_withdrawal` or a `retreat` alone names a member in `replacement_id` who
  isn't a declarer, is the withdrawing member, is withdrawing too, or was named by a
  withdrawing member earlier in marching order. It also comes back for a declaration
  in a formation move that sets `replacement_id`, because every declarer moves with
  the formation. It has the withdrawing member's id as its `character` param and the
  named id as `replacement`.
- Attack declarations: `battle.declaration.unknown_group`,
  `battle.declaration.no_target`, `battle.declaration.weapon_not_wielded`,
  `battle.declaration.item_unusable` for a wielded magic item with no weapon stats,
  like a wand, `battle.declaration.cannot_move` for an attack that sets `move="close"` by a member
  who can't move, `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank` for a melee attack by a
  member who won't stand in the group's front rank once the round's moves are made,
  and the checks of `validate_attack`:
  `combat.attack.out_of_reach`, `combat.attack.out_of_range`,
  `combat.attack.reload`, `combat.attack.attacker_incapacitated`, and
  `combat.attack.attacker_blind`. The session judges an attack at the member's own
  distance to the group, after the member's `close` if the declaration sets one, and
  `combat.attack.out_of_reach` has that distance as its `distance_feet` param.
- A declaration that sets `back_stab`: `battle.declaration.back_stab_not_attack` on
  any action but `attack`, before any other check. On an attack,
  `battle.declaration.back_stab_no_ability` and
  `battle.declaration.back_stab_target_aware` before the attack checks, and
  `battle.declaration.back_stab_not_melee` after the group and weapon checks and
  before the melee checks. A back-stab gets only the first of these that applies,
  and each has the member's id as its `character` param. A back-stab by a member who
  is hiding doesn't get `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank`.
  `BattleDeclaration.back_stab`
  gives the order in full.
- Hide declarations: `battle.declaration.hide_not_a_thief` when the member's class
  has no thief skills, and `battle.declaration.hide_in_front_rank` when the member will
  stand in the first row of the party's ranks toward a group still in the fight once
  the round's moves are made. The session checks them in that order, after the
  back-stab checks and the check of `move`, and each has the member's id as its
  `character` param.
  `EncounterView.can_hide` lists the
  members who can hide.
- Cast declarations: `battle.declaration.missing_spell`,
  `battle.declaration.unknown_group`,
  `battle.declaration.invisible_target`, and the cast checks
  `magic.cast.unknown_spell`, `magic.cast.silenced_area`,
  `magic.cast.unknown_mode`, `magic.cast.unknown_target`,
  `magic.cast.not_memorized`, `magic.cast.caster_incapacitated`,
  `magic.cast.caster_restrained`, `magic.cast.anti_magic_shell`,
  `magic.cast.not_reversible`, `magic.cast.target_count`,
  `magic.cast.target_must_be_creature`, `magic.cast.out_of_range`. The range is measured
  from the caster to each target's group, or to each target member where they'll stand
  once the round's moves are made, and a touch spell reaches 5'. A touch spell on a
  monster also gets `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank` when the caster isn't in the
  party's front rank toward the monster's group, and `combat.attack.out_of_reach` when the
  monster isn't in its group's front rank.
- Turn-undead declarations: `magic.turning.not_a_turner` and
  `magic.turning.caster_incapacitated`. A turning also gets
  `battle.declaration.no_target` when no living monster is left in any group that
  hasn't fled. That never refuses a round, because a battle always has a living
  monster when the round starts. The session checks the turning again just before it
  resolves, and a turning that gets `no_target` then fails and has no effect.
- Item declarations: `battle.declaration.item_unusable`,
  `battle.declaration.unknown_group`, `battle.declaration.no_target`,
  `items.use.not_usable`, `items.device.inert`, `items.scroll.spent`,
  `items.scroll.wrong_caster`, `items.scroll.no_such_spell`,
  `exploration.action.requires_light`, and `combat.attack.out_of_reach`. A staff's
  strike for a charge is a melee attack, so it also gets
  `battle.declaration.not_in_front_rank` when the member won't stand in the group's
  front rank once the round's moves are made. A scroll read can also get the cast
  checks on its spell and targets (`magic.cast.unknown_mode`, `magic.cast.unknown_target`,
  `battle.declaration.invisible_target`, `magic.cast.target_count`,
  `magic.cast.target_must_be_creature`, `magic.cast.out_of_range`,
  `magic.cast.caster_incapacitated`, `magic.cast.caster_restrained`,
  `magic.cast.anti_magic_shell`). A thrown item can also get the `validate_attack` checks
  listed for attack declarations, and it gets `battle.declaration.item_unusable` for an
  item the member doesn't carry or can't throw before `battle.declaration.unknown_group`.
  A potion given to another member to drink gets
  `battle.declaration.target_count` for more than one id in `targets`,
  `items.use.target_not_allowed`, `items.use.target_cannot_drink`, and
  `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach`. A staff of healing's touch gets
  `battle.declaration.target_count`, `items.use.unknown_target`,
  `items.use.target_cannot_be_healed` on a creature that's dead or turned to stone,
  `items.use.invisible_target` on another creature that's invisible,
  `items.use.target_healed_today` on a creature the staff already healed today, and
  `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach` on another member. On a monster, it gets the
  checks of a touch spell on a monster.
- Hand-over declarations, `give_item`: `battle.declaration.target_count` for anything
  but one id in `targets`, `exploration.give.same_member`,
  `session.command.unknown_member`, `session.command.member_incapacitated`,
  `items.curse.stuck`, `exploration.item.not_carried`, and
  `battle.declaration.member_out_of_reach`, in that order.

**Events:**

Opening the round:
`BattleRoundEvent`, a
`SpellDeclaredEvent` per declared
cast, and
`InitiativeRolledEvent`, which reports
which side acts first.

Movement: a `MemberMovedEvent` each time a
member moves by themselves, a
`MemberWithdrewEvent` each time a member
who falls back alone trades places in the marching order with the member they named,
and a `GroupMovedEvent` each time a group's
distance from the party line changes, when monsters close or run, and when the whole
party moves in a formation move. After the moves, for each member who hides, in
marching order, a `HideAttemptedEvent`
followed by the referee's
`DetectionRolledEvent` of their hide in
shadows roll. A hiding member's back-stab adds the referee's `DetectionRolledEvent` of
their move silently roll before its first attack roll.

Missiles and melee:
`AttackRolledEvent`,
`DamageDealtEvent`,
`DamageAbsorbedEvent`,
`HitPointsReportedEvent`,
`SavingThrowRolledEvent`,
`EquipmentDestroyedEvent`,
`LevelDrainedEvent` with
`SpellForgottenEvent` when a drain
costs a caster prepared spells, and
`DeathEvent`.

Magic: `SpellCastEvent`,
`TargetsSelectedEvent` when the
engine picks the spell's targets,
`SpellDisruptedEvent`,
`DeclarationFizzledEvent` when a
device use, a potion given to another member, a hand-over, or a turning fails the
check the session makes just before it resolves, and at `battle.melee.fizzled` when
a melee attack can't resolve when it comes up, because its group has no monster left
to strike or because of where the member stands,
`MagicDispelledEvent`,
`UndeadTurnedEvent`, and the effects
a spell leaves behind
(`EffectAttachedEvent`,
`EffectReleasedEvent`,
`ConditionGainedEvent`,
`ConditionRemovedEvent`,
`HealingAppliedEvent`).

Items: `ItemsGivenEvent` for a hand-over,
after an `EffectReleasedEvent` for each effect
of an equipped magic item handed over, and
`ItemUsedEvent`, with
`ItemIdentifiedEvent` and
`CurseRevealedEvent` the first time an
item is used.

Morale: `MoraleCheckedEvent`,
`MonsterFledEvent` for a group that
fails its morale check and flees, and
`MonstersLeftBehindEvent`
when a fleeing group leaves behind members who can't move. A group that broke runs its
full rate each round, starting in the round it breaks. In the round its move takes it
farther than `FLEE_EXIT_FEET` from every living
member, which can be the round it breaks, a
`MonsterEscapedEvent` comes right after
that move's `GroupMovedEvent`. The group has then left the battle.

Closing the round: the clock advances one round, and these events report what
that changes:
`EffectExpiredEvent`,
`EffectTickedEvent`,
`MonsterRevivedEvent`,
`LightEvent`, and
`ProvisionsEvent`.

A round that ends the battle adds a
`BattleEndedEvent`, after the
`MonsterEscapedEvent` when an escape ended it. A group whose living members are all
turned or afraid, and which stands past `FLEE_EXIT_FEET` without a move of its own,
gets away as the battle ends, and its `MonsterEscapedEvent` comes right before the
`BattleEndedEvent`. The events of the encounter's end follow
(`EncounterEndedEvent`,
`MonsterDefeatedEvent`s, a
`LootDroppedEvent` when the slain leave
anything on the floor, and, under the immediate XP timing,
`XpAwardedEvent` and
`CharacterLeveledUpEvent`). When every
party member is dead or turned to stone, a
`GameOverEvent` follows instead.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"rest"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
How long to rest. `turn` is a single turn, the rest a party in a dungeon needs once every
six turns to avoid fatigue. `night` is 48 turns and counts as sleep. `day` is 144 turns,
counts as sleep, and applies natural healing to every living member. Sleep is what
`PrepareSpells` needs, so a caster's day starts with
a `night` or a `day` rest. Exhaustion from a pursuit clears after three turns of rest in
total. In a dungeon, a wandering encounter can cut any of the three short.

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description:
Whether the party rests quietly in an out-of-the-way place, which the OSE SRD calls hiding.

On a level with the usual 1-in-6 chance of wandering monsters, a hidden rest makes no
wandering-monster rolls at all, as long as the party has made no noise and has no bright
light. That's because `true` lowers the chance of each check during the rest by 1, after
noise and bright light have raised it, and the session makes no roll for a chance of 0 in 6.
In town no checks run, so the flag changes nothing there.

Your game or the referee decides whether the place qualifies. The session accepts the flag
as given. With `false`, the default, the checks run at the level's chance with noise and
light added, as they do while the party explores.

Rest.title: Rest
Rest.description:
Rest the party for one turn, a night (48 turns), or a full day (144 turns).

Send it in town or while exploring. Set `kind` to `"turn"`, `"night"`, or `"day"` to choose
the length. A turn is ten minutes of game time. A rest clears the party's fatigue, the −1
penalty a party in a dungeon gets when it goes six turns without a turn of rest
(`FATIGUE_KIND`). Three turns of rest also clear
exhaustion, the heavier penalty a party gets for running from a long pursuit
(`EXHAUSTED_KIND`).

A night or a day of rest counts as sleep, which casters need before
`PrepareSpells`. A full day of rest also applies
natural healing to every living member.

In a dungeon, the wandering-monster checks go on while the party rests. A check that
turns up monsters interrupts the rest and opens an encounter. To lower the chance of each
check by 1, set `hidden` when the party rests quietly in an out-of-the-way place.

An interrupted rest isn't sleep, and it heals nobody. It still counts the full turns the
party rested before the monsters came. One full turn clears fatigue, and each full turn
counts toward the three turns of rest that clear exhaustion. A rest interrupted during
its first turn clears nothing.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - an encounter or battle is underway, or the
  session has ended.

**Events:**

The events of the time that passes come first: light burning down, provisions, and
wandering-monster checks. Then comes a `RestedEvent`
with code `exploration.rest.rested`. An interrupted rest ends with the encounter's
opening events and a `RestedEvent` with code `exploration.rest.interrupted`
instead. A rest that clears fatigue or exhaustion, interrupted or not, adds a
`FatigueEvent` or an
`ExhaustionEvent`, and a full day's natural
healing adds a `HealingAppliedEvent`
for each member it heals.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the party knows whether it got its rest.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `rested`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
How long the party tried to rest: `"turn"` for the one-turn breather the dungeon rule
calls for, `"night"`, or `"day"`.

RestedEvent.title: RestedEvent
RestedEvent.description:
A rest finished, or was interrupted before it could.

Emitted by `Rest`. The `code` says how the rest went:
`exploration.rest.rested` for a rest that ran to its end, and
`exploration.rest.interrupted` for one a wandering monster cut short.

A completed rest clears the penalty for going without rest, and counts toward recovering
from exhaustion after a chase. A rest of a full day, 144 turns, also heals the party. An interrupted
rest heals nobody. If the party rested at least one full turn (10 minutes of game
time, or 60 rounds) before the monsters came, the rest still clears that penalty, and
each full turn counts toward recovery.

name.title: Name
name.description:
Optional display name for the restored session, 1 to 200 characters without control characters.
Defaults to `adventure_name` from the save when omitted or `null`.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"reveal_objective"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

quest_id.title: Quest Id
quest_id.description:
Which quest the objective belongs to, by
`QuestSpec.id`. The quest has to be active already.

objective_id.title: Objective Id
objective_id.description:
Which objective to show the players, by
`ObjectiveSpec.id` within that quest. The session
refuses an objective that's already revealed or complete with `session.command.quest_state`.

RevealObjective.title: RevealObjective
RevealObjective.description:
Referee: show the players a hidden objective of an active quest.

A hidden objective is missing from the player view until it's revealed or completed.
Completing an objective reveals it, so an objective the party finishes before anyone
announces it needs no reveal. The command accepts only the ids the adventure's quest
specs define, as `ActivateQuest` describes, and
the `ActivateQuest` example shows a quest from start to finish.

When the objective's author wrote an `offer` text in its narrative, an accepted reveal
adds that text to the journal, and the event includes it. No
`JournalEntryAddedEvent` follows,
because the objective's event already includes the text. This command is legal in
every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.unknown_quest` - `quest_id` matches no quest of the
  adventure.
- `session.command.unknown_objective` - `objective_id` matches no objective of
  that quest.
- `session.command.quest_state` - the quest isn't active, or the objective
  is already revealed or already complete. The rejection includes the quest
  id and the state that caused the refusal.

**Events:**

`ObjectiveRevealedEvent` with
the quest id, the objective id, and the objective's offer text.

name.title: Name
name.description:
The reverse's name, as the SRD prints it, like `"Cause Light Wounds"`.

Show this rather than the template's `name` when a cast is reversed.

prose.title: Prose
prose.description:
The SRD text for the reverse, all of it.

Each of the reverse's `modes` has the part of this text that covers that mode as its own
`prose`. In the built-in catalog, the format is the same as a mode's
prose: line-oriented text with no inline markup, one paragraph, list item, heading, table row, or stat line
per line, where a run of lines that start with `|` is a table whose first line is the header row and whose
second is the delimiter row. It's not Markdown, so lay it out line by line.

modes.title: Modes
modes.description:
One `SpellMode` per castable usage of the reverse, at least one, each with a
different key.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description:
The reverse's printed duration, when the page prints a different one for it.

`null` means the normal form's duration applies.

duration_spec.description:
The structured form of `duration`, as a `DurationSpec`.

`null` means the reverse lasts as long as the normal form, which is the usual case. A page that
prints two durations in one line, like *remove curse*'s `Instant / Permanent (curse)`, gives
the second one to the reverse.

range.title: Range
range.description:
The reverse's range, when the reverse's text states one of its own, such as `"120’"`. Show this to a player.

`null` means the normal form's printed `range` applies to the reverse too, which is the usual case. The
page's range line belongs to the normal form, so a reverse states a different range in its text. In the
built-in catalog, only *cause fear*, the reverse of *remove fear*, does: it "Causes a target within
120’ to flee", while *remove fear* reaches "The caster or a creature touched".

range_spec.description:
The structured form of `range`, as a `RangeSpec`.

`null` means the reverse reaches as far as the normal form. Casting reads it for a reversed cast, and
`SpellTemplate.range_spec_for` returns the range
that applies to either form.

Set both `range` and `range_spec`, or neither of them.

ReversedForm.title: ReversedForm
ReversedForm.description:
The reverse of a reversible spell, stored on the spell's entry.

*Cure light wounds* reverses into *cause light wounds*, and *light* into *darkness*. The reverse
is never a separate catalog entry. Read it from
`SpellTemplate.reversed_form`, which is
`null` on a spell that doesn't reverse. To cast it, pass `reversed=True` to
`cast_spell` with a `mode` key from this form's `modes`. The
reverse's keys can differ from the normal form's: *cure light wounds* has `heal` and
`cure_paralysis`, and its reverse has `harm`.

When the form is chosen depends on the kind of caster. An arcane caster chooses normal or
reversed when memorizing, and the choice is the
`MemorizedSpell`'s `reversed` field. A divine caster
memorizes the normal form and chooses when casting, by speaking the words backwards, so any of
their memorized copies can be cast either way.

Constructing one raises `pydantic.ValidationError` when only one of `range` and `range_spec` is
set, so the range a client shows is always the range casting checks.

Role.title: Role
Role.description:
What an API key may do in a game: `player` or `referee`.

- `player`: plays games and sees only player-visible state and events.
- `referee`: everything `player` may do, plus the referee view, referee events, referee
  commands, chosen seeds, character and save imports, and full adventure and save documents.

A role restricts visibility and actions inside a game, not data ownership. Every key for a
client application can read and modify all of that client's characters, adventures, sessions,
and saves, regardless of role.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"roll_dice"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description:
The roll, in the notation `parse` accepts, like `"1d20"`,
`"3d6+2"`, or `"2d6+1x10"`. A malformed expression fails validation when the command is
constructed rather than coming back as a rejection, so it never reaches the session and
draws nothing.

RollDice.title: RollDice
RollDice.description:
Referee: roll dice through the session, so the roll is seeded, logged, and replayed.

Use it when the referee decides a chance outcome that osrlib doesn't model, like a
puzzle, a bluff, or whether a frayed rope holds. A roll made through the session is
logged, replayed, and reported as an event, unlike a roll you make yourself.
This command is legal in every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included. The session draws the roll
from the separate
`ADJUDICATION_STREAM`, so a referee's roll
never changes what any other stream draws. A malformed `expression` fails validation with
pydantic's `ValidationError` when the command is constructed, as a malformed `count_dice` on
`SpawnMonsters` does, so it never reaches the
session and makes no random roll.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

None.

**Events:**

`DiceRolledEvent` with the
expression, the total, and each die's result. The event has referee visibility.

rolls.title: Rolls
rolls.description: What each die came up, in the order they were rolled. One entry per die.

modifier.title: Modifier
modifier.description: The modifier that was added to the sum of the dice, copied from the expression.

multiplier.title: Multiplier
multiplier.description: The multiplier that was applied after the modifier, copied from the expression.

total.title: Total
total.description:
The result of the roll: the sum of the dice, plus the modifier, times the multiplier.

Not clamped, so a `1d4-1` roll can total 0.

RollResult.title: RollResult
RollResult.description:
What a dice roll produced: each die, and the total they add up to.

`roll` returns one. Use `total` as the result of the
roll, and show `rolls` to the player if you display dice.
`damage_roll` returns one too, and a
`DamageDealtEvent` lists its dice in `rolls`,
so you can use the same display code for damage.

level_number.title: Level Number
level_number.description: Dungeon depth counting from 1 at the top level, used to select the wandering encounter table.

anyOf.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

seed.title: Seed
seed.description:
Optional seed (0 to 2^53 - 1). Pass the `seed` from an earlier response with the same body to reproduce the
stocked room, or omit it to let the server draw a random seed.

RoomRequest.title: RoomRequest
RoomRequest.description: Dungeon level and optional seed for stocking one dungeon room.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Random number seed, an integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9,007,199,254,740,991).

room.description:
Rolled room `contents` (`empty`, `monster`, `special`, or `trap`), `treasure_present`, and any `encounter`,
`npc_party`, or unguarded `treasure`.

RoomResponse.title: RoomResponse
RoomResponse.description: Stocked dungeon room result and the seed that produced it.

RoutineUse.title: RoutineUse
RoutineUse.description:
When a monster may use one of its attack routines, taken from the monster's OSE SRD entry.

Each `AttackRoutine` has one of these values in its
`use` field. There are four values:

- `PRIMARY`: the first routine the stat block prints.
- `ALTERNATIVE`: a routine the monster may use instead of the first in any round.
- `SITUATIONAL`: a routine for a situation osrlib doesn't model, like a charge or a ship.
- `SPECIAL`: a breath, a gaze, or a spell, which battle never rolls as an attack.

The first routine of every built-in template is `PRIMARY`, and each later routine has one of
the other three values. In battle, an `ActionPolicy`
chooses what each monster does in a round. It reads this value to decide whether it may pick
the routine for a round of melee. The default policy,
`ScriptedPolicy`, picks with equal chance among a
monster's `PRIMARY` and `ALTERNATIVE` routines. A policy of your own can pick any routine by
its index in `MonsterAction.routine`.

hp_reroll_at_first_level.title: Hp Reroll At First Level
hp_reroll_at_first_level.description:
Reroll a first-level hit die that comes up 1 or 2. An optional rule, off by default.

Turn it on and osrlib rerolls the raw die until it shows 3 or more, before the CON
modifier is added, so a first-level character starts with at least 3 hit points before
that modifier.

max_hp_at_first_level.title: Max Hp At First Level
max_hp_at_first_level.description:
Count a first-level character's hit die as its maximum. A house rule, off by default.

The SRD doesn't print this rule. Its character creation has you roll the class's hit die. Turn
the flag on and a first-level character's hit points are the hit die's size plus the CON
modifier, and at least 1, so a fighter with CON 7 starts with 8 - 1 = 7.
`roll_hit_points` still throws the dice it throws with
the flag off, so the creation stream ends in the same place and the starting gold roll after it is
the same. With `hp_reroll_at_first_level` also on, a die showing 1 or 2 is still thrown again and
`HitPointRoll.rolls` lists every die, but the
reroll can't change the hit points. The flag affects only the hit points rolled at character
creation. `level_up` rolls each later level's hit die as usual.

ability_score_method.title: Ability Score Method
ability_score_method.description:
How a new character's ability scores are rolled. `"3d6"` by default, the SRD's method.

`"4d6_drop_lowest"` is a house rule, not an SRD rule. With it, each ability throws four d6 and
the lowest die doesn't count, so the score is the sum of the other three, from 3 to 18.
`create_character` passes the method to
`roll_ability_scores`, and the result lists the
dropped die of each ability in
`AbilityScoreRolls.dropped`. The method
affects only the characters you create. The NPC adventurers that encounters generate always
roll 3d6.

encumbrance.description:
Which system tracks carried weight and sets movement rate. Basic by default.

See `EncumbranceMode` for what each mode
counts, and `osrlib.core.items` for the weights and rates it
reads.

variable_weapon_damage.title: Variable Weapon Damage
variable_weapon_damage.description:
Let each weapon deal the damage its description lists. An optional rule, on by default.

Turn it off and every weapon deals 1d6, and so does every piece of gear swung as one,
which is the SRD's baseline combat system. The exception is a character wearing a
girdle of giant strength, whose weapon attacks deal 2d8. With the flag on, the girdle
doubles weapon damage instead. Either way, an unarmed attack deals 1d2, and monsters
deal the damage printed in their descriptions.

individual_initiative.title: Individual Initiative
individual_initiative.description:
Roll initiative for each combatant instead of once per side. An optional rule, off by default.

Turn it on and every participant rolls a separate 1d6. A character adds its DEX
modifier, and a halfling also adds its class initiative bonus. The tabletop game
leaves a monster's initiative modifier to the referee, so you pass one to
`participant_modifier`, and it's 0 if you
don't.

thac0_arithmetic.title: Thac0 Arithmetic
thac0_arithmetic.description:
Work out the attack target number by subtraction instead of reading the attack matrix.

An optional rule, off by default. Turn it on and the number to roll is `THAC0 − AC`
with no clamping. The SRD's ascending-armour-class procedure is the same arithmetic,
so this one flag covers both. Every number in the matrix is within 2 to 20, and the
subtraction has no such limit, so the two differ only when `THAC0 − AC` falls outside that
range.

weapon_reload.title: Weapon Reload
weapon_reload.description:
Stop a weapon with the reload quality, mainly the crossbow, from firing two rounds running.

An optional rule, off by default. Turn it on and the attack validator refuses the shot
when the combat context you pass shows the weapon fired last round. In a session, the
battle code records what fired each round. Without a session, you set that in the
context yourself.

hd5_counts_as_magical.title: Hd5 Counts As Magical
hd5_counts_as_magical.description:
Let big monsters hurt creatures that only silver or magic weapons can harm. An optional rule, off by default.

The SRD prints this among its invulnerability rules. Turn it on, and a monster with 5 or
more Hit Dice gets past such a defense. So does a monster that has the same kind of
defense itself. A monster that energy drain has taken Hit Dice from counts only the Hit
Dice it has left. osrlib applies the rule only where the defense is limited to silver
and magic, as the rule is worded. It reads "another invulnerable monster" as a monster
with such a defense.

magic_item_death_save.title: Magic Item Death Save
magic_item_death_save.description:
Give a dead character's magic items a saving throw against the effect that killed their owner.

An optional rule the SRD leaves to the referee, on by default. It applies when a
destructive source, like a breath weapon or *disintegrate*, kills a character and
destroys their equipment. osrlib rolls a save for each magic item in the dead
character's inventory, using the owner's save values against the source's category
and adding the item's best combat bonus. An item that saves isn't destroyed. Turn the
flag off and every item is destroyed.

xp_award_timing.description:
When the party receives earned experience. On return by default, which is the tabletop rule.

See `XpAwardTiming`. The immediate setting is an
adaptation, and it suits a game whose party never goes home.

deprivation_penalties.title: Deprivation Penalties
deprivation_penalties.description:
Attach mechanical penalties to going without food or water. An adaptation, off by default.

The tabletop rules leave starvation penalties to the referee. osrlib tracks the party's
food and water either way, so this flag changes only what happens once they run out.
Turn it on and osrlib applies this schedule, which it bases on the SRD's examples:

- After one full day without food or water, −1 to attack rolls, and the character needs
  rest twice as often, so fatigue sets in after three turns without rest instead of six.
- After two days, movement rate also halves.
- From the third day on, the character also loses 1d4 hit points each day.

Hunger and thirst don't add together: the longer of the two counts.
[The adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/) has the
reasoning.

aoe_friendly_fire.title: Aoe Friendly Fire
aoe_friendly_fire.description:
Let an area effect cast at a monster group in melee catch the party members fighting it.

An adaptation, on by default. Turn it off and an area effect aimed at a monster group
never counts party members among its targets, so a fireball is safe to cast at
monsters the party is fighting in melee.

formation_width_limit.title: Formation Width Limit
formation_width_limit.description:
Cap how many combatants can fight side by side, by how wide the passage is.

An adaptation, on by default. The cap is the party's frontage, the width of the space
it fights across, divided by the five feet one combatant needs. Each dungeon cell is
ten feet wide, so two may fight side by side in a one-cell corridor and four in a room
two cells across. The SRD notes that two or three characters can fight side by side
in a ten-foot passage, and osrlib uses the lower number. Turn the flag off and there's
no cap, so every combatant may melee.

failed_trap_removal_springs.title: Failed Trap Removal Springs
failed_trap_removal_springs.description:
Spring a treasure trap on the thief who fails to remove it. An adaptation, on by default.

The SRD says a thief may try only once to remove a treasure trap, and it doesn't say what
a failure does. Turn the flag off and a failed
`RemoveTreasureTrap` leaves the trap armed.
The party still knows where it is. That thief can't try again, another thief in the
party can, and the trap still gets its 2-in-6 chance to spring when someone takes the
treasure.

back_stab_needs_both_skills.title: Back Stab Needs Both Skills
back_stab_needs_both_skills.description:
Require both of a hiding thief's skill rolls for a back-stab. An adaptation, on by default.

A thief can hide during a battle with a `hide` declaration and then back-stab from hiding, as
`BattleDeclaration.back_stab` describes.
The session rolls the thief's hide in shadows skill when the hide resolves, and move silently
when the back-stab comes up. With the flag on, the attack is a back-stab only when both rolls
passed. Turn it off and either roll passing is enough. The session makes both rolls under
either setting, so the flag changes no draw. The monsters' choice of targets reads the hide in
shadows roll alone under either setting.

The SRD says hide in shadows "Requires the thief to be motionless—attacking or moving while
hiding is not possible", and that with move silently "A thief may attempt to sneak past
enemies unnoticed". Neither setting is the rules as written.
[The adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/) has the
reasoning.

Ruleset.title: Ruleset
Ruleset.description:
The rules for a game: one flag per decision osrlib lets you make.

Build one at the start of a game and pass it to
`GameSession.new`, or to each kernel function
that takes a `ruleset` argument. `Ruleset()` gives you the SRD rules as written, so pass
only the flags you want to change. The model is frozen, so you can't change a ruleset
mid-game. Saves and replays contain it, so a resumed game uses the rules it started with. An
unknown field name raises a pydantic `ValidationError`, so a misspelled flag fails
instead of doing nothing.

Each flag is one of three kinds. An optional rule is an alternative the SRD prints
beside its standard procedure, and osrlib's default is the book's. An adaptation is a
default osrlib supplies where the tabletop game leaves the decision to a human
referee. A house rule is a change the SRD doesn't print, and its default is the SRD's
procedure. [The adaptations register](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/adaptations/)
gives the reasoning behind each one.

SaveCategory.title: SaveCategory
SaveCategory.description:
The B/X saving throw categories.

Pass one to `saving_throw`. The category depends
on what forces the save: each spell lists its category, and a breath weapon uses `breath`.
When a destructive source kills a creature, its magic items save in the category that
matches the source.

Each value is the lowercase name of a field of
`SavingThrows`, which has a creature's target
number for that category. The values appear in events and saved games, and stay fixed
within a `schema_version`, the version stamp of the saved format.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Save identifier (`sav_` followed by 22 characters). Pass to `POST /v1/saves/{save_id}/restore`
or `GET /v1/saves/{save_id}`.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description:
Source session `id` that produced the save (even if you later deleted that session), or
`null` when imported via `POST /v1/saves/import`.

adventure_id.title: Adventure Id
adventure_id.description:
Source session's `adventure_id` when you saved the session (even if later deleted), or `null`
for an imported save or a save made from a session restored from an imported save.

adventure_name.title: Adventure Name
adventure_name.description: Title of the adventure embedded in the save.

label.title: Label
label.description: Optional human-readable label (1 to 200 characters), or `null` when unlabeled.

mode.description: Session mode when you saved the session.

clock.description: Elapsed in-game time when you saved the session.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when the server stored the save, in RFC 3339 format such as
`"2026-11-20T22:01:05Z"`.

SaveInfo.title: SaveInfo
SaveInfo.description: Metadata for a saved game snapshot, without its referee-only save document.

category.description: Which saving throw the target rolls, as a `SaveCategory`.

modifier.title: Modifier
modifier.description:
The adjustment added to the target's roll. A negative value makes the save harder.

*Hold person*'s single-target mode is −2, and *feeblemind* is −4.

on_save.title: On Save
on_save.description:
What passing the save does.

`negates` means the spell does nothing to that target. `half` means the target still takes half
the damage, rounded down.

SaveSpec.title: SaveSpec
SaveSpec.description:
The saving throw one castable usage of a spell allows its targets, and what passing it does.

Read one from `SpellMode.save`, which is `null` when the
mode allows no save. Casting rolls each target's save for you on the magic stream, with
`saving_throw`. Read this model to show a player what a
target faces before they cast, or to explain why a target came through unharmed.

A spell's save counts as a save against magic, so a character's WIS adjustment applies. A
monster with an automatic save against the element of a damage spell, like a red dragon against
*fire ball*, passes without a roll.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: saving throws are rolled in the open, monsters included.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The entity id of the creature that saved.

category.title: Category
category.description:
Which saving throw it was, as a `SaveCategory` value: `death`, `wands`,
`paralysis`, `breath`, or `spells`.

roll.title: Roll
roll.description: The d20 as it landed, before modifiers. `null` on an automatic save.

modifier.title: Modifier
modifier.description: The sum of everything added to the roll, like a spell, a ring, and your adjustment.

required.title: Required
required.description: The number the roll plus the modifier had to reach. `null` on an automatic save.

SavingThrowRolledEvent.title: SavingThrowRolledEvent
SavingThrowRolledEvent.description:
A saving throw and how it went.

`saving_throw` reports one of these whenever a creature gets a chance to
avoid something. What passing or failing means depends on what forced the save, so read this event with the
events after it.

A monster whose defenses give it an automatic save against a magical effect's element, as a red dragon has
against magical fire, rolls nothing. Then `roll` and `required` are `null`.

death.title: Death
death.description: The target against death rays and poison.

paralysis.title: Paralysis
paralysis.description: The target against paralysis and being turned to stone.

breath.title: Breath
breath.description: The target against a breath attack, like a dragon's.

spells.title: Spells
spells.description: The target against spells, rods, and staves.

SavingThrows.title: SavingThrows
SavingThrows.description:
The five saving throw targets, one for each kind of danger.

A save succeeds on a 1d20 roll equal to or higher than the target for the danger, so a lower
target is better. Read a character's current targets from
`Character.saves` and a monster's from
`MonsterInstance.saves`.
`saving_throw` rolls a save against them for you. Frozen.

id.title: Id
id.description: The curse id, for example `"energy_drain"`.

name.title: Name
name.description: The display name.

prose.title: Prose
prose.description: The curse as its page prints it. Show this to the referee or the player.

wired.title: Wired
wired.description:
True when the engine resolves the curse itself. In the compiled catalog these are energy drain, which takes a
level, and slow healing, under which natural healing needs two days of rest instead of one and healing magic
restores half, rounded down.
False means the curse is only prose, and you decide what happens.

ScrollCurse.title: ScrollCurse
ScrollCurse.description:
One of the cursed scroll's example curses.

The SRD lists example curses a cursed scroll can have and leaves the choice to the
referee. osrlib compiles them into the
`curses` field of the cursed scroll's template.
In a session, when a character reads the cursed scroll, the engine picks one of them at
random. The engine resolves the curses marked `wired`. The rest are prose for you to adjudicate.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"search"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description:
The member who searches, by `MemberView.id`. The
chance depends on the member's class, so match the searcher to `kind`. An elf finds secret
doors on 2 in 6. A dwarf finds room traps and construction tricks on 2 in 6. Every other
class has 1 in 6 for secret doors and room traps, and no chance at construction tricks.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
Which kind of hidden feature to look for. `secret_doors` checks the four sides of the
party's cell. `room_traps` checks the cell's area and the areas behind its known doors,
so a trap that springs when a door opens can be found from the corridor first.
`construction` checks the cell for authored construction tricks, like a sliding wall or a
false floor. Each member gets one attempt for each kind on each cell, so a party covers a
cell by sending different members, or by sending one member once for each kind.

Search.title: Search
Search.description:
Search the party's cell for one kind of hidden feature (one turn).

The party must be exploring a dungeon (see
`EnterDungeon`). The searcher needs light, or
infravision. Each member gets one attempt for each kind on each cell, for the rest of
the game. A trap the party has found never springs.

A `room_traps` search also covers the cell's known doors. A room trap that triggers on
`open`, in the area beyond a known door, can be found from this side of the door.

An undiscovered secret door hides any trap behind it from the cells on both sides. So
when a member discovers a secret door, every member gets their `room_traps` attempt back
on both cells the door joins, and can search again for the trap behind it. The referee's
`SetDoorState` with `discovered=True` gives the
attempts back the same way. Attempts of other kinds, and attempts on every other cell,
stay used.

Modes:

`exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the session is not exploring a dungeon.
- `session.command.unknown_member` - `character_id` matches no party member.
- `session.command.member_incapacitated` - the member cannot act.
- `exploration.action.requires_light` - the party is in the dark and the
  searcher lacks infravision.
- `exploration.search.already_tried` - this member already searched this
  cell for this kind.

**Events:**

`DetectionRolledEvent` with the
roll, a `TrapEvent` for each room trap
found, with the searcher's id in its `character_id`, then
`SearchCompletedEvent` listing
what turned up. For a trap found through a door, the events record that door
twice: in the trap event's `direction`, and as a third part of the token in
`found`, `"room_trap:<area id>:<direction>"`. For a trap found inside the
party's area, they record no door. One turn passes, with the turn's usual events.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: what the search turned up is the party's to act on.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `search_completed`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

character_id.title: Character Id
character_id.description: The member who searched.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description:
What was searched for: `"secret_doors"`, `"room_traps"`, `"construction"`, or
`"treasure_traps"` for a treasure feature inspected by a thief.

found.title: Found
found.description:
What turned up, as references like `"secret_door:north"`, `"room_trap:<area id>"`, or
`"construction:<feature id>"`, and empty when nothing did. A room trap found through a door
from the searched cell has the door's direction in a third segment,
`"room_trap:<area id>:<direction>"`, and one found inside the searched area has none. A found
secret door becomes an ordinary door the party can see and use, and a found room trap no longer
springs on the party.

feature_ids.title: Feature Ids
feature_ids.description:
The `feature:` handles of the construction tricks the search found, in the order of their
`"construction:<feature id>"` entries in `found`, and empty when it found none. Each is the
`MapFeatureView.id` under which the player view lists the
trick from the view built after this command, so you can tell which listed feature the search
revealed without reading the authored id in `found`.

SearchCompletedEvent.title: SearchCompletedEvent
SearchCompletedEvent.description:
A search of the party's cell finished, with whatever it turned up.

Emitted by `Search`, after the referee-visibility
`DetectionRolledEvent` that reports the
die. `InspectTreasure` emits it with
`exploration.search.nothing` when the thief finds no trap. When the thief finds a trap,
the session emits a `TrapEvent` instead.

An empty result means the searcher found nothing, which doesn't mean nothing is
there. Each character gets one attempt per cell per kind of search, so another
character may still find it.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"sell_treasure"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

item_ids.title: Item Ids
item_ids.description:
The gems and jewellery to sell, by the per-instance ids they have in
`MemberView.inventory`. The value of each one goes
to the member who carries it, so one command can pay several purses. Name each valuable
once. Magic items have no fixed price, and the session refuses them with
`town.sell.no_fixed_value`.

SellTreasure.title: SellTreasure
SellTreasure.description:
Sell gems and jewellery in town at their full value (takes no game time).

The party must be in town. Each entry is a valuable's instance id, and the
gold goes into the purse of the member who carries it. A valuable sells for its full
`value_gp`, so its sale price equals its XP value (1 gp for 1 XP). The OSE SRD prices
treasure but gives no rate at which a town buys it, so osrlib uses full value. The SRD
gives magic items no fixed sale value, so the session refuses to sell them.

Modes:

`town`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the party is not in town.
- `town.sell.no_fixed_value` - an entry is a magic item, which has no fixed
  price.
- `exploration.item.not_carried` - no member carries a valuable with that
  instance id, or `item_ids` lists the same instance id twice.

**Events:**

One `TreasureSoldEvent` for each member
whose valuables sold, with the value in gold pieces added to their purse.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description:
Current session revision. Pass as `expected_revision` on
`POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/commands` to guard against concurrent moves.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description:
Commands legal in `mode` for your API key's role, in osrlib's catalog order (`player` keys
receive only `play` commands). Execution can still return `accepted: false` when an in-world
condition blocks the move.

SessionCommands.title: SessionCommands
SessionCommands.description: Mode, revision, and legal commands for a session.

id.title: Id
id.description: Session identifier (`ses_` followed by 22 characters).

name.title: Name
name.description:
Display name of the session. Defaults to `adventure_name` and can be updated via
`PATCH /v1/sessions/{session_id}`.

adventure_id.title: Adventure Id
adventure_id.description:
Adventure identifier that started the session, or `null` when restored from an imported save.
Play continues unaffected if `adventure_id` is `null` or you deleted the original adventure,
because each session embeds a copy of the adventure.

adventure_name.title: Adventure Name
adventure_name.description: Title of the session's embedded adventure.

mode.description:
Current session mode (`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, or `victory`)
after the last accepted command.

ended.title: Ended
ended.description: Whether the session has reached a terminal mode (`game_over` or `victory`).

revision.title: Revision
revision.description:
Count of accepted command requests in this session. Starts at 0 on `POST /v1/sessions` and on
`POST /v1/saves/{save_id}/restore`.

clock.description: Elapsed in-game time after the last accepted command.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: osrlib save document schema version of the stored session.

engine_version.title: Engine Version
engine_version.description: osrlib version string that last wrote the session.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when the server created the session, in RFC 3339 format such as
`"2026-11-20T22:01:05Z"`.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description:
UTC timestamp of the last accepted command (RFC 3339 format), or `created_at` when `revision`
is 0. Renaming the session leaves `updated_at` unchanged.

SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo
SessionInfo.description: Metadata for a game session, returned by session list, create, get, rename, and restore operations.

SessionMode.title: SessionMode
SessionMode.description:
Where the party is in play, which determines the commands the session accepts.

Read the current mode from
`GameSession.mode`, and compare it with a
command class's `allowed_modes` to find out whether the session accepts that command now.
The session refuses a command sent in a mode outside its `allowed_modes` with
`session.command.wrong_mode`.

The values are lowercase strings, and saves contain them, so a value never changes
within one `schema_version`. `town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, and `battle` are the modes of
a game in progress.

A play command is an action the players choose, like
`MoveParty`. A referee command is an action game logic
takes, like `GrantItem`, and its summary starts with
"Referee:".

`game_over` and `victory` are the terminal modes, which mean the session has ended.
The session refuses every play command in both. It accepts most referee commands in both,
with these exceptions:

- `PlaceParty` is illegal in `victory`.
- `SpawnMonsters`,
  `SpawnNpcParty`, and
  `AddMember` are illegal in both, because they would
  restart play.
- `EndEncounter` is illegal in both, because it
  needs an open encounter.
- `RemoveMember` is illegal in both, because the
  party changes only between encounters in a game that is still going.

No play command leaves a terminal mode. A referee's `PlaceParty` is the only way out of
`game_over`, and no command leaves `victory`.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"set_door_state"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

dungeon_id.title: Dungeon Id
dungeon_id.description:
Which dungeon the door is in, by
`DungeonSpec.id`. It doesn't have to be the dungeon the
party is in.

level_number.title: Level Number
level_number.description: Which level of that dungeon, counting from 1.

x.title: X
x.description: The cell's x coordinate on that level's grid.

y.title: Y
y.description: The cell's y coordinate on that level's grid.

direction.description:
Which of the cell's four sides the door is on. Two cells share each edge, so naming a
cell's north side and naming its northern neighbour's south side set the same door. The
session refuses an edge with no door with `session.command.no_door`.

open.title: Open
open.description:
Whether the door stands open. `null`, the default, leaves it as it is. A change emits a
`DoorEvent` at referee visibility, and setting the value
the door already has emits nothing.

wedged.title: Wedged
wedged.description:
Whether a spike holds the door. `null` leaves it as it is. A wedged door doesn't swing
shut behind the party, and `CloseDoor` can't close it.

discovered.title: Discovered
discovered.description:
Whether the party has found the door. `null` leaves it as it is. Setting it to `true`
makes a secret door visible without a search, and `false` hides it again. Revealing a
secret door gives every member their `room_traps` search back on both cells the door
joins, as finding it with `Search` does.

unlocked.title: Unlocked
unlocked.description:
Whether the lock has been undone. `null` leaves it as it is. Setting it to `true` lets
`OpenDoor` open a locked door without a thief picking the
lock.

SetDoorState.title: SetDoorState
SetDoorState.description:
Referee: change the state of a door on any level of any dungeon.

Use it when your game logic opens, closes, reveals, or unlocks a door, like a
lever that opens a portcullis. The door in the adventure document never changes. What
changes is its state in play: whether it stands open, is wedged, has been found, and has
been unlocked. A field you leave `null` leaves the current value unchanged. The door doesn't have
to be next to the party. This command is legal in every mode, `game_over` and
`victory` included.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.unknown_location` - `dungeon_id` matches no dungeon, or
  `level_number` matches no level in it.
- `session.command.no_door` - the edge on that side of that cell isn't a door,
  or the cell is off the level's grid.

**Events:**

A `DoorEvent` at referee visibility when the
door opens or closes, and otherwise none.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"set_flag"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

key.title: Key
key.description:
The flag's name: any non-empty string you choose. Keep a name the same between releases
of your game, because saves contain the flags and adventure documents refer to them by name.

value.title: Value
value.description:
What the flag is set to: a string, an integer, or a boolean. Setting a flag that's
already set replaces its value. To compare this value in an adventure document, use a
`FlagEqualsCondition`. So a door that opens
once a lever has been pulled is a flag set here, and a gate on the door that tests it.

SetFlag.title: SetFlag
SetFlag.description:
Referee: set a session flag, like one that records a lever pulled to open a portcullis.

A flag is a named value you store in the session. This command is legal in
every mode, `game_over` and `victory` included. Flags are saved with the session. Your code and
listeners read them from the referee view. To test one in an adventure document, use a
`FlagEqualsCondition`, like the condition on
a door that opens once the lever has been pulled.

Modes:

`town`, `exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`, `game_over`, `victory`

**Rejections:**

None.

**Events:**

`FlagSetEvent` with the key and value.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"spawn_monsters"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description:
Which monster to spawn, from the session's
`effective_monsters` catalog: either
a built-in id from `load_monsters` (see the
[monster id index](https://mmacy.github.io/osrlib-python/reference/content-ids/monsters/))
or one the adventure bundles.

count_dice.title: Count Dice
count_dice.description:
How many to spawn, as a dice expression like `"2d6"`, rolled on the session's
`ENCOUNTER_STREAM`. Use it when the number should
depend on the seed, and use `count_fixed` when it shouldn't. Set exactly one of the two. A
malformed expression fails validation when the command is constructed, so the session never
sees it, and so does an expression that can roll more than 100, like `"1d100+1"` or
`"11d10"`. A roll below 1 counts as 1. For more than 100 monsters, send the command again
while the encounter is open, and the new group joins it. The session refuses that second
command during a pursuit.

count_fixed.title: Count Fixed
count_fixed.description:
How many to spawn, as an exact number from 1 to 100. Use it when the author chose the
number. Set exactly one of this and `count_dice`. For more than 100 monsters, send the
command again while the encounter is open, and the new group joins it. The session refuses
that second command during a pursuit.

distance_feet.title: Distance Feet
distance_feet.description:
How far away the monsters appear, in feet. A new encounter opens at this distance, and
a group that joins an open encounter starts at it. The distance determines whether
missiles reach, how long closing in takes, and whether the party can outrun the monsters.
B/X uses 2d6 times 10 feet for a wandering encounter, so a number in that range is
typical. `0` puts them right next to the party.

SpawnMonsters.title: SpawnMonsters
SpawnMonsters.description:
Referee: create monsters at a distance from the party, in a new encounter or the open one.

Use it for an encounter you decide on, like monsters an LLM referee brings in or
a scripted ambush. Use it also for monsters that arrive during a fight, like the
animals a lycanthrope summons. The party must be standing in a dungeon, because
encounters take place on the dungeon grid, so the command isn't legal in `town`. It isn't
legal once the session has ended either, because it would start new play. Set exactly one of
`count_dice` and `count_fixed`, or constructing the command fails validation.

When no encounter is open, the command opens one with the monsters. When an encounter
or a battle is open, the monsters join it as one new group at `distance_feet`:

- The group rolls no surprise and no reaction. It shares the encounter's surprise and its
  stance, which is the monsters' reaction to the party. So when the party surprised the
  monsters already there, and they can't act for a round, the new group can't act either.
- The command takes no time and runs no round. The group first acts in the next round,
  when the monster side acts.
- The session refuses the command during a pursuit, because a pursuit runs at the pace of
  its slowest group, and a new group could change that pace.

Modes:

`exploring`, `encounter`, `battle`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the party is in town, or the session has ended.
- `session.command.unknown_monster` - `template_id` matches no monster.
- `encounter.spawn.mid_pursuit` - the monsters are pursuing the party, and no
  new group can join during a pursuit.

**Events:**

`MonstersSpawnedEvent` comes first.

When the command opens an encounter, the encounter's opening follows: an
`EffectAttachedEvent` for each monster that
regenerates, like a troll,
`SurpriseRolledEvent`s,
`EncounterStartedEvent`, the
reaction roll, and a
`StanceChangedEvent`. When the monsters'
reaction is to attack, battle opens at once. A group whose morale score is 2 then flees
and gets away as the battle opens, with a
`MonsterFledEvent` followed right away by a
`MonsterEscapedEvent`.

When the monsters join an open encounter, an `EffectAttachedEvent` for each monster
that regenerates follows instead, then an
`EncounterGroupJoinedEvent`, which
the players see. When the group joins a battle and its morale score is 2, it gets away
at once, because a monster with that score won't fight. A `MonsterFledEvent` and then
a `MonsterEscapedEvent` come last.

command_type.title: Command Type
command_type.description: Always `"spawn_npc_party"`. Pass it in every request body to select this command.

source.title: Source
source.description: Referee only. Who or what issued the command, such as a trigger id, a quest id, or the name of a subsystem in your application (at least 1 character), or `null` when unset. The session records `source` in `command_log` without changing how the command executes. A player who sets `source` gets 403 `referee_required`.

party_kind.title: Party Kind
party_kind.description:
Which table to build the party from: `basic` for low-level adventurers, or `expert` for
higher-level ones. Either kind of party's group in the encounter has the label `"adventurer"`
and the plural `"adventurers"`.

count_dice.title: Count Dice
count_dice.description:
How many adventurers, as a dice expression rolled on the session's
`ENCOUNTER_STREAM`. A malformed expression fails
validation when the command is constructed, and so does an expression that can roll more
than 100, like `"1d100+1"`. A roll below 1 counts as 1. Don't set it together with
`count_fixed`.

When both this and `count_fixed` are `null`, the default, the engine rolls the B/X number
for `party_kind`: 1d4+4 for `basic` and 1d6+3 for `expert`.

count_fixed.title: Count Fixed
count_fixed.description:
How many adventurers, as an exact number from 1 to 100. Use it when the adventure's
author chose the size of the band. The session rolls nothing for the size. Don't set it
together with `count_dice`. A band has at most 100 adventurers, whether you set this or
`count_dice`. The command can't add adventurers to an open encounter, so a larger band
isn't possible.

distance_feet.title: Distance Feet
distance_feet.description:
How far away the NPC party appears, in feet, on the same terms as
`SpawnMonsters.distance_feet`.

SpawnNpcParty.title: SpawnNpcParty
SpawnNpcParty.description:
Referee: generate a party of NPC adventurers and open an encounter with them.

An NPC adventurer is a character the engine generates, with a class, a level, and gear,
rather than a monster from the catalog. The party must be standing in a dungeon with no
encounter already open, so the command is legal only in `exploring`. Unlike
`SpawnMonsters`, it can't add a group to an open
encounter.

Set `count_fixed` for a band of an exact size, `count_dice` to roll the size, or neither
to roll the B/X number for `party_kind`. Setting both fails validation.

Modes:

`exploring`

**Rejections:**

- `session.command.wrong_mode` - the party is in town, an encounter or a battle is
  open, or the session has ended.

**Events:**

`NpcPartySpawnedEvent`, which lists the
NPC party at referee visibility, then the encounter's opening, as for
`SpawnMonsters`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the book belongs to the player.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

caster_id.title: Caster Id
caster_id.description: The entity id of the caster whose book gained the spell.

SpellBookUpdatedEvent.title: SpellBookUpdatedEvent
SpellBookUpdatedEvent.description:
A new spell has gone into an arcane caster's spell book.

`add_spell_to_book` reports this. A caster may prepare only the
spells in its book. Adding a spell to the book doesn't prepare it. Preparing is a separate step, which
`memorize_spells` reports with a `SpellsMemorizedEvent`.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, like `combat.attack.hit`: two or more lowercase parts separated by dots. The first part is
the area of the rules the event comes from, like `combat` or `magic`.

Branch on it, and pass the event to `format_message` to turn it into English.
Building an event with a code in any other format raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: everyone hears a spell cast aloud.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

caster_id.title: Caster Id
caster_id.description: The entity id of the caster.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description:
The key of the spell mode that was cast. For a spell with more than one mode, like one that can harm or
heal, it's the mode the caster chose.

mode_display_name.title: Mode Display Name
mode_display_name.description:
The cast mode's `SpellMode.display_name`, such as
`"Blind a creature"` for the `blind` mode of *light*, for a line that states which usage the caster chose. It's read
from the form that was cast, so a reversed cast has the reverse's label. An event loaded from a save written
before the field existed has an empty string, and `format_message` names the
mode by `mode`.

reversed.title: Reversed
reversed.description: True when the spell was cast in its reversed form.

target_ids.title: Target Ids
target_ids.description: The entity ids or locations the caster aimed the spell at. Empty for a spell with no target.

manual.title: Manual
manual.description:
True when osrlib didn't resolve the spell's effect, because the rules leave that mode to the referee. The
copy is used up, and you play out the outcome from the spell's text.

SpellCastEvent.title: SpellCastEvent
SpellCastEvent.description:
A spell was cast, from memory or from a scroll.

`cast_spell` reports this when a caster casts a memorized spell, which uses
up the memorized copy, and `cast_from_scroll` reports it when a caster
reads a spell from a scroll. What the spell did comes in the events after this one: saving throws, damage,
conditions, effects, healing, and deaths.

When a cast affects no one, the event has the code `magic.cast.no_effect`, and the spell is still used up. Refusing
the cast instead would show the player, at no cost, which targets the spell could affect, and the B/X rules don't
reveal that.

visibility.description: Player visibility: a declaration is made out loud.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The event type, `spell_declared`, which identifies this class in serialized form.

caster_id.title: Caster Id
caster_id.description: Who is casting: a party member's id, or an NPC adventurer's.

spell_id.title: Spell Id
spell_id.description: Which spell was declared, as its catalog id.

reversed.title: Reversed
reversed.description: Whether the reversed form was declared, for a spell that has one.

SpellDeclaredEvent.title: SpellDeclaredEvent
SpellDeclaredEvent.description:
Somebody declared a spell, before anyone knows who acts first.

Emitted by `ResolveBattleRound` for
each caster who declared one, party member or NPC alike, at the start of the round.

In B/X, spells are declared before initiative is rolled. A caster who takes damage
before their turn loses the spell, and the other side knows what is coming. A lost
spell arrives later in the round as a
`SpellDisruptedEvent`.

code.title: Code
code.description: Which of the two failures this is, defaulting to `magic.cast.disrupted`.

visibility.description: Player visibility: the caster's spell visibly fails.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: The fixed string that identifies this event class in a serialized event.

caster_id.title: Caster Id
caster_id.description: The entity id of the caster.

reversed.title: Reversed
reversed.description: True when the lost copy was the spell's reversed form.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description:
Why a `magic.cast.fizzled` spell failed: the code of the first check that failed when the session checked
the spell again during the battle round.

Any check a spell passes at the start of the round can fail, so read the code and don't assume a cause. An
ally's silence on the party's cell gives `magic.cast.silenced_area`, and a scroll read in the dark gives
`exploration.action.requires_light`. Match on it as you match on the code of a
`Rejection`. The rejection code reference explains
each code. `null` on a `magic.cast.disrupted` event, whose cause is the hit, and on an event from a log
written before the field existed.

SpellDisruptedEvent.title: SpellDisruptedEvent
SpellDisruptedEvent.description:
A spell the caster declared came to nothing, and the caster lost it anyway.

It's reported in two cases, and you tell them apart by `code`:

- `magic.cast.disrupted`: `disrupt_casting` reports it when a caster
  who declared a spell is hit, or stopped some other way, before the spell goes off.
- `magic.cast.fizzled`: a session reports it during a battle round. In the round's magic phase, the session
  checks each declared spell again, just before the spell would go off. If a check the spell passed at the start of
  the round now fails, because something earlier in the round changed, the spell fizzles. Two examples are an ally's
  *silence 15' radius* centered on the party's cell, and the party's last torch going out when its bearer
